- **CREATEROLE is REQUIRED to be removed after the first start has completed** (the rab-api log shows the migrate
  result with serve=true, or a restart reports state CURRENT; `/healthz` 200 alone is a loose signal). This is runbook
  4a step 6, owner decision 2026-11-17; Twenty's app user never has CREATEROLE. `crewflow_owner` needs CREATEROLE only on the first start: the bootstrap creates the schema
  roles, and the role migrations up to 1786691000000 run. Until the admin runs `ALTER ROLE crewflow_owner NOCREATEROLE`,
  a leaked URL is the schema owner with CREATEROLE (behaviour catalogue).
  - No runtime path and no migration after 1786691000000 creates, alters or grants a role; the code was searched.
  - The upgrade runner refuses a workspace step that writes the role catalogs.
  - The API provisions workspaces through `core.provision_workspace` (SECURITY DEFINER, owned by `crewflow`). The
    Worker provisions with `SET ROLE crewflow`.
  - Proven on PG16 with NOCREATEROLE (2026-11-17, runbook 4a "Status"):
    - a restart: db-setup, migrate, and the API / Worker boot gates;
    - an upgrade that applied the 8 migrations after R256, the C3 cutover functions among them;
    - the app's own provisioning and upgrade-runner integration specs: 112 passed, 0 failed. They cover the API
      server path (`core.provision_workspace`), the Worker's `SET ROLE crewflow` path, the 0.6.0 workspace commands
      and the locked start.
  - Residual (flagged assumption): a future release with role migrations needs CREATEROLE back for that one upgrade.
    The migration child refuses with exit 67 until it is granted.
  - After NOCREATEROLE, `crewflow_owner` still holds the ADMIN option on the schema roles it created. It can still GRANT
    them to existing roles. The posture check detects such a member at the next boot; it does not prevent the grant.
- **Fail closed.** Every check runs inside the transaction, before anything is created:
  - PostgreSQL 16 or later;
  - an admin that can create roles and grant on the database;
  - no existing Crewflow role on the cluster;
  - no database-wide `search_path` default;
  - SCRAM password encryption.

  The script then re-checks the exact result before COMMIT. On a provider without CREATEROLE the install is refused,
  either by the script or by the migrate child (exit 67), and nothing is created.
- **Tests.** Disposable PostgreSQL 16.16 InstaBox runs on 2026-11-17 used a scratch harness, not committed (runbook
  section 4a "Status"); the latest run had 36 checks and 0 failures. The script ran as a NOSUPERUSER CREATEROLE admin,
  and after it these all passed:
  - db-setup's owner-URL mode;
  - the full migration chain as `crewflow_owner`;
  - `owner-login-posture.ts` rules 1-4;
  - `runDatabaseBootGates` for the API and the Worker;
  - the PG16 posture golden.

  These refusals were proven:
  - an admin without CREATEROLE;
  - a NOCREATEROLE `crewflow_owner` on a fresh install;
  - a schema role pre-created by the admin;
  - the M1 and L1 regressions above.

  The password itself was never in a `log_statement=all` server log. No CI job runs this script yet.

### Rollback
A rollback across this release needs the previous release's compose files (its image has no `worker-start.sh`,
`db-setup.sh` or bootstrap child: under this release's files db-setup fails and rab-api never starts) and a
`crewflow_owner` URL in `PG_DATABASE_URL`. With a `crewflow_owner` URL in compose.env it is that same URL (db-setup never
changed its password). With an admin URL or the bundled db, the URL is printed by a one-off `docker run` of the current
image that runs the apps' own derive step on the read-only volume (`--pull never --log-driver none --network none --read-only --cap-drop ALL --user
1000:1000`; runbook 3.6; SENSITIVE output; not yet run live), or a new password is set with `01-crewflow-owner.sql`.

- **Tests.** owner-credential / owner-password-file / derive-runtime-url / owner-bootstrap / db-target / runtime-login /
  runtime-db-config / never-in-runtime-env / deployment-identity specs; the Worker's `owner-password-wait` spec; the
  bootstrap harness `bootstrap-owner-login-check.ts` (OWNER-DB-FINAL A6: fresh, restart, lost file, stale file, missing
  database, crewflow_owner URL unchanged, refusals, H1, N1, N2); the prestart shell tests (target and password files, any
  non-empty `PG_DATABASE_URL` refused, APP_SECRET refused by db-setup.sh, the bounded wait, PID 1, one-off); the compose
  gates and their tests (a variable carrying the crewflow_owner password, a mount at the password-file path other than
  db-setup's volume (db-setup read-write, rab-api / rab-worker read-only), APP_SECRET on db-setup, a non-empty or
  interpolated `PG_DATABASE_URL` on rab-api / rab-worker, `PG_DATABASE_ADMIN_URL`); the image gate (any file under
  `/run/crewflow/db-target` in the image fails it); area 6's `deploy-order-tests/run-db-setup-tests.cjs` on postgres 16,
  17 and 18, NOT yet re-run on the Helm model.

## XP-09 Q6 — refresh-token revocation keeps the first revocation time (branch fix/refresh-token-revoke-first-wins, 2026-11-13, PR #132)
- **Threat:** an attacker or user replays an old, rotated refresh token, or several revocations happen (logout, password
  change, reuse detection). Each one rewrote `core.refresh_token.revoked_at` on every row of the family or user, including
  rows already revoked. That erased when a token actually stopped being valid (reuse-investigation evidence) and restarted
  the 181-day retention clock of `core.worker_cleanup_auth_tokens`, so repeated replays could keep dead token rows forever.
- **Control:** `RefreshTokenService.revokeFamily`, `revokeAllForUser` and `revokeAllForUserExcept` ("log out of other
  devices" and the MFA-change path, profile.service.ts / mfa-management.service.ts) stamp only rows
  `WHERE revoked_at IS NULL` — the same rule as `revokeAllForOrganisation` and the `user_session` CAS. Live rows are still revoked; revoked rows keep their
  first time. No row can become un-revoked.
- **Tests:** `refresh-token-revoke-first-wins.integration.spec.ts` (revoke, then revoke again later → revoked_at unchanged,
  for all three methods, incl. revokeAllForUserExcept keeping the excepted family live and backdated times unchanged; replaying a rotated token twice keeps its rotation time; fails 3/3 on the previous code) and unit tests
  in `refresh-token.service.spec.ts`.

## OWNER-DB-ULTIMATE Part B — upgrade logbook `core.upgrade_migration`, like Twenty's upgradeMigration (branch deploy/upgrade-ledger; SQL owner-approved: REVISED, REVISED 2 and the PG18 self-check, 2026-11-13/14)

- **What.** Every start records each upgrade step in `core.upgrade_migration` (migration
  `UpgradeMigrationLedger1786721470000`): `<version>_TypeOrmMigrations`, then one row per upgrade command, `completed`
  or `failed`, attempt N, `executed_by_version`, `forced`, `is_initial` (one-time adoption of an R254 / R256 history as
  0.4.0 / 0.5.0; a new workspace's first row). Behaviour re-implemented from twentyhq/twenty @ eedb0a73 (the
  upgrade-migration service, upgrade command runner, workspace.service.ts:813), not copied.
- **Threats.** (1) A request handler, the legacy runtime role or another tenant reads or forges upgrade history (a fake
  completed step skips a needed upgrade, or a failure is hidden). (2) Rows are rewritten or deleted to hide a failed or
  forced upgrade. (3) An old or unknown database is upgraded across a skipped release. (4) A test-only seam (a fake or
  failing upgrade command) reaches a real deployment. (5) Public `/healthz` tells an unauthenticated caller the version,
  step or error text. (6) An operator rolls an image back across 0.6.0 and the service does not come up.
- **Controls.**
  - **Table + RLS in the same migration.** Owner `rab_secure_owner` (NOLOGIN); `REVOKE ALL` from PUBLIC, crewflow and
    crewflow_app; the owner role holds SELECT, INSERT and DELETE only. ENABLE + FORCE RLS. No UPDATE or TRUNCATE
    privilege for anyone. CHECKs: name pattern, status `completed|failed`, attempt ≥ 1, strict version, a message only on
    failed rows and ≤ 4000 chars, `is_initial` ⇒ attempt 1 and not forced. FK `workspace_id` → `core.manager_workspace`
    ON DELETE CASCADE. Twenty's four indexes (two partial unique).
  - **Scope setting.** Every policy is keyed on the transaction-local `rab.upgrade_scope`, set only by the upgrade code
    (`withUpgradeScope`; the value is a bound parameter):
    - `upgrade`: read and insert, only with no tenant bound and only while THIS backend holds the migration advisory
      lock (pg_locks, classid/objid of `0x637265776d696772`);
    - `status`: read only, no tenant bound;
    - `workspace_init`: insert of an `is_initial` row for a workspace of the bound organisation only;
    - unset (every request handler): 0 rows, insert 42501. A RESTRICTIVE `USING (false) WITH CHECK (false)` policy
      covers crewflow_app.
    `withUpgradeScope` refuses to open a scope in a transaction that already wrote, in a multi-statement transaction, or
    over a non-empty scope (a simple-protocol pre-check), and checks the same backend afterwards. `TenantContextService`
    clears the setting in every tenant transaction.
  - **Owner DELETE, for the cascade only (REVISED 2).** PostgreSQL runs an ON DELETE CASCADE as the referencing table's
    owner and checks that owner's DELETE privilege, so the owner keeps DELETE. There is no DELETE policy: any direct
    DELETE (the owner login included) removes 0 rows under FORCE RLS. Rows leave only with their workspace.
  - **Test seams refused outside tests.** `CREWFLOW_TEST_UPGRADE_COMMANDS` / `CREWFLOW_TEST_UPGRADE_FAIL_COMMAND` exit 64
    unless NODE_ENV=test on a database marked `crewflow.disposable_test_database`, outside production
    (runtime-db-config.ts, migrate-on-start.ts), and `api-prestart.sh` refuses them with the other migration seams.
  - **Version refusal.** Before any write, `decideUpgradeStart` refuses a database that has not completed the previous
    version, has an unknown / unadoptable history, or skips a release: exit 65, nothing applied (supported floor R254 =
    0.4.0, R256 = 0.5.0). `upgrade --force` (a one-off `docker compose run --rm --no-deps rab-api node
    packages/rab-server/dist/command upgrade --force`) skips only that refusal and marks every row it writes
    `forced = true`; no environment variable can set it. A `CREWFLOW_APP_VERSION` that disagrees with package.json, or is
    set without one, exits 64.
  - **Failure semantics.** A failed migration never serves (exit 66, retried on the next start). Only a verified failed
    upgrade COMMAND with every migration applied serves (exit 70). `CREWFLOW_UPGRADE_FAILURE`, `_POLICY` and
    `CREWFLOW_UPGRADE_INCOMPLETE` were removed and are refused (64).
  - **`/healthz` is a boolean (owner decision 2026-11-14).** Public: exactly
    `upgrade: { status: 'up', upgradeFailed: true|false }`. No version, step, state word or error text in any state;
    always `up` (200). The state, step, versions, attempt and forced flag are on the platform-admin health report only,
    and `error_message` is never shown there either.
  - **Rollback is a restore.** Going back from 0.6.0 to an older image (R256, R254) is only possible by restoring the
    pre-0.6.0 backup: the older image's semantic-posture boot gate refuses the logbook objects (finding L7). Runbook 3.3
    and 3.6 and the rab-docs deployment page say so; the backup is mandatory before 0.6.0.
- **Residual risks (accepted).**
  - **R1 (Info, accepted 2026-11-13):** `markNewWorkspaceInitial` takes a structural `{ id, organisationId }`, not proof
    that the workspace was just created. A caller on the creating code path could write an `is_initial` row for another
    existing workspace of the SAME organisation. This is bounded by the import allowlist (`upgrade-imports.spec.ts`), the
    same-organisation policy and the bound-organisation check; no xmin-based proof was added in SQL.
  - `error_message` is stored as-is (length-capped) and may contain what the failing step printed. Only the upgrade and
    status scopes can read it; request handlers and /healthz cannot.
  - The semantic goldens grew (+7 lines on PG16/17/18; the `acl|` section is generalized to `ACL_WATCHED_TABLES`), so any
    older image refuses a 0.6.0 database (rollback is a restore, above).
- **Tests.**
  - `upgrade-migration-ledger.integration.spec.ts` (11 tests): scopes, the lock, cross-org 42501, an owner DELETE that
    removes 0 rows, the cascade, UPDATE / TRUNCATE 42501, the CHECKs, the real node-pg driver for the simple-protocol
    pre-check, and a read-only transaction refused (R2).
  - The upgrade-version / -sequence / -version-check / -runner / -status / upgrade-imports specs.
  - `upgrade-status.spec.ts`: no version, step, state or error text in /healthz in any state; the admin card keeps the
    detail.
  - runtime-db-config and the prestart shell tests: the removed names, the seams, the exit 66/70 veto.
  - The semantic-posture acl spec; the security-posture golden (+4) and the semantic goldens (pg16/17/18).
  - B2's suites (`upgrade-ledger-tests/`, the S-layer specs) on PG16/17/18.

## X2.3 / Part F2 — dev and QA on Part A's database setup; one postgres server per data volume (branch build/dev-qa-helm-setup, 2026-11-13; supersedes the #120 draft)
- **Change:** docker-compose.yml (dev) and docker-compose.qa.yml (QA) run Part A's setup: the bundled `db` (production's text
  word for word, gate-checked), a one-shot `db-setup` (the only service with a database URL, pinned to the bundled db — a
  shell-exported `PG_DATABASE_URL` cannot redirect it), `server` on api-prestart.sh and `worker` on worker-start.sh building the
  crewflow_owner URL from the setup volume mounted read-only; migrate on start; consume-only worker. The old `devdb`/`postgres`
  and `migrate` services are gone. Dev/QA use their own password names (`CREWFLOW_DEV_DB_PASSWORD`, `CREWFLOW_QA_DB_PASSWORD`),
  so a production `PG_DATABASE_PASSWORD` left in a shell never reaches dev.
- **Threat (review M1):** two postgres servers started on one data volume (e.g. `docker compose run db`, `--scale db=2`) corrupt
  it — the 2026-10-15 incident. The old dev stack prevented it only with `container_name: rab-devdb`; production's bundled db
  had no guard. **Control:** every bundled db (docker-compose.production.yml, docker-compose.image.yml, dev, QA) takes a kernel
  `flock -n` on `/var/lib/postgresql/.crewflow-server.lock` before touching the volume and holds it for the server's life; a
  second container refuses (exit 1). The production compose file changed; nothing is deployed until the owner deploys.
- **Risk accepted as in production:** PT-01/BC-08 (one schema-owning login) now also apply to dev and QA (loopback-only,
  throwaway data). Dev server/worker still read packages/rab-server/.env for APP_SECRET etc.; every database key is pinned in
  compose and the start scripts refuse the dangerous ones. Unchanged: FORCE RLS, both RESET ROLEs, current_user = session_user,
  the refusals, the migration lock.
- **Data:** `rab_devdb_data` / `rab-devdb` are no longer referenced and are left untouched (the dev cut-over is the owner's).
  The dev database lives on the EXTERNAL volume `crewflow_dev_db_data` (owner decision 2026-11-14, #136 b), created once by
  hand; `docker compose down -v` keeps it. The CA and setup (password file) volumes stay per project: after `down -v` the
  next `up` makes a new CA and db-setup resets crewflow_owner to a new random password (Part A lost-file path) before the
  apps start; verified live (same cluster and data, old password refused, new one works, no password in any log). QA and
  production keep per-project volumes.
- **Residual:** flock assumes a local volume driver (not an NFS-style network volume).
- **Tests:** compose-credential-isolation.cjs (Part A contract, db/network/volume parity with production, mount rules, the lock,
  no `PG_DATABASE_PASSWORD` in dev/QA) with denial tests; deployment-worker.test.cjs (worker-start.sh, limits);
  compose-owner-login.cjs (lock in image.yml); live: dev bring-up + restart on PG16 (crewflow_owner NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS,
  password file unchanged across restart, no password in any log) and run-db-setup-tests.cjs block `lock` (PG16 PASS: the
  second db exits 1 with the refusal, the first stays healthy).

## OWNER-DB-ULTIMATE Part D — per-workspace upgrade commands and the workspace command runner, like Twenty's (branch deploy/workspace-command-runner; no new SQL)

- **What.** Workspace schema changes ship as WORKSPACE upgrade commands per release (`upgrade-commands/<major-minor>/`,
  registry `WORKSPACE_UPGRADE_COMMANDS`; 0.6 has none). The workspace command runner runs them once per workspace, on the
  locked migration session, after the release's instance commands. Each (command, workspace) is recorded in Part B's
  `core.upgrade_migration` (workspace_id set, `completed` / `failed`, attempt + 1). The workspace-module list is frozen at
  20 (the template); a structural command adds a structure level (21, 22, …). On 0.6.0 every READY workspace at module 20
  with a matching structure is adopted with one `is_initial` row. Behaviour re-implemented from twentyhq/twenty @ eedb0a73
  (workspace-command-runner.service.ts, workspace-iterator.service.ts, upgrade-sequence-reader / -runner,
  run-instance-commands previous-version check), not copied. No DDL, function or grant was added: the runner uses Part B's
  approved table, existing functions (`worker_list_workspaces`, `verify_workspace_schema_v1`, `workspace_schema_fingerprint`)
  and existing registry columns.
- **Threats.**
  1. A workspace's command touches another workspace's schema or data, `core`, or the role catalogs (DDL, DML, GRANT,
     CREATE / ALTER ROLE), or forges logbook rows.
  2. A command leaves the session changed (role, tenant binding, `rab.*`, search_path, advisory locks) for the next workspace.
  3. A workspace is served by code that expects a structure it does not have (a failed structural step, a data-step failure
     before a pending structural step, drift, a refused adoption).
  4. One workspace's failure stops or marks the others.
  5. `--force` hides an earlier failed step.
  6. A test hook reaches production.
  7. A long upgrade is killed by the health check / restart loop and leaves partial state.
- **Controls.**
  - **One REPEATABLE READ transaction per (workspace, command):** `SET LOCAL ROLE crewflow` (refused when the session can
    neither be nor SET crewflow), tenant bound to that workspace, `search_path = pg_catalog, pg_temp`, per-schema advisory
    lock, registry row FOR UPDATE (READY, derived name).
  - **Post-step checks before COMMIT (any failure rolls back):**
    - a static refusal of SQL naming another `workspace_<hex>`;
    - session invariants: same backend and transaction, role, every `rab.*` by name, search_path;
    - a catalog-write gate: a DATA step that writes any catalog is refused `DDL_IN_DATA_STEP`;
    - for structural steps, the catalog xmin scan (no catalog row outside the schema written by this transaction; the
      schema's own TOAST and the internal RI triggers of its own FKs are allowed); for steps declaring `mayDrop`, also the
      outside object counts (an undeclared drop is refused `UNDECLARED_DROP`);
    - write counters compared as a delta within the transaction: no insert / update / delete on any table outside the
      schema, nor on pg_authid, pg_auth_members, pg_db_role_setting, pg_database, pg_largeobject_metadata,
      pg_publication(_rel); plus xmin scans of the readable shared catalogs. `track_counts = on` is required per run;
    - extra structure: no rule, all relations permanent, no inheritance, no foreign type or operator;
    - `verify_workspace_schema_v1` + fingerprint equal to the expected value of the workspace's structure level for this
      PostgreSQL major.
  - **After the transaction:** role none, current_user = session_user, every `rab.*` empty (checked by name: pg_settings does
    not list placeholder settings, proven on PG16/17/18), search_path as at the start, no extra session advisory lock.
    Otherwise the step is refused `SESSION_LEAK` and the session reset; a reset that fails stops the run.
  - **Failure isolation:** a failed workspace gets its own `failed` row and stops only its own later steps. A per-workspace
    fault outside a step (a vanished workspace, a logbook write) is recorded against that workspace; only a run-level fault
    stops the run. Pending steps are every workspace step after the cursor up to the code version, so a step `--force`
    skipped runs first. The previous-version check also needs every workspace to have completed the previous version's last
    workspace step.
  - **Blocked workspaces (owner decisions D2/D3):** a workspace whose step failed with a structure that does not match this
    code is BLOCKED until its step succeeds. That covers a structural step, a mismatched structure, a level below the
    code's, a refused adoption, and no / unknown cursor.
    - Marker: `upgrade-blocked: <step> (<CLASS>)` in the existing registry column `migration_error`.
    - `SchemaResolverService` answers 503 "Workspace is being upgraded." only to a caller whose session is bound to that
      workspace's organisation and who reaches the resolver (workspace membership is enforced earlier by the guards);
      another organisation's caller gets 404 as usual.
    - The Worker's walks skip it and per-job paths defer it (no attempt counted).
    - The admin health page names it: workspace id, step, error class, never a message.
    - The step retries every start.
    - A data-only failure with a matching structure is served (still reported failed).
    - A block that cannot be written stops the start. A cache-epoch bump that fails while a block changed or is in force
      stops the start (`WorkspaceBlockCacheError`, outcome postCheck, exit 68: every migration applied, a post-migration
      gate refused).
  - **Test hooks:** `runMigrateOnStart`'s `testWorkspace` and the provisioner's `workspaceRegistry` are code-only and refused
    outside NODE_ENV=test, before any connection; a guard spec proves no non-spec file passes them.
  - **Long upgrades:** each (workspace, step) commits and is recorded on its own, so a kill loses at most the workspace in
    flight and the next start resumes. Measured at 1,000 workspaces: data step ≈0.4–0.6 s, structural ADD COLUMN
    ≈0.9–1.3 s per workspace.
- **Accepted limits (owner-accepted 2026-11-14).**
  - **D-T1:** the checks are a detector, not a privilege boundary. The command runs as `crewflow` (which owns every
    workspace schema) on the session that set the binding and role, so it can re-bind, RESET ROLE (`crewflow_owner` holds
    CREATEROLE) or set `rab.upgrade_scope`. The checks detect and roll back what that changes; they cannot stop a command
    that COMMITs mid-way (it is then refused). Not detected: `NOTIFY` (delivered at COMMIT), `nextval` on a sequence outside
    the schema, large-object payload writes in a STRUCTURAL step (in a data step a large-object write is a catalog write
    and is refused, DDL_IN_DATA_STEP). Commands are reviewed code, never input-driven.
  - **Redis needed at start while a block is in force:** every start that changes a block, or runs while any workspace is
    blocked, must bump the entity-cache epoch; if Redis is down the API start refuses (68), so a lasting block plus a Redis
    outage keeps the API from starting. A Worker already running is not stopped by that refusal; its discovery and claim
    walks re-check the registry and skip a blocked workspace.
  - **D-T2:** steps run under REPEATABLE READ; a concurrent writer can fail a data step with 40001 (recorded failed,
    retried).
  - **HWS off (open owner question):** the block is enforced where workspaces are routed to their schemas
    (`HWS_RUNTIME_ENABLED`). With HWS off, requests use `core` and nothing is blocked; the admin page still names the
    workspace.
  - **Rules for command authors:** data steps may not write any catalog (DDL, GRANT, TRUNCATE, temporary tables, ALTER ROLE);
    structural steps that drop or recreate objects declare `mayDrop`; every command is idempotent.
- **Tests.** Unit: sequence, pending, positions, isolation scan, freeze, source guard, structure level, delta counters,
  track_counts, rab.* list, hook refusal. Integration on PG16/17/18: adoption, per-workspace runs, every abuse case above, the
  D2/D3 blocks, the P1 code-level block, the locked start with a level-21 probe, the P2 refusal. Worker unit tests for the
  pauses.

## QR expiry from the shift's current end (owner decision 0i, 2026-11-14; branch fix/qr-expiry-from-shift)
- **Threat / defect:** the Shift QR's JWT `exp` was signing time + (shift length + 15 + 120 min). The pre-shift report
  signs its QR up to `REPORT_AVAILABLE_BEFORE_MINUTES` (180) before the start, so a printed QR expired ~45 min before the
  shift ended: staff could not clock out with it, and a manager extending a shift could not extend the QR.
- **Control:** `AttendanceQrService.validateQr` decides expiry at scan time from the freshly re-read shift: accepted while
  server `now <=` the staff member's own end (since the follow-ups below) `+ QR_POST_SHIFT_GRACE_MINUTES` (the same grace setting `assertClockWindow` closes with; one
  definition, `AttendanceQrService.validUntil`), refused `INVALID_QR` / `expired` after. New tokens carry no `exp`.
  Fail-closed reasoning: `QrTokenService.verify` still checks signature (HKDF-derived key, HS256 pinned), issuer and
  audience, but is never an accept on its own; its only caller always loads the shift and applies the time bound after the
  shift/venue/`ver` checks. An unreadable end time or a missing grace setting refuses. A token signed before this change
  keeps its own `exp` (both bounds apply), so no already-printed QR gains validity. Unchanged: a QR for one shift is refused
  for another (`shift_mismatch`), the confirmed-assignment re-check, check-in-first, `assertClockWindow`, the geofence.
- **Not exported, one verifier:** `QrTokenService` is no longer exported from `AttendanceModule`; other modules get
  `AttendanceQrService` only. `qr-token-verify.arch.spec.ts` fails if any production file in rab-server or rab-worker
  other than `attendance-qr.service.ts` calls `QrTokenService.verify`, names the class outside the reviewed files, or
  derives the QR key (`rab-qr-token-v1`) itself.
- **Follow-ups approved by the owner (2026-11-14, branch fix/qr-followups).**
  - *14-day ceiling.* `QrTokenService.verify` refuses any QR whose `iat` is older than `QR_MAX_AGE_DAYS` (default 14,
    validated 1-90; jsonwebtoken `maxAge`), whatever the shift's end: `expired`. A token without `iat` is `invalid`; a
    missing setting refuses instead of verifying without a ceiling.
  - *Rotation (revocation).* `POST /rest/v1/shifts/:id/rotate-qr` (`SchedulingService.rotateShiftQr`) bumps
    `shift.qr_version` and `updated_at`; every older token is then refused `revoked` (a venue change stays
    `venue_mismatch`). Layers: `PermissionGuard(schedule.create)` (the shift-management flag cancel/archive use) → the
    same flag re-checked in the service first (403 for any id) → `assertShiftOwned` (404 out of scope, never 403) →
    refused 409 `SHIFT_CLOSED` for a status with no outgoing transition in `SHIFT_TRANSITIONS` (completed, cancelled,
    declined) → refused 409 `SHIFT_ENDED` once the shift has ended (`ends_at > now()` read in the same `SELECT … FOR
    UPDATE`, database clock; a missing row or null value also refuses — owner decision M2, 2026-11-15) → workspace RLS →
    compare-and-set on (qr_version, status) → audit `shift.qr_rotated` (shipped off-host as
    `security_configuration` / warning, like `venue.geofence_updated`). No client field is written. The bumped
    `updated_at` makes the pre-shift report scheduler regenerate and re-send the roster with the new QR, but only while
    the shift has not ended (its scan requires `ends_at > now()`). The DEFAULT Venue Manager role does not hold
    `schedule.create`, so it cannot rotate. A Venue Manager role granted `schedule.create` still cannot reach the route:
    it is manager-web only (`@ManagerApplication`) and the `venue_manager` role may only sign in to the Venue Manager app;
    the service itself applies the venue scope (404 outside the role's venues) for any other caller. API only for now
    (the QR is shown in the Venue Manager mobile apps, not the web console).
  - *Report rendered across a rotation (review M1).* The pre-shift scheduler locks the shift row before the report row,
    discards a render whose shift `qr_version` or `updated_at` changed while it rendered (no stored file, no email; the
    next tick rebuilds), and stamps the report with the database clock (`now()` of its write transaction). Rotation takes
    the shift row FOR UPDATE and then writes `updated_at = clock_timestamp()` (`rotate-shift-qr.sql.ts`), so a rotation
    that waited on the report's FOR SHARE lock writes a time after that commit, later than the stamp, and the next tick
    regenerates with the new QR. Pinned by a lock-wait regression test (fails with `now()`) and a source pin.
  - *Geofence-exit clock-out (review M3).* The automatic geofence-exit clock-out is a staff self clock-out too: refused
    `CLOCK_WINDOW_CLOSED` after the staff member's own end + grace, like the manual and on-behalf clock-outs.
  - *Settings (review L2).* `QR_POST_SHIFT_GRACE_MINUTES` is 0..1440, `QR_MAX_AGE_DAYS` 1..90 whole days, and the API and
    Worker refuse to boot when `REPORT_AVAILABLE_BEFORE_MINUTES >= QR_MAX_AGE_DAYS x 1440`. That guarantees only that a
    printed QR is still inside the age ceiling when the shift starts, not through its end + grace (shift length is not
    bounded by any setting).
  - *No rotation after the shift has ended (review M2, owner decision 2026-11-15).* A rotation after `ends_at` would strand
    staff still clocked in (the report is not regenerated after the end), so it is refused 409 `SHIFT_ENDED` in the
    service, under the shift row lock, before the compare-and-set and the audit write. Fail closed: a missing row or a null
    `not_ended` refuses (unit-tested with a mocked lock result); integration-tested over HTTP and from the service.
  - *Bounded corrected / recovered clock-out (review L4, owner decision 2026-11-15).* `correct(clockOutAt)` refuses 422
    `INVALID_CLOCK_OUT_TIME` when the value is in the future (database clock), before `clockInAt`, or after the staff
    member's OWN end + `QR_POST_SHIFT_GRACE_MINUTES` (`attendanceWindow(effectiveAssignmentTime(...)).closesAt`, the same
    bound as every other clock-out path). Every comparison is written "not inside", so an unreadable time refuses. Worked
    minutes still come only from `@rab/shared` `computeWorkedMinutes`. Tested per bound, including a seat that ends before
    the shift (own end, not shift end). The `correct(clockInAt)` lower bound that was open here is
    resolved by PR #163 (explicit confirmation below start − `CLOCK_IN_EARLY_MINUTES`, hard floor at start −
    `CLOCK_IN_CONFIRM_FLOOR_HOURS`); see "Unusually early clock-in needs explicit confirmation" below.
  - *Per-staff grace, end to end.* One grace, `QR_POST_SHIFT_GRACE_MINUTES` (120), always from the staff member's OWN end
    (`effectiveAssignmentTime`): the QR is accepted until own end + grace (`validUntil` takes the seat; `validateQr`
    requires it), the staff self clock-out now has the same `assertClockWindow` check the on-behalf clock-out has, and the
    attendance monitor flags MISSING_CLOCK_OUT and the manager recovery opens only strictly after it
    (`missing-clock-out-policy.ts` `isPastClockOutGrace`; the old 30-minute constant is gone). The staff clock-out and
    the manager recovery no longer overlap.
- **How a printed QR's validity can still grow.** A published shift cannot be rescheduled, but its end can move later:
  every offer with a per-staff time widens the shift envelope (`OfferService`, `GREATEST(ends_at, $3)`) with no ceiling in
  `validateAssignmentTime`. Since the follow-ups the QR follows the scanning staff member's own seat end, and the 14-day
  ceiling bounds any token's life absolutely.

```
SECURITY TRADE-OFF
Decision:   New Shift QR tokens carry no exp; expiry is decided at scan time from the staff member's own end + 120 min,
            under a hard 14-day age ceiling (QR_MAX_AGE_DAYS), with manager rotation to revoke.
Reason:     The owner's rule (decision 0i) is that an extended shift extends the QR. An exp fixed at signing either
            expires a QR printed 3 h early before the shift ends (the bug) or caps extensions arbitrarily.
Risk:       A leaked or photographed QR stays usable for that shift until the staff member's own end + grace (at most 14
            days from printing) unless a manager rotates it. The QR is only one factor: clock-in also needs the caller's
            own JWT, a CONFIRMED booking re-read fresh, check-in first and the clock window; clock-out needs the caller's
            own open attendance and the same window; at an enforcing venue both need a fresh geofence fix.
Mitigation: Signature/HS256/issuer/audience pinned; 14-day maxAge; shift, venue and qr_version re-checked on every scan;
            rotation (revoked); one verify caller (architecture test); unreadable end or missing settings refuse.
Reversal:   A shorter QR_MAX_AGE_DAYS, or rotating QRs automatically on schedule changes.
```
- **Tests:** `attendance-qr.service.spec.ts` (printed 3 h early: accepted in the last minutes and through the grace,
  refused 1 s after own end + grace; extended and shortened shifts; per-seat grace with two seats; 14-day ceiling at
  T+14d-1s / T+14d+1s and via the setting; no-iat; rotation `revoked` vs `venue_mismatch`; foreign shift; tampered /
  forged-key / malformed; wrong issuer / audience / HS512 / alg:none; legacy `exp`; fail-closed settings),
  `qr-token-verify.arch.spec.ts`, `env.validation.qr.spec.ts`, `shift-qr-rotation-scope` (other manager 404, venue-scoped
  role 403 over HTTP / 404 outside / rotates inside, overlapping rotations one 201 + one 409), `report-worker-concurrency`
  (rotation mid-render: discarded, no email; next tick's PDF QR decodes to ver 2), `attendance-abuse-cases` (geofence-exit
  CLOCK_WINDOW_CLOSED at own end + 121 min, control at + 100; clock-out with a QR printed 3 h early, CLOCK_WINDOW_CLOSED past
  own end + grace, rotateShiftQr: revoked / accepted, 403 guard and service, 404 other tenant, 409 cancelled / completed;
  the staff-vs-manager race just after the grace), rab-worker `worker-operations-abuse-cases` › clock-out grace end to end
  (monitor at own end + 100 min leaves the row open and the staff clock-out works; own end + 121 min refused then flagged;
  two seats: A flagged / refused after its own end + grace while B is accepted), and the pdf-equality self-test.

  refused 1 s after end + grace; extended and shortened shifts; foreign shift; tampered / forged-key / malformed; legacy
  `exp`; fail-closed config; wrong issuer / wrong audience / HS512 / alg:none refused), `qr-token-verify.arch.spec.ts`,
  `attendance-abuse-cases` › QR expiry follows the shift's current end + grace (the QR decision over HTTP with a QR
  printed 3 h before the start; the attendance monitor is not running there), and the pdf-equality self-test (the
  QR decoded from the PDF is accepted until its shift end + grace and refused 1 s later).

## OWNER-DB-ULTIMATE Part D: the first structural workspace command, `staff_profile_member_select` (structure level 21) and fingerprint v2 (branch feat/ws-staff-member-select)

- **What:**
  - The owner-approved SELECT policy `staff_profile_member_select` on every workspace schema's `staff_profile`, shipped as
    workspace upgrade command `0.6.0_StaffProfileMemberSelect_1786721480000`. The runner applies it per existing workspace; new
    workspaces get it from the re-created `core.provision_workspace`.
  - Fingerprint v2 (`core.workspace_schema_fingerprint_v2[_lines]`, rab_secure_owner-owned, SECURITY INVOKER, EXECUTE crewflow).
  - `verify_workspace_schema_v1` at 42 policies.
- **Threats:**
  1. A custom-role member reads staff of another workspace or organisation, or without staff.view.
  2. A member reads money (pay rates).
  3. A system role (Venue Manager, Staff) gains staff access through the policy.
  4. A tampered or pre-existing policy of the same name is silently accepted.
  5. A workspace stays at level 20 and is served by code that expects 21.
  6. The new fingerprint functions widen what the runtime can run.
- **Controls:**
  - (1) RLS binding: `organisation_id = core.current_org() AND workspace_id = core.current_workspace()`.
  - (1) The SECURITY INVOKER helper requires an ACTIVE membership of THIS workspace and a non-system role of THIS workspace holding
    staff.view. Tested: no staff.view → 0 rows; another workspace → 0; suspended or removed membership → 0; a role of another
    workspace → 0; a system role → 0; another organisation → 0; no tenant context → 0; the policy is SELECT only.
  - (2) Money is hidden in the service layer, not by RLS (RLS is row-level). MemberAccessPolicyService projection
    (`payRate` hidden by default, `sensitiveAuthority: payroll.view`); role writes and assignments refuse revealing a field whose
    authority the editor lacks (403 ROLE_ESCALATION); members can never hold payroll.view.
  - (3) `r.is_system = false`.
  - (4) The command creates the policy only when absent; the post-step v2 fingerprint check refuses anything else and the workspace
    is blocked (tested).
  - (5) The runner blocks a workspace below the code level (503 to its members, the Worker pauses); routing floor 20; the deploy
    post-check floor is unchanged.
  - (6) EXECUTE is granted to crewflow only; crewflow_app has none (tested). Not SECURITY DEFINER.
- **Accepted / open:**
  - A workspace owner who holds payroll.view can delegate visibility of the staff default pay rate to a member role (existing
    behaviour, owner question in WS-COMMANDS.md §0b.2).
  - Level-21 v2 fingerprints are declared for PostgreSQL 16, 17 and 18 (generated on throwaway clusters, identical across two frozen-template workspaces per major).
  - Fingerprint v2 known limits (v3 candidates, D-RUNNER §9.1): schema-local collations by name only, pg_default_acl, opclass/opfamily/text-search/extended statistics, relam/relreplident; the periodic drift job still compares v1 for level 21+.
  - down() refuses while any workspace still carries the policy (operator cleanup first), so a rollback can't leave level-21 workspaces failing verification.
- **Also fixed:** `RoleService.assertRelationsInScopeTx` read `core.venue` / `core.job_role` explicitly, so with HWS on every venue or job-role record filter on a member role was refused; it now reads through the tenant's bound search_path (core with HWS off, the validated workspace schema with HWS on).
- **Tests:**
  - `ws-staff-member-select.integration.spec.ts`;
  - the runner specs (probes at code level + 1);
  - the `server-path-provisioning-db` tamper cases;
  - unit guards: reviewed structure level 21 with floor 20, pending majors.

## Part C1 — HWS (one schema per workspace) on by default outside production; user deletion checks every workspace (branch hws/c1a-on-by-default, 2026-11-14)
- **Change.** `HWS_RUNTIME_ENABLED` unset now means ON in development and test and OFF when ANY production signal is set
  (`NODE_ENV`, `RAB_RUNTIME_ENV` or `DB_TARGET` = production, trimmed, any case; the existing `isProductionRuntime`). An explicit
  `true`/`false` wins everywhere; any other value refuses to boot. One rule (`hws-runtime-default.ts`) for the API, Worker and
  standalone provisioner. Production compose files still pin `"false"` until the C3 cutover. QA and the bullmq test stack flip to on.
- **Threats and controls.**
  - *HWS turned on in production by accident* (e.g. a CLI command run with `DB_TARGET=production` and no `NODE_ENV`), splitting
    writes between workspace schemas and `core` or letting `hws:backfill --apply` run outside the cutover: any production signal
    forces OFF; tests for the env class, the provisioner and the backfill guard.
  - *Manager venue list read another workspace* (`ManagerService.listVenues`, C0 audit BROKEN path): permission re-checked in the
    service (403), a manager outside the org or workspace is 404, an org admin's read is gated by `core.admin_workspace_in_org`,
    and the read runs in the target workspace's context.
  - *User hard delete erased history in another workspace* (C0 audit BROKEN path; another person's data): `assertCanDelete`
    checks the bound scope and every candidate workspace of the organisation (core copies and READY schema); a schema that exists
    but is not READY refuses with `USER_DELETION_UNVERIFIABLE` (workspace id logged server-side only); `user_note.subject_user_id`
    counts as history; `deleteUser` records visible staff history in every workspace scope before the delete and refuses (409,
    whole transaction rolled back) if any of it disappears; FK refusals (23503) are a 409, not a 500.
- **Other tenant-binding changes.** `storage:reconcile` binds the tenant identity without routing to a workspace schema (every
  query there is on `core.stored_file`, same RLS), so one non-READY workspace no longer stops it for every tenant; a `rab-ai` job
  for a workspace that is not yet routable is skipped (the Worker's `isNotYetRoutableWorkspace` rule), not failed; `seed-qa`
  provisions the workspace schema through `core.provision_workspace`.
- **Residual (owner review pending).** The per-workspace check runs under the caller's RLS, so "no rows" can mean "hidden". The
  post-delete re-check compares only `shift_assignment`, `job_offer` and `attendance`, and a narrow window remains: a staff
  profile the caller cannot see that gets its first history row from a concurrent transaction just before the delete is not in
  the snapshot. Rows in `shift_request_staff`, `venue_manager_staff` (cascade) and `replacement_request.selected_staff_profile_id`
  (set NULL) are not compared. A delete refused by a foreign key (23503) is reported as the same 409 (constraint/table names
  logged server-side). The complete control is a SECURITY DEFINER boolean `core.user_has_protected_history` covering all of
  these (draft in docs/plans/phase-x3/C1-STATUS.md, FOR OWNER REVIEW, not run anywhere).
- **Scale finding (owner decision pending).** Deleting a `core` row referenced from every workspace schema locks every referencing
  table (~31 per workspace for `core."user"`); from about 300 workspaces this fails with "out of shared memory" at the default
  `max_locks_per_transaction`. Applies to production today (schemas are provisioned with HWS off). CI's disposable database runs
  with `max_locks_per_transaction=2048`.
- **CI.** The server and Worker suites run HWS ON by default; one HWS-OFF job each keeps production's mode covered until C4
  (`--skip-nx-cache` so ON and OFF results never mix). Test-only: fixture workspace schemas are dropped after each test file on
  disposable databases (SECURITY TRADE-OFF in C1-STATUS: their core rows stay READY with no schema; routing refuses them, Worker
  scans skip them).
- **Tests.** env.validation.hws-runtime.spec.ts, workspace-provisioner.config.spec.ts, hws-c1-org-level-workspace-paths
  integration (venues 404 across workspace/org; delete refused for history in another schema, in the core copy, or an
  unverifiable schema; CEO cannot cascade another workspace's staff profile), the Worker isolation specs with a real
  wrong-organisation binding, and the full suites with HWS on (server 2,846 pass / 10 fail = the member staff-visibility gap
  awaiting owner SQL; Worker 741/741).

## Unusually early clock-in needs explicit confirmation, with a 12-hour hard floor (owner decisions 2026-11-15; branch feat/attendance-unusual-clock-in-warning, PR #163)
- **Threat:** corrected or recorded hours feed pay (money).
  - Before this, `POST /attendance/:id/correct` accepted any past clock-in with no lower bound. A mistyped or deliberate early time (for example 05:00 for a 09:00 shift) silently inflated worked minutes and pay for a Venue Manager with `attendance.edit` on the seat's venue.
  - `record-attendance` refused such a time outright (400), with no way to record a genuine early start.
- **Control: explicit confirmation, enforced in the service, not only the UI.**
  - A manager-entered clock-in earlier than the staff member's OWN scheduled start (`effectiveAssignmentTime`) minus `CLOCK_IN_EARLY_MINUTES` (15) is saved only when the request carries `confirmUnusualClockIn: true`.
  - Otherwise the answer is 409 `CLOCK_IN_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` (`earliestAllowed`, `enteredTime`) and nothing is written.
  - Checked in `AttendanceService` (layer 2) after:
    - the route guard (`PermissionGuard(attendance.edit)`, Venue Manager app only);
    - the service-level `attendance.edit` re-check;
    - the scope check (404 outside the venue / workspace);
    - the finalised-report lock;
    - every other validation and state rule.
  - It runs inside the workspace-bound transaction with workspace RLS.
  - The flag is declared on both DTOs (`@IsOptional() @IsBoolean()`; `forbidNonWhitelisted` stays global): a non-boolean is 400, and only the exact value `true` counts.
  - The allowance is the same `attendanceWindow().opensAt` every clock-in path uses. The comparison is written "not inside", so an unreadable bound asks for confirmation instead of passing.
  - The shift's scheduled start is only read, never written.
  - In `correct`, an identical resubmission of the stored value is the idempotent no-op, checked before the floor. It returns 201 (not 422) even when a later schedule change put that stored value beyond the floor; a new value there is still refused.
  - The floor is absolute on `correct` too (follow-up to PR #163): a `clockOutAt` or `breakMinutes` correction that leaves in place a stored clock-in now beyond the floor (after a later schedule move) is refused with 422 `CLOCK_IN_TOO_EARLY_ABSOLUTE`, with or without the confirmation, and nothing is written. Only a new clock-in can need the confirmation on this path.
- **Same rule on `record-attendance`.**
  - The old hard 400 for an early clock-in becomes the same 409 / confirm rule.
  - Every other check is unchanged: future, clock-out bound, out > in, break < span, version, booking state, finalised.
  - The overlap with another booking is not a pre-confirmation check: it is the database exclusion constraint (23P01) raised when the row is saved. A confirmed resend can therefore still get 409 for an overlap, and nothing is written.
  - On an existing row the clock-in is judged when the manager enters or changes it, and also when the stored one is kept but is now earlier than the allowance against the seat's CURRENT start (for example the seat start moved later) with no confirmation of exactly that time on record (see "Stored clock-in made unusual" below).
- **Hard floor.**
  - A clock-in earlier than the staff member's own start minus `CLOCK_IN_CONFIRM_FLOOR_HOURS` is always refused, even after Confirm: 422 `CLOCK_IN_TOO_EARLY_ABSOLUTE` (`earliestPossible`). This applies to both endpoints.
  - `CLOCK_IN_CONFIRM_FLOOR_HOURS` defaults to 12 and is validated as whole hours 1-48.
  - The API and Worker refuse to boot when `CLOCK_IN_CONFIRM_FLOOR_HOURS x 60 <= CLOCK_IN_EARLY_MINUTES`, and the service also clamps the floor so it is never later than the normal allowance. Written "not inside": an unreadable bound refuses.
  - This caps how far one acknowledged edit can move a clock-in, and so how much it can add to pay.
- **No second approver (owner decision 2026-11-15).** The confirmation is the entering manager's own explicit acknowledgement, not an extra authorisation. Any Venue Manager allowed to correct the seat can confirm.
- **Audit and visibility.**
  - The confirmed save is recorded in the existing single audit row: `attendance.corrected`, or `attendance.manager_recorded` for a new record.
  - Its metadata adds `unusualClockInConfirmed`, `earliestAllowed` and `confirmedClockInAt`; actor and time are the row's own.
  - The `attendance_correction` row keeps the original value, corrected value, reason and `corrected_by`.
  - No duplicate audit or correction rows; a retried Confirm writes nothing.
  - The shift report row the reviewer and finaliser see carries `unusualClockInConfirmed` ("Unusual time confirmed" in both mobile apps and the web Venue Offers timesheet).
    - It is derived server-side from that audit row, while the stored clock-in still equals the confirmed one and is still before the allowance.
    - It is never a client claim, and needs no new column or migration.
  - The row returns to `under_review`, so the existing attendance review and payroll approval still apply before any payment.
  - Worked minutes still come only from `@rab/shared` `computeWorkedMinutes`, priced at the confirmation-time rate snapshot.
- **Stored clock-in made unusual (review finding 2, closed by owner decision 2026-11-16, option b).**
  - On `record-attendance`, a stored clock-in that is not being changed is judged whenever it is now earlier than the allowance against the seat's current start and no audit row confirms exactly that time. The same predicate as the report flag: `unusualClockInConfirmed` with a matching `confirmedClockInAt`.
  - Then any write on the row needs `confirmUnusualClockIn: true` (409 `CLOCK_IN_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` otherwise), and the 12 h floor applies (422 `CLOCK_IN_TOO_EARLY_ABSOLUTE`, even confirmed).
  - The floor is absolute: it applies to a stored clock-in outside the allowance whether or not it was confirmed. If the start moves past a confirmed time + 12 h, the next record-attendance write is refused with 422 and nothing is written. The confirmation lookup only decides the 409.
  - The confirmation is checked last; nothing is written on refusal.
  - The confirmed write records `confirmedClockInAt` = the stored time in its audit row, so the report row then shows "Unusual time confirmed".
  - A stored clock-in already confirmed is never asked to confirm again; the floor still applies to it. One still inside the allowance is not judged.
  - The "not inside the allowance" test fails closed: an unreadable bound is judged.
- **Old app versions** (release note `packages/rab-iphone/docs/RELEASE_NOTES.md`):
  - An app built before this change cannot send `confirmUnusualClockIn`. It shows the 409 sentence as an error, so an unusually early clock-in cannot be saved until the app is updated.
  - Normal corrections are unaffected.
  - The floor applies to every version.

```
SECURITY TRADE-OFF
Decision:   An early manager-entered clock-in (between start - CLOCK_IN_CONFIRM_FLOOR_HOURS and start -
            CLOCK_IN_EARLY_MINUTES) is accepted with the entering manager's own explicit confirmation; no second
            approver. record-attendance moves from a hard 400 to the same confirm rule; on an existing row a stored
            clock-in is judged again only when it is now unusual and was never confirmed.
Reason:     Owner decisions 2026-11-15: genuine early starts must be recordable, a second approver is not wanted, and
            recording a missing clock-out must not re-ask about a clock-in that was already confirmed.
Risk:       A Venue Manager with attendance.edit can still add up to ~12 h before the staff member's start to paid time
            by confirming; the confirmation is an acknowledgement, not an authorisation.
Mitigation: 12 h hard floor (422, even confirmed) with a boot refusal for an inconsistent configuration; confirmation
            enforced in the service after every other rule; audited in the single audit row (unusualClockInConfirmed,
            earliestAllowed, confirmedClockInAt, actor, time); shown on the report row to the reviewer and finaliser;
            the row is reopened for review and payroll approval still applies before payment.
Reversal:   Lower CLOCK_IN_CONFIRM_FLOOR_HOURS, or require a second approver (payroll.approve) for a confirmed time.
```
- **Tests:**
  - `venue-manager-scoping.integration.spec.ts` › correct, unusually early clock-in:
    - a normal correction, and one exactly at start − 15 min, need no confirmation;
    - earlier without the flag, or with `false`, gets 409 with the exact body and nothing written; `'true'` is 400;
    - the allowance is measured from the seat's own start;
    - Confirm saves once: original and corrected values, the confirming manager, the time and the metadata are kept; a retry adds nothing; the report flag is set, and is cleared by a later normal correction;
    - future time and clock-in after clock-out are still 400, even with the flag;
    - a finalised report gets the existing 409; `clockOutAt` / `breakMinutes` with the flag record no confirmation; an open row gets the existing "still on shift" 409;
    - another workspace 404, the web console 403, revoked `attendance.edit` 403 at the route and `ForbiddenException` from the service;
    - floor: start − 12 h − 1 min gets 422 even confirmed; exactly start − 12 h gets 409, then 201;
    - re-sending the stored value after the schedule moved it beyond the floor is 201 with nothing written, and a new value there is 422;
    - a `clockOutAt` or `breakMinutes` correction with a stored clock-in beyond the moved floor gets 422 with or without the flag, nothing written; an identical resubmission is still 201.
  - `manual-attendance.integration.spec.ts` › record-attendance, unusually early clock-in:
    - early gets 409, then 200 with the flag; the audit row has the confirmation fields; the report row is flagged; idempotent; an ordinary record is not flagged;
    - existing row: an early change needs confirmation, and a later break-only change is not re-asked;
    - the same floor boundaries;
    - another workspace or another organisation gets 404 even with the confirmation, and nothing is written;
    - a stored clock-in made unusual by a later seat start: recording only the clock-out is 409 with nothing written; with Confirm it is saved, audited (`confirmedClockInAt` = the stored time) and flagged; a later break-only change is not re-asked; beyond the moved floor it is 422 even confirmed; still inside the allowance it is not asked;
    - the floor is absolute: a confirmed stored clock-in whose start then moves past it + 12 h gets 422 on the next write, with or without the flag, and nothing is written.
  - `env.validation.clock-in-floor.spec.ts` (range, plus the floor-vs-allowance boot refusal).
  - Flutter `report_review_timesheet_test.dart` and Swift `VMUnusualClockInTests` cover the dialog, Edit keeping values, Confirm resending with the flag, the 422 shown as an error and never the dialog, the report flag and the layouts.
  - rab-front `VenueOfferPipeline.spec.tsx` covers the timesheet flag.

## OWNER-DB-ULTIMATE Part D, decision 0a: workspace → core foreign keys removed (structure level 22; SQL owner-approved 2026-11-15; branch feat/ws-drop-core-fks, PR #149)

- **What:**
  - Workspace command `0.6.0_DropWorkspaceCoreForeignKeys_1786721530000` drops the 72 foreign keys from every workspace schema
    to `core."user"`, `core.organisation` and `core.manager_workspace` (31 + 21 + 20). The 56 foreign keys inside the schema
    stay. This follows the Twenty pattern: foreign keys only inside a workspace schema.
  - Core migration `WorkspaceCoreForeignKeyRemoval1786721530000`:
    - re-creates `verify_workspace_schema_v1` (56 FKs at level 22+);
    - re-creates `core.provision_workspace`, whose template has the 72 definitions removed, so a new workspace never creates
      them;
    - has a `down()` that refuses while level-22 workspaces exist.
  - Level-22 v2 fingerprints are declared for PostgreSQL 16, 17 and 18.
  - Integrity is now enforced by the application, plus a daily report-only orphan check.
- **Threats and controls:**
  - *A write stores a user, organisation or workspace id that does not exist or belongs to another tenant.*
    - Control: `organisation_id` / `workspace_id` are bound by FORCE RLS WITH CHECK plus each table's binding CHECK.
      Non-actor user ids go through `assertUsersOfOrganisationTx`: the user must exist in the caller's organisation, otherwise
      404. That is stricter than the old FK, which accepted any organisation's user.
    - Test: ws-core-fk-app-enforcement (another organisation, another workspace, a missing organisation; a missing or foreign
      user).
  - *F3, a reference write racing a user delete stores a dangling id.*
    - Control: the reference check takes `FOR KEY SHARE` on the referenced users, replacing the FK's lock. A concurrent delete
      waits for the writer, or the writer waits and then gets 404. core."user"'s UPDATE and SELECT policies share their USING
      predicate, so the lock never hides a readable row.
    - Test: ws-core-fk-app-enforcement F3 (an uncommitted delete blocks the check; after COMMIT it is 404).
  - *A user deletion orphans evidence or leaves personal data behind* (the lost RESTRICT / CASCADE / SET NULL). A user is
    soft-deleted by default (owner 0g); only a never-activated invite with no history is hard-deleted, inside a savepoint.
    - Before the delete, every scope is probed for the 23 former no-ON-DELETE user columns. A hit means a soft delete.
    - After the delete, the former CASCADE / SET NULL actions run in every scope. A 23503 rolls the savepoint back to a soft
      delete.
    - Tests: ws-core-fk-app-enforcement (RESTRICT probe → soft; CASCADE / SET NULL → hard with the own profile removed and
      attribution cleared; a payslip still needing the profile → 23503 → soft; a paid shift → soft).
  - *F2, a hard delete loses pay history hidden from the caller.* Owner decision (b), no new SQL.
    - Control: in a workspace schema, visible history of a staff profile the caller cannot see makes the hard delete unsafe,
      so the account is soft-deleted (the 0g rule).
    - Cost, stated plainly: this is deliberately over-strict. Another user's hidden history counts too. Once any
      creator-private staff history exists in a workspace, a CEO hard delete of an invite effectively always falls back to soft.
    - Tests (hws-c1 4.6), each case asserting the logged fallback reason:
      - L1 hidden-profile cases: `hidden_workspace_history` with HWS on (`history_lost` with HWS off); soft delete, profile
        and history intact, no new orphan;
      - an explicit over-strict case: another user's hidden profile with visible history, then a CEO delete of a clean
        invite: soft, `hidden_workspace_history`, the other profile intact, orphan count unchanged.
  - *F1, the Worker invite cleanup hard-deletes an expired invitee still referenced from a level-22 schema.* Before this fix the
    definer's `foreign_key_violation` guard was the only protection.
    - Control, in every READY level-22 schema of the organisation:
      - the history checks run again with read rights that see every row, and the 23 columns are probed;
      - after the definer's delete, the invitee's own references are cleared, then the Worker verifies that none is left;
      - a leftover or a 23503 rolls the candidate back and retains it.
    - Control (re-review N1): a workspace schema that exists but does not resolve (not READY, unsupported version, name
      mismatch) retains the invitee and is never skipped.
    - Tests: account-invite-cleanup integration (a paid-shift invitee is retained with every row and no orphan; a profile-only
      invitee is deleted with its profile and no orphan; an unresolvable schema retains it) and off-means-off case 6 under the
      production login.
  - *F1-T, accepted by the owner 2026-11-15: the Worker reads and writes as the workspace owner.*
    - The binding is `rab.actor_type = 'worker'` plus `rab.user_id = manager_workspace.owner_user_id`, the same as the orphan
      check's (0a-T2).
    - It is used ONLY to check, and then clear, that one invitee's own references: its staff profile, the notes about it, and
      its attribution columns.
    - It runs only in a Worker maintenance job with no request input. The settings are transaction-local and are restored per
      workspace.
    - Tests: the F1-T scope cases.
      - Under the owner-member production login (off-means-off case 7): the schema has 0 FKs to core."user", the invitee and
        its profile are gone, another user's profile and notes are untouched, and a note the invitee wrote about that user
        keeps its subject with the author cleared. No orphan.
      - The same case as the superuser fixture login (account-invite-cleanup F1-T).
      - With HWS off both cases are core-FK scope checks.
      - The CASCADE / SET NULL / RESTRICT classification (2 / 6 / 23 columns) is pinned in workspace-user-references.spec.
  - *Orphans accumulate unnoticed.*
    - Control: a daily Worker orphan check, report-only, counts only (never ids or values). It reads as the Worker plus the
      workspace owner's read rights, in a READ ONLY transaction.
    - Test: ws-core-fk-removal (a planted orphan is found).
  - *The old lock storm* (availability): one core delete used to lock every referencing table of every workspace.
    - Control: removing these FKs removes the fan-out.
    - Tests: ws-core-fk-removal measured 1,430 relation locks with 13 level-21 workspaces and 0 at level 22; user-soft-delete
      shows no lock in another organisation's schemas.
- **Accepted by the owner (2026-11-15):**
  - R-1: the delete-time checks see only what the caller may read. Residual: anything the caller cannot read is never
    deleted, but can stay as an orphan of the deleted invite, which the daily orphan check reports. That covers:
    - a hidden profile whose history is also hidden;
    - a workspace outside the caller's candidate set;
    - history added to a hidden profile after the snapshot.
  - R-2: the expired-invite definer (1786721520000) is unchanged. The level-22 path in the Worker covers it (F1).
  - R-3: 0a is re-applied on top of C1's and 0g's user deletion.
  - R-4: each workspace's upgrade step holds ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on the three core tables (bounded by the runner's 5 s
    lock_timeout). Run the 0.6.0 upgrade in a quiet window (MIGRATION-AND-ROLLBACK-PLAN.md §4.4). The TypeScript provisioner
    (rollback artifact) still creates and then drops the FKs.
- **Tests:**
  - ws-core-fk-app-enforcement;
  - ws-core-fk-removal (lock test, orphan report);
  - account-invite-cleanup (F1, F1-T, N1) and account-invite-cleanup-off-means-off case 7 (F1-T under the production login);
  - workspace-user-references.spec (the classification);
  - hws-c1 4.6 with asserted fallback reasons, and user-soft-delete (0g + 0a);
  - payroll-evidence-restrict (the F3 raw delete at level 22);
  - the runner and template suites on top of level 22.

## Part C3 — HWS cutover copy path: core business tables copied into one schema per workspace (option A′ and SQL owner-approved 2026-11-15; branch feat/c3-cutover-copy, PR #150; OFF until release 0.7.0)

- **What:**
  - Core migration `HwsCutoverCopyFunctions1786721540000` (SQL in
    `database/typeorm/workspace-schema/backfill/hws-cutover-sql.ts`, beside `privileged-copy.ts`) adds:
    - frozen crewflow SECURITY DEFINER functions that probe, copy (in batches) and verify the 21 workspace business tables of
      one workspace, from `core` into that workspace's own schema;
    - two rab_secure_owner tables: `core.hws_cutover_state` (per workspace: `started` / `verified`) and
      `core.hws_cutover_activation` (a one-way singleton sentinel);
    - a write fence trigger on the 21 core tables;
    - an AFTER INSERT trigger on `core.manager_workspace` that marks a new workspace `verified` once the cutover is active;
    - TRUNCATE guards on both new tables;
    - `core.hws_cutover_started_any()` for the boot check.
  - Instance upgrade command `0.7.0_HwsCutover_1786721540100` (`upgrade-commands/0-7/hws-cutover.ts`), resumable and
    idempotent:
    - it blocks every pending workspace first;
    - it refuses without a verified backup;
    - then, per workspace, it marks the workspace `started`, copies, and compares per-table row counts and checksums;
    - it marks the workspace `verified` and unblocks it only if they match.
  - Fail-closed routing (`hws-cutover-routing.ts`, read in the resolver's registry query): `started` is always refused. Once
    the sentinel exists, anything other than `verified` is refused with 503 "workspace is being upgraded"; that includes a
    missing row and an unreadable table.
  - **Off in #150:** the `0-7` command directory is NOT registered, so no deployment runs it. The 0.7.0 release's entry
    ("Part C3 switched on") will cover (draft #175, not merged) registration, the version bump, switching HWS on in
    production and the backup mount.
- **Threats and controls:**
  - *A copy puts one tenant's rows into another workspace's schema.*
    - Control: every definer call is bound to one workspace and its organisation (tenant GUCs, set per transaction). Source
      rows are filtered by `workspace_id` AND `organisation_id = core.current_org()`. Core rows of W that carry another
      organisation (`org_mismatch`) refuse W. Each workspace table's `<table>_workspace_bound` CHECK rejects a foreign row.
    - Test: hws-c3-cutover "review L-1" (a core row of W under another organisation is never copied; W is refused,
      ORG_MISMATCH).
  - *The RLS bypass window (SECURITY TRADE-OFF A′, owner-accepted).* FORCE RLS has to be lifted to read every row of W from
    core and write it into W's schema.
    - Control: FORCE is lifted only inside frozen crewflow SECURITY DEFINER functions, under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on each
      relation. It is restored and asserted before return, and never committed off: a failure rolls the lift back with the
      transaction.
    - Control: EXECUTE on the probe / copy / verify / pointer definers only to crewflow and its members (that includes the
      runtime login under owner-login, BC-01); PUBLIC holds nothing; crewflow_app holds EXECUTE only on
      hws_cutover_started_any() (boolean). The migration advisory lock on the same backend and the tenant guard are mistake
      guards, not the authorisation boundary.
    - Test: hws-c3-cutover:
      - abuse cases (no lock, another tenant, a table outside the list, limits, not READY, crewflow_app → refused);
      - a kill partway through the copy leaves the workspace blocked, FORCE on and no verified row.
  - *A partially copied workspace is served* (data appears missing, or writes land in a half-copied schema).
    - Control: every pending workspace is blocked (Part D marker, 503) before any copy. The cache epoch is bumped right
      after blocking, and a failed bump stops the step.
    - Control: a workspace whose copy started but did not verify is refused by the resolver even without its marker.
    - Control: the rule "anything but `verified` is refused" is gated on the one-way database sentinel. The sentinel has no
      UPDATE or DELETE policy and is TRUNCATE-guarded, so pruning or rolling back the command cannot switch fail-closed
      routing off.
    - Test: hws-c3-cutover:
      - "review H-1" (a probe that cannot get its lock fails only after every workspace with core rows is blocked);
      - "review L-4" (the epoch bump);
      - "fail-closed routing" ×3: with no state, a workspace is refused once the cutover is active; when the scan's first
        query throws, nothing is blocked, yet no workspace is served from an empty schema; a workspace created after the
        cutover is marked at insertion and served;
      - "re-check N-2" (the sentinel survives DELETE / UPDATE by crewflow, crewflow_app, crewflow_worker and the runtime
        login; TRUNCATE by the runtime login, crewflow and crewflow_app).
  - *A copy runs without a way back* (owner rule: a backup before every cutover).
    - Control: the command refuses before any copy unless `CREWFLOW_HWS_CUTOVER_BACKUP_MARKER` names a verified backup:
      - the marker is bound to this database's name and, when `pg_control_system()` is readable, to this cluster's
        `system_identifier`;
      - it is at most 24 h old by the database clock, and not from the future;
      - the dump next to it has a `PGDMP` header and the recorded size, and is re-hashed in full (sha256);
      - `restoreVerified` is true;
      - files are opened without following symlinks (O_NOFOLLOW and O_NONBLOCK, then fstat).
    - Test:
      - hws-c3-cutover "no backup → refused" (the workspace is blocked, nothing is copied);
      - unit hws-cutover.spec covers the marker refusals: unset, not JSON, extra or missing field, restore not attested,
        another database, another cluster, older than 24 h, from the future, a path in `dumpFile`, a missing, truncated,
        swapped or non-custom dump. The refusal never echoes the marker path or its content.
  - *A copy that does not match is switched over.*
    - Control: per table, row counts and checksums of every column are compared between core and the workspace schema,
      inside SQL. Money is compared as bigint pence in SQL and never logged.
    - Control: a mismatch leaves W `started` and blocked (`HWS_CUTOVER_MISMATCH`), never half-switched.
    - Control: a workspace whose own schema already holds rows while it is not `started` is refused (`BOTH_POPULATED`).
      Under owner decision Q5 an operator merges by hand; core rows are never discarded.
    - Test: hws-c3-cutover:
      - "resume" (every table verified: counts, rows, checksums, money, minutes; no duplicate, no gap);
      - checksum mismatch → blocked;
      - both-populated → refused, nothing merged.
  - *A crash or kill mid-copy leaves a broken workspace, or a re-run duplicates rows.*
    - Control: the copy is batched and keyed (`ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`). `started` survives a crash, and the next start
      resumes and verifies.
    - Control: only the statement pointers of payroll rows a batch itself inserted are reconciled. Live workspace pointers
      are never touched, so no duplicate pay statements.
    - Test: hws-c3-cutover:
      - kill, then resume;
      - "idempotent" (a second run copies nothing and writes no second verified row);
      - "review M-1" (a live pointer survives fail-then-succeed);
      - the Part B logbook records failed, then completed.
  - *Writes to a core copy after its workspace was cut over are silently lost* (an HWS-off or older process still writes to
    core).
    - Control: the write fence on the 21 core tables refuses INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE of a workspace's rows for the runtime
      logins (42501) from the moment its cutover is `started` (a state row exists), so a stale writer fails loudly.
      `core.user_note` has no `workspace_id` and is fenced per organisation (any workspace of the organisation started).
      attendance_correction stays insert-only, as before.
    - Control (review M-3): an API or Worker started with `HWS_RUNTIME_ENABLED=false` refuses to boot once any workspace's
      cutover has started or the sentinel exists (`core.hws_cutover_started_any()`, in `assertHwsStartupInvariants`).
    - Control: with HWS off, the cutover command refuses (`HWS_RUNTIME_OFF`) when any workspace is pending, writing
      nothing: no block, no state, no sentinel. With nothing pending it returns without writing, which the runner would
      record as complete; the step is unregistered on main, so this never runs. From 0.7.0 (#175) that case becomes an
      unrecorded deferral.
    - Test:
      - hws-c3-cutover "review M-3" (a fenced write → 42501; the HWS-off boot guard refuses) and "HWS off: refused,
        nothing blocked, nothing copied";
      - unit hws-startup-guard.spec.
  - *Rows are dropped because they do not map to exactly one workspace.*
    - Control (owner decisions Q2 and Q12): nothing is dropped.
      - A note whose subject has profiles in more than one workspace refuses that workspace
        (`HWS_CUTOVER_USER_NOTE_AMBIGUOUS`).
      - A note whose subject has no profile refuses every workspace of the organisation (`HWS_CUTOVER_USER_NOTE_UNMAPPED`).
      - Rows of the organisation with no workspace refuse it (`HWS_CUTOVER_UNOWNED_ROWS`).
      - The operator report lists up to 100 note ids, for assignment by hand.
    - Test: hws-c3-cutover:
      - "review M-2" (one bad workspace does not keep the others blocked);
      - "review L-3" (ambiguous notes count as core data);
      - "owner decision Q2" (unmapped: the note is named, nothing is dropped);
      - "re-check Info-A" (unowned rows).
  - *The cutover state is forged to mark an uncopied workspace `verified`* (re-check N-1).
    - Control: `core.hws_cutover_state` and the sentinel are rab_secure_owner-owned.
      - Only crewflow (the cutover, through owner-only policies) and the new-workspace trigger write them.
      - No function an application session can call writes them, and an UPDATE faking a "new" workspace never marks it.
      - crewflow_app and crewflow_worker read only. The runtime login reads only as itself, but under owner-login it can act
        as crewflow and then write them (accepted residual R-2, BC-01).
      - Audit rows are never read back as state.
    - Test: hws-c3-cutover:
      - "re-check N-1": as crewflow_app and as crewflow_worker, a direct state or sentinel INSERT → 42501, and the faked-new
        UPDATE marks nothing;
      - "review L-2": a forged audit row does not make W verified.
  - *TRUNCATE bypasses RLS*, so the runtime login (owner-login model, BC-01) could empty the state or the sentinel.
    - Control: statement-level BEFORE TRUNCATE triggers (`core.hws_cutover_truncate_guard()`); only rab_secure_owner itself
      and a superuser pass.
    - Test: hws-c3-cutover "re-check N-2" (TRUNCATE by the runtime login, crewflow and crewflow_app → 42501).
  - *Disclosure through logs or the audit trail.*
    - Control: logs and the `workspace.hws_cutover_verified` audit row carry only workspace ids, table names, counts and
      checksums, plus the user_note ids of the Q2/Q12 operator report and the backup's takenAt: no money, no row values, no
      marker path, no URL.
  - *One start keeps the API blocked for too long* (availability).
    - Control (owner decision Q6): each start has a 5-minute budget (`HWS_CUTOVER_TIME_BUDGET_MS`). Once it is spent, no
      further workspace starts, but every start makes at least one. The rest stay blocked with 503 and continue at the next
      start (`HWS_CUTOVER_TIME_BUDGET`).
    - Test: hws-c3-cutover "owner decision Q6".
- **Accepted by the owner (2026-11-15):**
  - R-1 (A′): FORCE is lifted inside a frozen definer call on the 21 core tables AND the 21 tables of W's own schema (the
    probe: all 43 relations at once, including `core.manager_profile` read-only). The SQL injection residual is unchanged:
    the owner login can already act as crewflow (BC-01).
  - R-2: crewflow has an owner-only SELECT policy on `core.hws_cutover_state`, so the boot check needs no tenant. As a result,
    a session that can SET ROLE crewflow sees every workspace's cutover state: workspace and organisation ids and timestamps,
    no business data. The same session can also write them (INSERT / UPDATE a verified state, INSERT the sentinel), and one
    that can SET ROLE rab_secure_owner can TRUNCATE both; same BC-01 residual as R-1.
  - R-3: the write fence lets crewflow, rab_secure_owner and a superuser through, because FK cascades from organisation and
    manager_workspace run as the owner. The injection residual is unchanged.
  - R-4: when `pg_control_system()` is unreadable (a managed provider), the backup is bound by database NAME only, so a dump
    of a same-named database on another cluster would pass the name check. The control is the runbook's "dump this database,
    verify the restore" steps.
  - R-5: each probe, copy or verify call holds ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on whole core tables (all organisations) for its duration —
    a probe on all 21 plus `core.manager_profile` at once — bounded by the per-start budget.
  - R-6: Q3 (VALIDATE `staff_profile_workspace_required` after a verified copy) is deferred to a structural workspace
    command at level 23, with its own owner SQL review. Validating inside the cutover would move every cut-over workspace off
    its level's expected fingerprint.
- **Tests:**
  - hws-c3-cutover.integration.spec:
    - the abuse cases of every function; HWS off refused; no backup refused and blocked;
    - kill then resume; copy correctness; idempotent re-run; checksum mismatch blocked; both-populated never merged;
    - zero rows with no tenant context; the logbook records failed, then completed;
    - the review cases H-1, M-1, M-2, M-3, L-1 to L-4, N-1, N-2 and Info-A; fail-closed routing; Q2 and Q6.
    - The sentinel is one-way in production, so the spec removes it as the cluster superuser after each run; otherwise
      routing in the shared CI database would change for every later spec.
  - hws-cutover.spec (unit): the frozen 21-table lists, the backup marker refusals, the routing truth table, and that neither
    the routing gate nor any application code depends on the registry or writes the state;
  - hws-startup-guard.spec: the HWS-off boot refusal;
  - the security-posture and semantic goldens (PG16/17/18), the R4 secure-owner invariants, check-rls-coverage
    (`hws_cutover_activation` forced), and the restricted-migrator drift review.

## Metadata engine M1: metadata tables (E1, #165), versioned cache (E5, #164), standard-object sync (E2, #166) (branches feat/metadata-m1-tables, feat/metadata-m1-cache, feat/metadata-m1-sync; M1 SQL owner-approved on conditions 2026-11-15, owner decision batch 11; final SQL incl. universal_identifier approved 2026-11-16)

- **What.** Crewflow's re-implementation of Twenty's metadata engine (twentyhq/twenty @ eedb0a73; behaviour re-implemented,
  never copied — AGPL). E1: `core.object_metadata`, `field_metadata`, `field_metadata_option`, `index_metadata`,
  `index_field_metadata` and the trigger function `core.metadata_guard()` (migration MetadataEngineTables1786721550000).
  E5: `core.workspace_metadata_state` (one version row per workspace) and the per-workspace metadata cache
  (MetadataVersionState1786721560000). E2: the 21 workspace tables synced into metadata as standard objects, per workspace
  (the 0.6.0 SyncStandardObjects upgrade step and the new-workspace path). Each table carries `organisation_id` +
  `workspace_id`. Metadata describes another tenant's data model and decides which columns the generic API exposes
  (money, sensitivity, read-only), so a write to it is a write to what the engine trusts.
- **Threats.**
  1. A workspace reads or changes another workspace's metadata, or any metadata with no tenant bound.
  2. The request path loosens built-in metadata: unlocks a locked field, clears `is_money` / `is_sensitive` /
     `is_ui_read_only`, renames an API name or repoints a physical name, deletes a standard or system object, or adds a
     custom field to a payroll / attendance object.
  3. A custom row takes ("squats") the universal identifier of a standard object or field before the sync inserts it, so the
     sync fails for that workspace or adopts the wrong row.
  4. A poisoned or stale cache entry serves a workspace another workspace's metadata, or old metadata after a change.
