  5. The privileged section of the sync leaks the `crewflow` role or a binding into later statements, or runs anything
     beyond the reviewed statements while elevated.
- **Controls.**
  - **Tenant isolation (all five tables):** ENABLE + FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and one tenant policy
    (`organisation_id = core.current_org() AND workspace_id = core.current_workspace()`, USING = WITH CHECK) in the same
    migration; composite foreign keys to `core.manager_workspace (id, organisation_id)` and between the metadata tables
    (no cross-workspace parent, relation target or label identifier). Owner `crewflow` (handed over inside
    withCrewflowCoreCreate), `crewflow_app` S/I/U/D, nothing for PUBLIC: the same shape as shift, venue, manager_venue and
    role_object/field_permission (security-posture.golden.txt; same policy hash in the semantic golden). `crewflow_owner`
    reaches them through its membership of `crewflow` (INHERIT; ADMIN only on crewflow_app), so FORCE RLS and the guard
    are the boundary; crewflow_app lacks only TRUNCATE, which the guard refuses, so no grant-parity trigger is needed.
  - **Identity split (`core.metadata_guard()`, BEFORE INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE and BEFORE TRUNCATE on all five):** only
    `crewflow`, `rab_secure_owner` or a superuser (the M-T2 allow-list) may insert or change built-in / locked metadata,
    options or index fields of built-in / locked fields, or indexes on built-in objects. The request path (crewflow_owner,
    crewflow_app) may change only display columns (label, description, icon, position) of built-in rows, and of system rows
    only the position. Physical names, type, kind flags, API names (OB-10), universal identifier, object and relation
    targets are immutable for everyone; a lock never comes off; standard / system objects and locked / system fields are
    never deleted directly (cascades from a custom object or a workspace still work). Parent lookups fail closed (23503)
    and hold the parent FOR SHARE. Error messages carry no input values. SECURITY INVOKER, pinned search_path, no PUBLIC
    EXECUTE.
  - **Payroll / attendance pinned to system:** `object_metadata_payroll_locked_ck` forces the 7 payroll / attendance
    objects (attendance, attendance_correction, payroll_record, payroll_run, payroll_run_line, payslip, payslip_document)
    to `is_system AND NOT allows_custom_fields`, so no custom field and no label change reaches them. Money fields are only
    locked, sensitive, read-only built-in NUMBERs; CURRENCY only on custom objects; core references only for four known
    core tables; labels refuse control, bidi and zero-width characters.
  - **Universal identifier (owner batch 11, Twenty syncable-entity alignment):** every object and field row carries one,
    NOT NULL, unique per workspace (`(workspace_id, universal_identifier)`), immutable. `<table>_universal_identifier_kind_ck`
    splits the namespace: custom rows hold a random version-4 UUID (column DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()), built-in rows the
    sync's deterministic version-8 UUID. A custom row therefore can never squat a standard identifier, and a built-in insert
    that forgets its identifier gets the v4 default and is refused (fails closed). Options, indexes and index fields are
    keyed by immutable natural keys and not synced by identifier.
  - **E5 cache (#164):** the version row moves in the same transaction as every metadata change (AFTER ROW trigger
    `core.metadata_version_bump()`, at most once per transaction, never backwards; the row is written only by that
    trigger, guarded by `core.workspace_metadata_state_guard()`), so committed metadata and the version never disagree
    (Twenty bumps after commit). Concurrent first changes serialise on a per-workspace advisory lock
    (`pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended('crewflow:metadata:' || workspace))`). Redis entries are HMAC-SHA256 envelopes
    bound to the Redis key, under a purpose sub-key derived from the existing auth-cache MAC key (APP_AUTH_CACHE_HMAC_KEY /
    APP_SECRET, no new secret); a bad MAC, a different identity (workspace, version, bump time) or any doubt rebuilds from
    PostgreSQL under the caller's tenant binding.
  - **E2 sync (#166):** built-in metadata is written in a narrow privileged section: `SAVEPOINT std_sync`, then
    `SET LOCAL ROLE crewflow`, only the fixed parameterised STANDARD_SYNC_SQL statements (read stored rows, insert / update
    the differences, never a delete), then the role and bindings are restored and checked. On any error
    `ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT std_sync` reverts role, bindings and metadata together. Pinned at runtime and statically by the
    elevated-statements specs.
  - **Upgrade runner (Part D):** a workspace command that declares `writesWorkspaceMetadata` may INSERT / UPDATE only its own
    workspace's rows of object_metadata, field_metadata, field_metadata_option and workspace_metadata_state
    (`WORKSPACE_METADATA_TABLES`, per-table write counters); every other write outside the schema keeps the "no write" rule.
- **Accepted limits (owner-accepted 2026-11-15, same boundary as option N / BC-01).**
  - **Injected SQL is detection-only.** `crewflow_owner` can, through its membership of `crewflow`, `SET ROLE crewflow`,
    ALTER, DISABLE TRIGGER or DROP these tables and replace the guard. The guard and the checks protect normal code paths;
    the semantic posture monitor detects a disabled or re-pointed trigger or a changed body afterwards.
  - **TRUNCATE rules.** TRUNCATE ignores RLS: it is refused to the request path on all five tables (also through
    `TRUNCATE core.manager_workspace CASCADE`) and allowed for the privileged identities (operators; test teardowns
    truncating as the superuser). The E5 version row is not TRUNCATE-guarded; the bump time in the cache identity makes a
    recreated row a new identity.
  - **pg_trigger_depth gap.** The delete lock applies at trigger depth 1 (a direct DELETE); deeper deletes are let through
    so FK cascades (workspace, organisation, a custom object's fields, a custom field's options) work. A DELETE issued from
    inside another trigger or function would also pass; creating one needs the BC-01 rights above.
  - **M1-S1 (SECURITY TRADE-OFF): the Part D runner may write its own workspace's metadata.** A command declaring
    `writesWorkspaceMetadata` runs as `crewflow` (the guard's privileged identity) and may insert / update that workspace's
    built-in metadata. The runner's write counters restrict it to the four tables above and to INSERT / UPDATE in the bound
    workspace; commands are reviewed code, never input-driven (same D-T1 detector limits as Part D).
  - **Universal identifier namespace is stricter than Twenty (owner-accepted 2026-11-16).** Twenty accepts any UUID; here custom = v4, built-in = v8.
    It is the cheapest database rule that stops squatting; if standard identifiers ever become hand-written constants, the
    CHECK changes in a new migration. The M2 executor must give the built-in system fields of custom objects a v8 identifier.
- **Tests.** Unit: the reviewed SQL text (metadata-tables-sql.spec.ts, metadata-version-sql.spec.ts), the cache envelope and
  LRU, the sync plan and its golden identifier digest, the elevated statements. Integration on the owner-login database as
  crewflow_owner (metadata-tables.integration.spec.ts): MD-1 catalog; MD-2 zero rows unbound; MT-07 cross-tenant reads and
  WITH CHECK; MD-3 composite keys; MT-26 / #165 the identity split and immutability; MD-4 type and shape rules; MD-5
  TRUNCATE; MD-6 workspace cascade; MD-7 the read service; MD-8 the RLS coverage gate; MD-9 universal identifiers; MD-10
  owner condition 2, on the real request path through TenantContextService (bound workspace read / write only, zero rows
  and no write unbound, no access to another workspace). #164: the version and cache specs, including concurrent first
  changes (condition 1). #166: the catalog, new-workspace and M1-S1 runner specs, and the role / binding restore after an
  error in the elevated section (condition 3).

## X2.5 — HTTP-first API shutdown, a bounded Worker drain, the owner-login connection budget (XR-09, XR-10, XD-05) (branch phase-x/x25-reliability, 2026-11-15, PR #168)
- **Asset:** the rate limiting of the credential routes (`@RateLimitRequired`, Redis-backed throttler); the API's and
  Worker's availability across a restart; the database's connection capacity and `crewflow_owner`'s connection limit.
- **XR-09, before:** `app.enableShutdownHooks()` let Nest quit the throttler and auth-cache Redis clients, the BullMQ
  producers and the realtime subscriber (`onModuleDestroy`) while the HTTP listener still accepted requests. The throttler
  failed closed, so every credential request in the stop window (up to the 40 s grace) got 503 `RATE_LIMIT_UNAVAILABLE`.
  Rate limiting was never bypassed, but sign-in and recovery broke for the whole window.
- **XR-09, control:** `engine/utils/http-first-shutdown.ts` replaces the shutdown hooks:
  1. the listener closes first, so new connections are refused and the client retries another replica;
  2. requests already in flight drain for up to 15 s while Redis is still up, so each one is still throttled by the real
     guard; responses sent during the drain close their connection;
  3. every remaining connection is closed, SSE streams included;
  4. only then does `app.close()` quit queues/Redis and then the database;
  5. the signal is re-raised (same exit status).

  A 35 s backstop exits 1 if the shutdown hangs, before Docker's SIGKILL at the 40 s grace.
  No request can reach a guard after its Redis client has quit. The in-flight tracker is registered ahead of Express's
  handler and also reads `writeHead` headers, so an SSE stream never holds the drain open.
- **XR-10, control:** `WORKER_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS` is declared and parsed strictly
  (`worker-shutdown-timeout.contract.ts`): unset means 30000; an integer 1000..34000 is accepted; anything else refuses to
  boot in both processes (it used to become NaN at shutdown, which skipped the drain, or outlived the 45 s grace, so the
  Worker was SIGKILLed mid-job). The message never echoes the value.
- **XD-05, control:** the startup connection budget counts every connection the single owner login opens: pools, /healthz
  probe, the Worker's in-process provisioner, the migrate-on-start child (now 5) and the boot probes. A `rolconnlimit` on
  `crewflow_owner` is compared with that whole total, and a deployment over capacity or over the login limit refuses to
  start (fail closed, unchanged rule; before, the check understated the login's use).
- **Residual:** a client must retry a refused connection (single API with stop-then-start: a short refusal window instead
  of 503s). A request still running at the 15 s deadline is cut. A deployment within two connections of its limit now
  refuses to boot (operator check in the PR).
- **Tests:** `http-first-shutdown.spec.ts` (refusal, not 503; in-flight request answered before Redis quits; streams
  recognised however their headers were set; deadline cut; second signal ignored; close failure exits 1),
  `api-shutdown-order.integration.spec.ts` (real AppModule and Redis-backed throttler), `worker-shutdown-timeout.contract.spec.ts`,
  `env.validation.worker-shutdown-timeout.spec.ts`, `connection-budget.spec.ts`, `connection-budget.event-listener.spec.ts`.

## X3.1 — on/off switches refuse a typo at boot (XR-05 / ENV-01) (branch phase-x/x31-strict-booleans, 2026-11-15, PR #169)
- **Asset:** the deployment's security and routing posture as the operator configured it: session-enforcement cutover,
  sign-in methods, SMTP TLS, the auth/session/entity caches, email, push and realtime delivery.
- **Actor:** an operator (or a template, override or platform setting) entering a switch value that is not exactly `true`.
- **Before:** fourteen switches (`EMAIL_DELIVERY_ENABLED`, `AUTH_CONTEXT_CACHE_ENABLED`, `USER_SESSION_CACHE_ENABLED`,
  `CORE_ENTITY_CACHE_ENABLED`, `WORKSPACE_METADATA_CACHE_ENABLED`, `WORKER_FAST_PUBLISH_NOTIFY`,
  `USER_SESSION_ENFORCEMENT_CUTOVER`, `AUTH_PASSWORD_ENABLED`, `AUTH_GOOGLE_ENABLED`, `AUTH_MICROSOFT_ENABLED`,
  `AUTH_OAUTH_HANDOFF_ENABLED`, `EMAIL_SMTP_NO_TLS`, `REALTIME_ENABLED`, `PUSH_ENABLED`) read `value === 'true'`, so any
  other value (`True`, `1`, `yes`, ` true`, a typo) silently meant false. For example `USER_SESSION_ENFORCEMENT_CUTOVER=True`
  left the cutover off, and nothing reported the mismatch.
- **Control:** all fourteen use the shared `strictBoolean` helper (`environment-variables.ts`). Exactly `true` or `false` is
  accepted, unset or empty keeps the default, and anything else refuses to boot (fail closed) with
  `<NAME> must be exactly true or false`. The message names the variable, never the value. The compose gate
  (`scripts/compose-owner-login.cjs`, `STRICT_SWITCHES`) refuses the same values in env files, templates and rendered
  services, so a typo fails the lint before it reaches a running host. `S3_FORCE_PATH_STYLE` uses the same helper (it was
  already strict).
- **Accepted exception:** `AI_AGENTS_ENABLED` stays loose on purpose: any value other than `true` is off. That is the safe
  side, and the variable is never a boot refusal (2026-10-22 crash-loop lesson).
- **Residual:** a typo now costs availability (a crash loop) instead of a silent posture change. Mitigated by the gate lint
  and the release note `packages/rab-docker/docs/release/RELEASE-NOTE-X3.1-STRICT-BOOLEANS.md`. A value set outside the
  committed compose files and env templates (a platform setting, a hand-edited server file) is checked only at boot.
- **Tests:** `env.validation.strict-booleans.spec.ts` (per flag: unset and empty keep the default, `true` and `false` are
  accepted, 15 typos each refuse to boot; no value echoed; S3 on the helper; `AI_AGENTS_ENABLED` stays loose);
  `compose-owner-login.test.cjs` (X3.1 env-file lint and per-service check; the two pins of the old transform now pin
  `strictBoolean`).

## X3.5-S6 — the Jest routing carries PG_DATABASE_URL only; legacy names warn under test (branch phase-x/x35-legacy-names-r1, PR #176, 2026-11-16, not merged)
- **Asset:** the disposable test cluster's superuser URL, and the guarantee that test and CI runs never resolve a connection
  through a deprecated name before release 2 refuses them.
- **Change (release 1):** setupFiles set PG_DATABASE_URL to the validated TEST application URL and blank DATABASE_URL /
  DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED / DB_POOL_MAX (a DB_POOL_MAX value carries over to PG_POOL_MAX_CONNECTIONS when that is unset), so the
  superuser URL no longer rides in the elevated legacy name and the factory resolves no elevated endpoint under Jest; the admin
  connection comes only from the validated pair. The Worker-login switch writes PG_DATABASE_URL. pg-config's deprecation
  warnings print under NODE_ENV=test too, and both Jest globalSetups refuse a routed environment (including what a later
  `.env` load would add) that still holds a legacy name; release 1 refuses nothing that was accepted before.
  `PG_LEGACY_NAMES_STRICT=true` (opt-in, set in CI on ci-security's check-rls step and ci-migration-security's two harness
  steps) refuses every legacy name outside production. Spawned runtime children drop the guard-written PG_DATABASE_URL and get
  their URL explicitly. `assertDirectLockUrl` (DBR-07) removed; the factory's documented-pooler denylist is the one rule.
- **Unchanged:** every X1.8 / X1.9 guard rule, every production and runtime refusal of the legacy names.
- **Abuse cases:** `test-database-guard.spec.ts` (X3.5-S6 and review #176 cases), `pg-config.spec.ts` (strict switch, warnings
  under test), `integration-test-database-gate.spec.ts` (no spec reads the blanked DATABASE_URL), `runtime-child-env.spec.ts`.
- **Release 2 (S8):** the fallbacks are removed and the legacy names refused everywhere; the strip lists keep every name.

## CI gate — exact owner-approved growth for the import-boundary ratchet (branch ci/import-boundaries-approved-growth, 2026-11-17; owner approval 2026-11-17 for PR #204; approvals read from the base ref since branch ci/import-boundaries-approvals-from-base, 2026-11-17)
- **Threat:** the import-boundary ratchet (`tools/check-import-boundaries.cjs`, PR #191) is a CI security gate: its `--base`
  step refuses any growth of `tools/import-boundaries.baseline.json` against the PR's base branch, so a new Worker import of
  rab-server internals (or engine -> modules, feature -> feature) cannot land unnoticed. It had no way to record an owner
  approval, so an approved change could only pass by weakening the gate, bypassing it, or deleting the step. Any approval
  mechanism is itself a way to widen the gate: a broad pattern, an open-ended count, a forgotten approval or an approval
  written by the PR that uses it would let PRs add violations silently.
- **Control:** approvals are data in `tools/import-boundaries.approved.json` (`{ "approved": [...] }`; until the follow-up
  branch they were the `APPROVED_GROWTH` constant in the check). Each entry names one rule, one file, the exact base count
  `from` (0 = no entry at the base), the exact head count `to`, an `approved: "owner YYYY-MM-DD"` date, a reason and an
  optional `target` (the resolved import target as `--list` prints it). `validateApprovedGrowth` refuses a malformed,
  undated, duplicate or non-growing entry, a `file` the check does not scan, and a `target` that is not an edge of that rule
  from that file (fail closed). `compareToBase` accepts a growth only when rule and file match exactly, the base count
  equals `from` and the head count equals `to`; one more edge, another file, another rule, or a different base count still
  fails. An entry whose `from` no longer equals the base count is reported STALE and fails `--base` while the head still
  lists it (by rule and file), so the entry must be deleted once the growth has merged and cannot be reused. Deleting it is
  never blocked: a PR whose approvals file no longer lists a stale base entry is not failed for it (review of #225, F1:
  before this, the stale loop read only the base list, so every PR failed, including the one deleting the entry, and the
  using PR could not delete it either because that tripped CHANGED TOGETHER: a deadlock of a required gate). Growth is
  still accepted only through the base list, so deleting an entry in the head can clear a hygiene failure but can never
  accept a growth.
  - **Approvals come from the base ref.** `--base` reads the approvals file with `git show <base>:tools/import-boundaries.approved.json`
    (the same fail-closed reader as the base baseline: an unknown ref, a shallow clone or any git failure throws; only "path
    does not exist in <ref>" means no approvals) and validates it the same way. An entry added in the head is never used by
    the PR that adds it: an approval has to be merged to the base branch, in its own PR, before any PR can use it. The head
    copy is still validated, so a malformed file fails in the PR that introduces it.
  - **Not in the same diff.** `--base` fails (CHANGED TOGETHER) when the diff from the merge-base with the base ref to the
    checkout changes the approvals file together with any `tools/*.baseline.json` (this ratchet's or another's). The one
    exception is the using PR consuming its own approval: when the head approvals document is exactly the base document
    minus the entries this PR uses (deep equality: same `_comment`, the remaining entries unchanged and in order), `--base`
    prints CONSUMED instead. Editing, adding or removing any other entry, or the comment, still fails CHANGED TOGETHER.
    So the using PR deletes its entry in the same PR and no cleanup PR or red window is needed.
  - **Base without a baseline.** When the base ref is `main` (`origin/main`, `refs/heads/main`, `refs/remotes/origin/main`)
    and it has no `tools/import-boundaries.baseline.json`, `--base` fails closed (exit 1): main has had the baseline since
    #191, so its absence means a broken checkout. Any other base without one is still "nothing to compare".
  - **Base-branch change reruns the gate.** `ci-security.yaml` triggers on `pull_request` types `opened, synchronize,
    reopened, edited`; `edited` covers a changed base branch, so a `--base` result computed against the old base does not
    stand. (It also reruns on a title or body edit; the concurrency group cancels the older run.)
  - **Target.** With a `target`, `--base` requires the head file to have at least `to - from` more edges of that rule to
    `target` than the file at the base ref (WRONG TARGET otherwise), so a different import in the same file cannot fill the
    slot, even when the file already imported the target at the base. The tree check (no base available) requires, while
    the file's count is above `from`, at least one edge of that rule from the file to `target` (TARGET MISSING).
  - git runs with `LC_ALL=C` and without `LANGUAGE`, so the "does not exist in" match does not depend on the runner's
    locale. `--base` accepts a plain ref name plus `~N` / `^N` ancestry suffixes only (no `@{...}`, `^{...}`, `:`, ranges,
    leading `^` or `-`); git runs without a shell.
  - The first two entries were the owner-approved (2026-11-17) Worker imports for PR #204: `push-dispatch.job.ts` 1 -> 2
    (`audit-events/audit-event-shipping`) and `push-send.processor.ts` 10 -> 11 (`audit/audit.service`), the same imports
    the email path already uses. Both were deleted by the cleanup PR (branch ci/import-boundaries-approved-growth-cleanup,
    #215), which merged straight after #204; the shipped list is empty.
- **Residual (accepted):**
  - Self-approval through the data list is now mechanically blocked: the using PR cannot add or edit its own approval.
    Editing the TOOL is not: CI runs the PR's own copy of `check-import-boundaries.cjs` and `ci-security.yaml`, so a PR that
    changes the check (for example to read approvals from the head again, or to drop the CHANGED TOGETHER rule) can pass
    its own gate. Changes to the tool and the workflow remain a review control (the owner's PR review; the repository has
    no CODEOWNERS file today), not a mechanical one.
  - The approval PR itself is reviewed like any PR: only the date format is validated, not who approved it. Two PRs from the
    same author (approval first, use second) both go through review.
  - A slot closes only when the base COUNT for that rule and file changes, not when the PR it was approved for merges or is
    closed: while the base still equals `from`, any PR may use the slot, and if the base later returns to `from` a forgotten
    entry would match once more. That is why a stale entry fails `--base` and must be deleted. A push to main never runs
    `--base` (the step is `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'`), so a stale entry is caught only on the next pull
    request. If a using PR merges without deleting its entry (CONSUMED is allowed, not required), every later PR that still
    lists the entry fails STALE until one of them deletes it; any PR may delete it, so this is a hygiene failure that the
    next PR clears, not an outage.
  - `target` is optional. Without it, counts are per file, not per edge, and an approved `to` could be met by a different
    import in that file; the reviewer checks the actual import (`--list`). The tree check's target rule is presence only;
    the exact count of new edges to the target is enforced by `--base`.
  - The CHANGED TOGETHER diff covers committed and uncommitted changes to tracked files; an untracked file is not in it
    (irrelevant in CI, where the checkout is a commit). `--write-baseline` still refuses any growth; the baseline is raised
    by hand in the using PR.
- **Tests:** `check-import-boundaries.test.cjs`: an approved exact growth passes; the same file one above `to` fails; an
  unlisted file growing fails; the same file under a different rule fails; a base count other than `from` fails and the
  approval is reported stale (also once the growth has merged); a consumed entry (base already at `to`) is stale, and the
  same entry matches again once the base returns to `from`, which is why stale must fail; partial use (from 10, to 12,
  head 11) fails as grown; `from: 0` matches a file absent at the base; malformed, undated, duplicate, non-growing,
  unscanned-file and wrong-target entries and malformed approval documents are refused; the shipped approvals file is
  valid and frozen. End to end in a throwaway git repository (`main(argv, { root })`): an approval present only in the
  head does not let the growth through (GROWN, exit 1), the same approval present on the base does (exit 0); an
  approval-only PR passes and its entry is not in force; approvals file plus a baseline in one diff fails (committed or
  uncommitted) even when the base approval matches; an approved count reached through a different import fails in
  `--base` (WRONG TARGET) and in the tree check (TARGET MISSING); a file that already imported the target at the base cannot
  fill the slot with another import (`--base`); the tree check exits 1 when the baseline file is missing. Review of #225:
  a branch that deletes a consumed approval (base count already at `to`) exits 0, an unrelated branch that still lists it
  exits 1 STALE; the using PR that deletes exactly its own used entry exits 0 (CONSUMED), and the same PR that also edits,
  adds or removes another entry, keeps and edits its own, or edits `_comment` fails CHANGED TOGETHER; a stale entry is
  reported only while the head lists it, and an approval only in the head never accepts a growth; `--base main` without a
  baseline exits 1 while another base without one is "nothing to compare"; the `ci-security.yaml` `pull_request` trigger
  lists `opened, synchronize, reopened, edited`. `--base` refs:
  `~N` / `^N` suffixes accepted, every other revision syntax refused, a step past the root commit throws. git's
  environment is `LC_ALL=C` without `LANGUAGE`, and a German locale in the caller still reads a missing path as absent.

## S-W1 — the Worker's member-invitation pre-send check also requires an active workspace (branch fix/s-w1-invitation-workspace-active, 2026-11-16)
- **Finding (Low, `docs/plans/untangle/worker.md` §4):** a manager invites a member; the workspace is then suspended or
  archived while the invitation email is still queued. The Worker's pre-send revalidation
  (`email-send.processor.ts` `revalidateMemberInvitation`) was a hand-copied subset of the server's liveness rule
  (`MemberInvitationService.loadLive`) and had lost the `manager_workspace.status = 'active'` condition, so the email was
  still delivered — disclosing the workspace's name and existence to the invitee after the workspace was closed.
  Acceptance was already refused by `loadLive`, so there was no access gain.
- **Control:** one rule, called by both. `modules/membership/utils/member-invitation-liveness.ts` exports
  `memberInvitationExpiredSql` (the `expires_at <= now()` boundary, database time), `memberInvitationStateFailure`
  (accepted / revoked / superseded / expired) and `memberInvitationParentFailure` (organisation not suspended, workspace
  exists and is `active`). `loadLive` (resolve, accept, accept-with-provider) and the Worker's pre-send check both decide
  with them, so "may this email be sent?" and "may this link be accepted?" can no longer drift. Fail closed: a workspace or
  organisation row the check cannot see (missing, or hidden by RLS), a null workspace id, or an invitation row whose
  expiry was not computed all count as not live. The workspace row is visible to the Worker only through
  `manager_workspace_member` (`id = current_workspace()`; the Worker binds the row's own workspace for this check only);
  the owner, platform-admin and MANAGE_IN_ORG branches of `manager_workspace_write` are false for the user-less Worker.
  `memberInvitationExpiredSql(alias)` throws unless the alias is a plain identifier (`/^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$/`), so it can
  never splice arbitrary text into SQL.
- **Kept unchanged:** every existing Worker check (invitation exists, same workspace as enqueued, not accepted / revoked /
  superseded / expired, latest email for the invitation, organisation not suspended) with the same reason texts and order;
  a not-live invitation's outbox row is settled the same way as before — CANCELLED (terminal, fenced by the claim token)
  with a sanitized reason, no provider call. New reason: `The workspace is no longer active.`. Token matching, the row lock
  and the inviter re-checks in acceptance are untouched. No schema, RLS or grant change.
- **Residual:** an email already handed to the provider before the workspace was closed cannot be recalled; accepting it
  is still refused server-side.
- **Tests:** rab-worker `member-invitation-delivery.integration.spec` W10 (suspended and archived workspace: no provider
  call, row CANCELLED with the workspace reason, a retried job sends nothing) and W11 (same setup, workspace active:
  delivered once); W1–W9 unchanged. rab-server `member-invitation-liveness.spec` (the shared decision table, including the
  fail-closed cases and the alias refusal) and `member-invitation.integration.spec` X3b (workspace archived after sending:
  resolve and accept both get the generic 400, no account is created, the invitation is not superseded).

## O-2 — CLI pre-auth reads and the platform_admin grant on the owner login under M-T1 FORCE RLS (branch fix/o2-cli-force-rls, 2026-11-16; PR #183; no new SQL)

- **Asset:** platform-wide administrator authority (`core.platform_admin`); every tenant's `core."user"` /
  `core.organisation` / `core.manager_workspace` rows; the legacy-file link columns.
- **Defect fixed (availability, not a leak):** since M-T1 these tables are FORCE'd with an owner-only definer policy. The CLI
  login `crewflow_owner` acting as itself sees zero rows with no tenant context, so `grant-platform-admin` answered "No active
  user found" for every real user (the documented recovery path when every admin is revoked was dead), `seed` failed on the
  organisation insert, and `storage:migrate-local` discovered nothing and exited 0. Proved live on a disposable database
  (`cli-owner-login-force-rls.integration.spec.ts`, failing before the fix).
- **Control now:** `command/ops/secure-owner-acting.ts` `withSecureOwner(manager, fn)` narrows the caller's open transaction
  with `SET LOCAL ROLE rab_secure_owner` (a frozen literal) for `fn` only, after checking: the process declared the `cli` role,
  a transaction is open, the session is the owner login acting as itself, not SUPERUSER/BYPASSRLS, and may SET the role; it
  checks `current_user` (and READ ONLY when asked) after narrowing and `RESET ROLE` (checked) after `fn` resolves. Lookups
  run in a READ ONLY transaction. The only writes made as the owner are the `platform_admin` grant row and seed's
  organisation; the session reset (CF-07) and the audit entries run as the login with tenant context. Every grant path is
  audited (`via: bootstrap_cli` / `via: seed`, actor NULL). This is the step `preauth-force-sql.ts` prescribes for operator
  scripts and what the three ops commands already do.
- **Barrier (the login is NOT it):** the API and the Worker connect with the same `crewflow_owner` login, so what keeps this
  off a request path is (1) the process-role check — only `command/main.ts` declares `cli`, and the step refuses `api` /
  `worker` / any other role (unit + live tests), and (2) a static test (`secure-owner-acting.spec.ts`) that fails when anything
  outside `src/command/**` imports the helper. Neither stops injected SQL (G-02, unchanged).
- **Threats:** *role left on a connection* — `SET LOCAL` ends with the transaction and the step resets explicitly; proved on
  ONE held connection (no pool checkout in between), with a negative control showing that probe does see a session-level role
  that survives COMMIT (`secure-owner-acting.integration.spec.ts`). *Wrong person granted* — unchanged: soft-deleted users
  excluded, an ambiguous email refuses, a non-matching `--org` refuses (abuse cases on the real login). *False migration
  record* — `storage:migrate-local --apply` link / clear UPDATEs are conditional (`... AND <col> IS NULL RETURNING id`) and
  must change exactly one row, otherwise the stored_file registration and the `file.migration_completed` audit roll back and
  the outcome is `failed` (unit-tested); `manager_workspace` logos are reported `unsupported` (exit 1 under `--apply`) and never
  touched, so no person's id is ever bound into `rab.user_id` to satisfy that table's write policy.
- **Residual:** `bootstrap-admin` exits 0 on `REFUSED_AMBIGUOUS_*` (proved live; owner item O-8, unchanged). The `--apply`
  happy path against real S3 was not run (no S3 in the disposable run); `manager_workspace` legacy logos stay unmigrated
  until a reviewed path exists. `seed` keeps no production target refusal (owner decision X1.3).

## SF-1 — bulk-email message is HTML-escaped (branch fix/sf1-bulk-email-escape, 2026-11-16)
- **Threat:** a manager or venue manager with bulk email (`POST /rest/v1/staff/bulk-email`, `POST /rest/v1/managers/bulk-email`,
  and the venue-manager route, which delegates to the manager one) typed raw HTML into the message. `ManagerService.bulkEmail`
  and `StaffService.bulkEmail` each built `` html: `<p>${dto.message}</p>` `` unescaped, so the HTML part sent under the
  organisation's identity could carry phishing links, fake buttons, tracking pixels or attribute injection. `BulkEmailDto.message`
  is only `@IsString @MaxLength(5000)`. (Mail clients do not run `<script>`, but links and images are the real harm.)
- **Control:** one renderer, `renderBulkNotificationEmail` in `engine/core-modules/email/templates.ts`, used by both services.
  It escapes the message with the canonical `engine/utils/escape-html.ts` helper (the five HTML-significant characters) and only
  then turns line breaks into `<br>`. The plain-text part stays the message as typed. `templates.ts`'s private copy of the
  escaper is replaced by the canonical import (same five characters, same output). Recipient scope, the outbox path and the
  audit row are unchanged.
- **Permission (owner decision batch 13, 2026-11-16):** sending a bulk email is an edit-level action, not a view.
  `POST /staff/bulk-email` now needs `staff.edit` (was `staff.view`) on the route guard, re-checked first in
  `StaffService.bulkEmail`. There is no `manager.edit` flag: `manager.manage` (the only manager flag, already the
  `ManagerController` class guard) is now also re-checked in `ManagerService.bulkEmail`; the Venue Manager route keeps its
  own `venue_manager.create` (class guard, re-checked in `VenueManagerService.bulkEmail` and again in
  `ManagerService.bulkEmail`, which accepts only those two flags and fails closed on anything else). 403 before any id is
  read; nothing is queued. The default `venue_manager` role holds `staff.view` but not `staff.edit`; it had no staff to
  email anyway (staff recipients are the caller's own creations).
- **Residual (accepted):** escaping removes markup, not text. A plain URL typed in the message is still shown as text, and
  many mail clients auto-link it. Acceptable for a message from a trusted, authenticated sender with an edit permission.
- **Tests:** `templates.spec.ts` (`<script>`, `<a href>`, `" onmouseover=` and `&`/`'` come out entity-escaped; line breaks
  become `<br>` only after escaping; text part unchanged) and `bulk-email-abuse-cases.integration.spec.ts` (the same hostile
  message is stored escaped in `email_outbox.rendered_html` for both the staff and the manager route; a role with
  `staff.view` but not `staff.edit`, and one without `manager.manage`, get 403 and nothing is queued).

## SF-2 (part 1 of 3) — staff, manager and venue-manager services re-check the route's flag (branch fix/sf2-service-perm-staff-manager, 2026-11-17)
- **Threat:** a job, CLI command, AI tool or another service calls a StaffService / ManagerService / VenueManagerService
  method directly. Those callers never pass a `PermissionGuard`, and these methods checked only scope or ownership, so a
  caller without the route's flag could read the staff or manager directory, create, edit, suspend or reactivate an
  account, reset a password, resend / correct / cancel an invitation, change an email, assign or unassign a venue, or delete
  a Venue Manager (CLAUDE.md layer 2; `docs/plans/untangle/server-modules.md` M3, finding SF-2, Medium).
- **Control:** one shared assert, `PermissionsService.assertPermissionTx(manager, ctx, flag)` (over `userHasPermissionTx`:
  overrides win over roles, memoised per transaction), called FIRST inside the method's own tenant transaction, so it is a
  403 for any id before a row is read (no existence oracle). Out-of-scope records keep their 404s. The flag is the one the
  route guard already holds, so the HTTP path is unchanged.
  - StaffService: `list`, `get`, `getTimeline`, `listNotes`, `listEmails` (`staff.view`); `create` (`staff.create`);
    `update`, `uploadAvatar`, `removeAvatar`, `changeEmail` incl. the direct INVITED path (`staff.edit`); `deactivate`,
    `reactivate` (`staff.deactivate`); `resetPassword`, `resendInvite`, `changePendingEmail`, `cancelInvite`
    (`user.reset_password`). `venueDirectory`, `venueTeamMember`, `setVenueTeamTags` keep `staff.view` but now check it
    inside their transaction instead of in a separate one.
  - ManagerService: `get`, `list`, `create`, `assignVenue`, `unassignVenue` (`manager.manage`). `update`, `setActive`,
    `resetPassword`, `changePendingEmail`, `changeEmail`, `getTimeline`, `listNotes`, `listEmails` take the caller's route
    flag (`manager.manage` by default; `venue_manager.create` from `VenueManagerService`), the pattern `addNote` and
    `bulkEmail` already use, and fail closed on any other flag. `resetPassword` and `changePendingEmail` also re-check the
    route's `user.reset_password`. `deleteVenueManagerUser` re-checks `venue_manager.create` in its own transaction (the
    implicit "caller checked first, in another transaction" rule is gone).
  - VenueManagerService: `createInOwnWorkspace` (`venue_manager.create`, in the creating transaction); `resendInvite` and
    `cancelInvite` also re-check `user.reset_password`.
  - `ManagerService.getWithin` (no check; caller authorises, caller's transaction) serves the Admin Panel's
    `OrganisationOnboardingService.getOrganisation`, which is authorised by its platform-admin re-check: a platform admin
    holds no role in the organisation it inspects. Same result as before.
- **Behaviour change:** saving a navigation shortcut to a Staff record now also needs `staff.view` (`StaffService.get`), the
  same flag the record's own route needs.
- **Not changed (owner decision pending):** `ManagerService.resendInvite` and `ManagerService.cancelInvite` have no flag
  re-check. The platform-admin CEO resend / revoke (`OrganisationOnboardingService.resendCeoInvite` / `revokeCeoInvite`)
  calls them with a context that holds no role in the target organisation, so a plain `manager.manage` re-check would break
  them; they need an explicit, audited authority path first. Their `/managers` routes stay guarded by `manager.manage` +
  `user.reset_password`; the Venue Manager route re-checks both in `VenueManagerService`.
- **Tests:** `sf2-layer2-staff-manager.integration.spec.ts` (each method called directly with the flag revoked by a per-user
  override: ForbiddenException, and the organisation's audit log, outbox, invites, files, accounts, staff profiles and venue
  links are unchanged; step-up-gated methods use a real signed-in session so only the flag refuses; positive controls with
  the flag; wrong-route-flag and fail-closed cases; the platform-admin `getOrganisation` read still works; HTTP 403/200
  unchanged). `permissions.service.spec.ts` covers the helper.

## SF-3 — create-and-send uses the normal shift-creation checks and audit (branch fix/sf3-create-shift-and-send-scope, 2026-11-16)
- **Threat:** a manager with `offer.send` → `POST /rest/v1/shifts/with-offers` (`OfferService.createShiftAndSend`) with the id
  of a job role that is RLS-visible but not theirs, or an archived venue or job role → a shift (OPEN, then OFFERED) and live
  offers were created anyway, with no `shift.created` audit row. It was a second shift-creation path that checked only the
  venue scope (`assertVenueAccessibleTx`) and skipped `SchedulingService.resolveDraftTargetsTx` (job-role scope, both
  archive checks), unlike `POST /rest/v1/shifts`. The job role also selects the snapshotted pay rate (venue role rate or the
  role's default), so a foreign role could price the shift.
- **Control:** one insert, `SchedulingService.insertNewShiftTx`, used by `createDraftTx` (DRAFT) and `createShiftAndSend`
  (OPEN): venue + job-role scope (`assertVenueAccessibleTx` + `assertJobRoleOwned`, 404 out of scope, never 403) → archived
  venue (409 `VENUE_ARCHIVED`) or job role (409 `JOB_ROLE_ARCHIVED`) refused → `resolvePayRate` snapshot → INSERT
  (workspace from the venue) → `shift.created` audit (status + requiredCount, no pay) in the same transaction. Only DRAFT or
  OPEN may be the initial status. Any refusal rolls back the whole transaction (no shift, no offer). Venue and job-role
  rules, rate resolution and the per-recipient send are unchanged.
- **Permission (owner decision batch 13, 2026-11-16):** create-and-send creates a shift, so it now needs `schedule.create`
  as well as `offer.send`, like `POST /shifts`. Both flags are on the route guard (`PermissionGuard` × 2) and both are
  re-checked in `createShiftAndSend` first (layer 2; 403 before any referenced id is read). Every default role that holds
  `offer.send` also holds `schedule.create`, so only a custom role with `offer.send` alone loses the action.
- **Tests:** `scheduling-offer-abuse-cases.integration.spec.ts` › "SF-3": a same-workspace job role created by someone else
  → 404 "Job role not found." with no shift and no offer (and `POST /shifts` gives the same 404); a role with `offer.send`
  but not `schedule.create` → 403, no shift; archived job role → 409 `JOB_ROLE_ARCHIVED`
  and archived venue → 409 `VENUE_ARCHIVED`, no shift; a successful create-and-send writes exactly one `shift.created`
  row (actor = caller, status `open`, no pay keys).

## SF-2 (part 2 of 3) — offer, replacement-request, scheduling and attendance services re-check the route's flag (branch fix/sf2-service-perm-offer-scheduling-attendance, 2026-11-17)
- **Threat:** a job, CLI command, AI tool or another service calls an OfferService / ReplacementRequestService /
  SchedulingService / AttendanceService method directly, so no `PermissionGuard` runs. These methods checked only scope
  or ownership: a caller without the flag could send, withdraw, confirm or reject offers, approve or decline shift
  requests, change requested staff, cancel shifts, create job roles, read the organisation-wide request lists, or clock in
  and out (CLAUDE.md layer 2; `docs/plans/untangle/server-modules.md` M3, finding SF-2, Medium). `listVenueOffers` and
  `listPendingApprovals` matter most: they widen past the caller's own shifts. `ReplacementRequestService.approve` sends an
  offer through `OfferService.sendOneWithManager`, whose contract leaves authorisation to the caller, and it checked none.
- **Control:** the shared `PermissionsService.assertPermissionTx` (part 1) or SchedulingService's existing `assertFlagTx`
  (same `userHasPermissionTx`), called FIRST inside the method's own tenant transaction: 403 for any id before a row is read
  or locked. Scope 404s and 409 transitions are unchanged; the flag is the route guard's, so HTTP is unchanged.
  - OfferService: `list`, `getBatch` (`schedule.view`); `listMine`, `staffAccept`, `decline` (`offer.respond`); `send`,
    `sendBulk` (`offer.send`; the replacement mode already re-checked it); `withdraw` (`offer.withdraw`); `managerConfirm`,
    `confirmAll`, `managerReject` (`offer.confirm`); `approveShiftRequest` (`staffing_request.approve`). A refused accept or
    confirm never reaches the lazy expiry / deadline-withdrawal transactions.
  - ReplacementRequestService: `list`, `get` (`schedule.view`); `approve`, `reject` (`offer.send`).
  - SchedulingService: `list`, `get`, `listJobRoles`, `getRequestedStaff` (`schedule.view`); `createJobRole`, `cancel`
    (`schedule.create`); `listVenueOffers`, `listPendingApprovals`, `declineRequest`, `addRequestedStaff`,
    `removeRequestedStaff` (`staffing_request.approve`).
  - AttendanceService: `checkIn`, `getCheckIn`, `clockIn`, `clockOut`, `autoClockOutOnGeofenceExit`, `getActive`,
    `getHistory`, `getForShift` (`attendance.clock`); `list` (`attendance.view`).
- **Behaviour change:** saving a navigation shortcut to a Shift, and the shift / offer timelines, now need `schedule.view` in
  `SchedulingService.get` too (the same flag their routes already require).
- **Not changed (owner items):** `cancel` stays on `schedule.create` (permission-matrix question open); no business rule,
  transition or seat logic changed.
- **Tests:** `sf2-layer2-offer-scheduling-attendance.integration.spec.ts` (each method called directly with the flag revoked
  by a per-user override, on real records — a pending and an accepted offer, an open shift, a pending shift request — and
  on unknown ids: ForbiddenException, and the organisation's audit log, notifications, realtime events, shifts, seats,
  offers, attendance, requested staff and replacement requests are unchanged; positive controls with the flag; HTTP 403/200
  unchanged).

## SF-4 — venue pay-rate creation checks job-role scope (branch fix/sf4-role-rate-job-role-scope, 2026-11-16)
- **Threat:** a manager with `venue.edit` → `POST /rest/v1/venues/:id/role-rates` with the id of a job role that RLS shows
  them (same organisation and workspace) but that is not theirs → a `venue_role_rate` row was written for it.
  `VenueService.createRoleRate` checked the venue scope and only that the role existed. That rate is what
  `SchedulingService.resolvePayRate` snapshots for new shifts at that venue and role, so it is payroll input.
- **Control:** one predicate, `isJobRoleInScope` (`modules/scheduling/utils/job-role-scope.ts`), the rule shift creation
  (`SchedulingService.assertJobRoleOwned`) and staff creation (`StaffService.assertJobRoleAccessible`) already applied, now
  used by all three (the two existing copies call it; behaviour unchanged). `createRoleRate` refuses an out-of-scope role
  with 404 "Job role not found." (never 403), before any write. A Venue Manager keeps the existing reference rule (any job
  role RLS shows them); an ordinary manager may use only a role they created. Layer 2: `createRoleRate`,
  `updateRoleRate` and `deleteRoleRate` now re-check the route's own `venue.edit` flag in the service (403, before any id
  is read). Rate values, defaults, effective dates and rate resolution are unchanged.
- **Not changed (flagged for the owner):** an archived job role is still accepted for a new venue rate (shift and staff
  creation refuse archived roles with 409; whether a pay rate counts as "new work" is a payroll decision). `updateRoleRate` still merges its DTO into the entity (the DTO has no `jobRoleId`, and
  `forbidNonWhitelisted` rejects extra fields, so it cannot re-point a rate at another role).
- **Audit (owner decision batch 13, 2026-11-16):** `createRoleRate`, `updateRoleRate` and `deleteRoleRate` each write one
  audit row in the same transaction — `venue_role_rate.created` / `.updated` / `.deleted`, `entityType` `venue_role_rate`,
  metadata exactly `{ venueId, jobRoleId, effectiveFrom, effectiveTo }` (after the change; before it, for a delete) — never
  a pay, charge or overtime amount. The three actions are classified NOT shipped off-host (business events, like
  `venue.photo_updated`) in `security-audit-event-catalogue.ts`; shipping them is a separate decision.
- **Tests:** `venue-jobrole-ownership-abuse-cases.integration.spec.ts` › "SF-4": an RLS-visible job role created by
  another manager, and another workspace's job role → 404 with no `venue_role_rate` row; the caller's own role → 201 with
  the values as sent; create, update and delete each write exactly one audit row with exactly those four metadata keys.

## SF-2 (part 3 of 3) — venue, shift-report and workspace-settings services re-check the route's flag (branch fix/sf2-service-perm-venue-reports-workspace, 2026-11-17)
- **Threat:** a job, CLI command, AI tool or another service calls a VenueService / ShiftReportService / WorkspaceService
  method directly, so no `PermissionGuard` runs. These checked only scope: a caller without the flag could create or edit
  a venue (including its geofence), read a venue's pay and charge rates, read or list shift reports, finalise a report
  (which triggers the worker PDF and email), or read the organisation's settings and sign-in methods (CLAUDE.md layer 2;
  `docs/plans/untangle/server-modules.md` M3, finding SF-2, Medium).
- **Control:** the shared `PermissionsService.assertPermissionTx` (part 1), or VenueService's existing
  `assertCanViewVenueTx` / `assertCanEditVenueTx` (same `userHasPermissionTx`), called FIRST inside the method's own
  tenant transaction: 403 for any id before a row is read or the finalise lock is taken. Scope 404s and transitions are
  unchanged; the flag is the route guard's, so HTTP is unchanged.
  - VenueService: `create` (`venue.create`); `update` (`venue.edit`); `listRoleRates` (`venue.view`). The role-rate writes
    already re-checked `venue.edit` (SF-4).
  - ShiftReportService: `listReports` (`report.view`); `finalise` (`report.export`); `getReport` takes the caller's route
    flag — `report.view` by default, `report.export` for the report the finalise route returns (that route is guarded by
    `report.export` alone, so a finalised report is never followed by a 403) — and fails closed on any other flag.
    `getReportWithManager` stays check-free: it runs inside other authorised transactions (attendance review, on-behalf
    punches, the offer pipeline).
  - WorkspaceService: `get`, `getAuthProviders` (`settings.view`).
- **Tests:** `sf2-layer2-venue-reports-workspace.integration.spec.ts` (each method called directly with the flag revoked by
  a per-user override, on real records and unknown ids: ForbiddenException, and the organisation's audit log, outbox,
  organisation row, venues, venue pay rates, shifts and shift reports are unchanged; the finalise route's report read works
  under `report.export` alone; fail-closed flag; positive controls; HTTP 403/200 unchanged).

## Part C2 (C2-7) — every workspace business-table statement names its schema; the search_path trap is required (branch feat/hws-c2-7, PR #170, 2026-11-16; no SQL)
- **Threat:** a statement that names a workspace business table (`shift`, `attendance`, `staff_profile`, …) without a schema
  is resolved by the transaction's `search_path`. A binder slip, a reused manager or a later code change that leaves the
  wrong `search_path` bound would then read or write another schema's rows (another workspace's, or the legacy `core`
  copies) without any error.
- **Control:** every such statement is named through `businessTables(manager)` (C2-0). The schema comes only from a binder
  (the registry-resolved, canonical `workspace_<32 hex>` of the bound workspace, or `core`), never from input. A manager
  that no binder bound cannot run the statement at all (`BusinessTablesError('unbound')`, before any SQL). C2-7 qualifies the
  last five sites (`post-shift-lifecycle.service.ts`, `templates/document-context.ts`) and one dynamic table the static scan
  could not see (`role.service.ts assertRelationsInScopeTx`, now two literal statements). The ratchet
  (`tools/check-workspace-table-qualified.cjs`) has an empty baseline and fails on any non-empty one. The runtime trap
  (`CREWFLOW_TEST_SEARCH_PATH_TRAP`, test-only, refused outside `NODE_ENV=test`) binds `search_path = ''`, so any
  unqualified table fails with 42P01. Its CI jobs (`test-search-path-trap` (1)–(3) in ci-server, `test-search-path-trap` in
  ci-worker) are now required: `continue-on-error` is removed. The owner adds them to branch protection.
- **Residual:** production still binds `search_path` to the resolved schema (defence in depth, lenient). Owner decision
  still open: bind `''` in production too (strict). The static ratchet cannot see a table name assembled from a variable;
  the required trap jobs cover that at runtime for every path the suites exercise.
- **Tests:** `worker-operations-abuse-cases.integration.spec.ts` › post-shift lifecycle now runs on the real binder. A foreign
  workspace is refused by the binder (`WorkspaceRoutingError('registry-missing')`). The L3 shape (the row's own schema bound,
  the organisation GUC switched to another org) advances 0 rows. A bare transaction outside any binder gets
  `BusinessTablesError('unbound')` for `advance` and `discover`. `tenant-context.service.spec.ts` and
  `workspace-execution-context.integration.spec.ts` pin the trap behaviour (`''` bound, the real schema still handed to the
  callback). Every server and worker suite passes under the trap.

## SF-6 — global search uses each list's own scope, with an organisation pin (branch fix/sf6-search-scope, 2026-11-17; no SQL)
- **Threat:** an owner-scope manager → `GET /rest/v1/search` → names of staff, venues, shifts and offers that their own
  lists hide. `SearchService` keyed the owner scope on `workspace_id` alone (`created_by` only for restricted workspace
  members), while `StaffService.list()` / `VenueService.list()` read `created_by` = the scope owner, `SchedulingService.list()`
  reads `created_by` = the caller (or a pending-approval request) and `OfferService.list()` reads offers the caller sent.
  Nothing in the database makes `manager_profile.workspace_id` unique per manager, so two owner-scope managers sharing a
  workspace would find each other's records. A Venue Manager's staff search had no Venue Manager branch (every staff row in
  the workspace, not their team), and `searchManagers` had no organisation predicate (RLS only).
- **Control:** `search.service.ts` applies the list's own predicate per type, plus explicit `organisation_id` (all five
  types) and `workspace_id` (owner scope) pins on top of RLS: staff = `created_by` = scope owner, and for a Venue Manager
  `created_by` = caller OR their saved team at their assigned venues (active accounts), the union of `StaffService.list()`
  and `venueDirectory()`; venues = assigned venues, or `created_by` = scope owner; shifts = `applyShiftReadScope` as
  `list()` uses it (`created_by` = caller or `pending_manager_approval`; a workspace member: the owner's shifts and their
  record filter); offers = `offerReadScopeCondition` itself (imported, not copied); managers = organisation-wide, as
  `ManagerService.list()`. The custom-member record filters apply as before. Search can now only be tighter than a list.
  Permission checks, hidden-field rules, ranking and the archived exclusion are unchanged.
- **Tests:** `sf6-search-scope.integration.spec.ts`: a staff row, a venue, a shift and an offer in B's workspace whose
  `created_by` is A are hidden from B's search (each was found before the change) and from B's lists, and A does not find
  them either; a Venue Manager's direct `SearchService.search` returns their team member and not another staff member of
  the same workspace (who was found before), matching `venueDirectory`; another organisation's manager with the same name
  is never returned; no over-narrowing: an owner-scope manager still finds a Venue Manager's pending-approval request in
  their workspace (as `list()` shows it). `search-managers-org-pin.spec.ts` pins the managers' organisation predicate
  itself (RLS alone would hide another organisation's managers, so the integration case cannot tell the two layers apart).
  `dashboard-search.integration.spec.ts`'s two cross-workspace tests used to assert the old
  `workspace_id`-only search result; they now assert the row is hidden from both managers.

## SF-7 — explicit field maps instead of DTO spreads in staff and venue writes (branch fix/sf7-explicit-field-maps, 2026-11-17; no SQL)
- **Threat:** a direct (non-HTTP) caller of `StaffService.update`, `VenueService.create`, `VenueService.update` or
  `VenueService.updateRoleRate` (a job, a CLI command, an AI tool, another service) → passes an object carrying fields the
  DTO does not declare → they reached the row. `update()` spread the rest of the staff DTO into `staff_profile`
  (`staffRef`, `createdBy`, `employmentStatus`...), `create()` spread the venue DTO AFTER `organisationId` / `createdBy` /
  `workspaceId` (so the DTO could replace them), and the two `merge` calls copied the whole DTO (`status`, `createdBy`, a
  rate's `jobRoleId` / `venueId`). The global ValidationPipe's `forbidNonWhitelisted` rejects these for HTTP callers only.
- **Control:** `engine/utils/pick-fields.util.ts` `pickFields(dto, FIELDS)` copies only the named keys whose value is not
  `undefined` (`null` kept for clearing) into a new object. Each site has its own allow-list, typed
  `as const satisfies readonly (keyof Dto & keyof Entity)[]` (a field missing from the DTO or the entity is a compile
  error): `STAFF_PROFILE_UPDATE_FIELDS` (the 22 profile fields of `UpdateStaffDto`; first name, last name and phone still
  go to `core."user"` as before), `VENUE_WRITE_FIELDS` (the 16 fields both venue DTOs declare; `create()` now sets the
  tenant and owner columns after the mapped fields) and `ROLE_RATE_UPDATE_FIELDS` (pay, charge, overtime, effective
  dates). HTTP behaviour is unchanged: every declared field is still written. The staff `profile.updated` audit row now
  lists only fields that were actually written (an explicit `undefined` key is no longer listed).
- **Not changed:** `VenueManagerService` passes `{ ...dto, type }` / `{ ...dto, userIds }` to other service methods (not
  entity writes; those methods map their own fields).
- **Tests:** `pick-fields.util.spec.ts` (undeclared keys such as `organisationId`, `createdBy`, `status` are never
  copied; `undefined` skipped, `null` and falsy kept; own properties only; source not mutated) and
  `sf7-explicit-field-maps.integration.spec.ts`, one case per site, each a direct service call with undeclared fields:
  staff `staffRef` / `createdBy` / `employmentStatus` not written and the audit lists only `preferredName`; venue create
  `status` / `createdBy` / `archivedAt` not written, organisation, workspace and creator are the caller's; venue update
  `status` / `createdBy` not merged; role-rate update `jobRoleId` / `venueId` cannot re-point the rate. In each case the
  declared field in the same call is written.
  `venue-write-fields.spec.ts` and `staff-profile-update-fields.spec.ts` compare each allow-list with the DTO's
  class-validator metadata (minus the named `core."user"` fields for staff), so a new DTO field cannot be silently dropped.

## Users page: bulk Send Email is offered only with the server's permission (branch fix/users-bulk-email-permission, 2026-11-17; no SQL)
- **Context:** since owner decision batch 13 (SF-1) bulk email needs `staff.edit` for Staff and `manager.manage` for
  Managers (route guard and service re-check). The web Users page still offered Send Email to every Staff-tab caller and
  to every CEO / platform admin on the Managers tab, so a view-only role got a 403 toast. No data was exposed (the server
  refused), but the UI advertised an action the caller does not hold.
- **Control (presentation only):** `Users.tsx` reads the existing permission source, `GET /auth/capabilities`: Send Email
  appears for Staff only with `staff.edit`, for Managers only with `manager.manage` (and the CEO / platform-admin tab
  rule as before), for the caller's Venue Managers with `venue_manager.create` (unchanged). `staff.edit` is added to the
  capability hints the endpoint returns (`auth.controller.ts`), computed from the same resolved permission set as every
  other hint (overrides honoured). The server-side checks are unchanged and remain the enforcement.
- **Not changed:** the user detail panel's own Send Email (single recipient, same endpoint) and its other actions are not
  permission-gated in the UI either; the server still refuses them with 403. Separate follow-up.
- **Tests:** `Users.spec.tsx` › "bulk Send Email follows the server permission": `staff.view` without `staff.edit` → no
  Send Email in the bar (made after the capabilities have loaded); with `staff.edit` → offered and carries the selected id;
  a CEO without `manager.manage` → not offered, with it → offered. Both denial cases fail on the previous code.
  `sc05-capabilities.integration.spec.ts` now expects the 19 keys including `staff.edit`, same booleans as one
  `userHasPermission` per flag. The mocked e2e fixture (`crewflow-fixtures.ts`) grants `staff.edit` so the existing bar
  specs keep their four actions.

## PostgreSQL majors: one supported list (16-18), refused everywhere else; every process uses its server's fingerprints (branch fix/pg-majors-15-18, PR #227, 2026-11-17; no migration; a psql version guard in the two provider-admin scripts)
- **Context:** the 0.6.0 deploy checklist warned that on PostgreSQL 17 / 18 new workspaces could not be created. Cause:
  only the migrate child and the workspace command runner selected the workspace fingerprints of the server's major
  (`selectWorkspaceFingerprintMajor`). The API, the Worker and the CLI never did, so `workspaceFingerprintMajor()` stayed
  at its default, 16. On 17 / 18 the Worker's in-process provisioner (`provisionWorkspaceSchema` → `recordProvisioned`)
  compared every workspace it built with the PostgreSQL 16 structure-level-22 value and marked it FAILED; the daily drift
  job reported READY module 14-20 workspaces as DRIFTED (alert only). The server path (`core.provision_workspace`, its
  literal baked by the migrate child for the right major), the migrate child and the runner were already correct. It failed
  closed (no wrong structure was accepted), so this was an availability defect, not an exposure.
- **Second gap (fail-open on the upper bound):** db-setup and the API / Worker / CLI boot gate checked only `>= 16`. A
  PostgreSQL 19 server got `crewflow_owner` created by db-setup before the migrate child refused it, and outside production
  a process on 19 started with the PostgreSQL 16 fingerprints.
- **Control:** `database/postgres/supported-majors.ts` is the one list (16, 17, 18) and the one refusal sentence
  ("PostgreSQL N is not supported; use 16-18 (PostgreSQL 16, 17 or 18).") read by the db-setup bootstrap child (both
  modes, from the Q2 facts, before the probe, the pending password file and any write), the migrate child
  (`assertSupportedPostgresMajor`) and boot gate 2. After the gates pass, `runDatabaseBootGates` selects the server's
  fingerprints for the process; `provisionWorkspaceSchema`, the Worker drift cycle and the two workspace CLIs also select on
  their own session first. A second, different major in one process is refused (never a silent switch).
- **Security review of PR #227 (APPROVE, fixes applied):**
  - L1: the legacy migrate path (separated layout, `setup-db.ts`, not the owner login) used to warn and migrate on an
    unsupported major. `selectFingerprintsForRun` now refuses outside 16-18 on both paths before any migration; only the
    fingerprint-completeness check stays owner-login only.
  - L2: the provider-admin psql scripts (`01-crewflow-owner.sql`, `transition-from-separated.sql`) refuse any major outside
    16-18 before `CREATE ROLE` (`\gset` / `\if`, then `1 / 0` under ON_ERROR_STOP): nothing is created. The harnesses that
    replay only the scripts' `CREATE ROLE` / `GRANT` lines are unaffected, and no golden or fingerprint changes. The CI job
    `owner-login (15, unsupported)` runs both scripts under psql on PostgreSQL 15: non-zero exit, no crewflow_owner.
  - I3: `resetWorkspaceFingerprintSelectionForTests` throws outside NODE_ENV=test.
  - I4: a major mismatch in the Worker's drift or provisioning loop logs one explicit `ALERT …` error line and still fails the
    cycle (counted in workspaceSchemaDriftFailures / workspaceProvisioningFailures, shown on the admin queues page).
  - L3: ci-twenty-tests runs the provisioning, payroll-evidence and invite-cleanup integration specs on 16, 17 and 18.
  - Follow-ups, not in this PR: I2, an unselected read of EXPECTED_WORKSPACE_FINGERPRINTS should throw outside tests instead of
    defaulting to PostgreSQL 16 (today every entrypoint selects; the default is a remaining fail-closed fallback); the
    `core.worker_delete_expired_invited_user` `restrict_violation` handler (new migration, owner SQL review).
- **Not supported, and why:** PostgreSQL 15 and earlier. The owner-login bootstrap grants `WITH INHERIT …, SET …`, merged
  migrations call `pg_has_role(…, 'SET')` and refuse below 16 themselves, the boot gate reads `pg_auth_members.set_option`,
  and on 15 a CREATEROLE login can grant `pg_execute_server_program` (M0 F-E1). Merged migrations are never edited.
- **PostgreSQL 18 SQLSTATE change (found by the PG18 suite run):** PostgreSQL 18 reports a violated `RESTRICT` foreign key
  as `23001` (restrict_violation) instead of `23503` (release notes, "Migration to Version 18"). Crewflow's RESTRICT keys
  are the payroll-evidence keys and several `core."user"` references. On 18, `hardDeleteFallbackReason` treated that as a
  genuine error: deleting a user that payroll evidence still references failed instead of falling back to a soft delete
  (fail-closed: nothing was deleted). Fixed in code: `database/postgres/sqlstate.ts` `isForeignKeyRefusal` (23503 or
  23001) in the user-deletion fallback, the invite-cleanup retain reason and the AI-agent role-FK mapping. The definer
  `core.worker_delete_expired_invited_user` still catches only `foreign_key_violation`; on 18 its restrict_violation now
  reaches the Worker's handler, which retains the invitee (nothing deleted; audit reason `workspace_referenced:<constraint>`
  instead of `referenced`). Changing the function needs a new migration, new body hashes in the PG16/17/18 semantic
  goldens and owner SQL review: proposed as a follow-up, not in this PR.
- **Tests:** `supported-majors.spec.ts` (the list is 16-18; each listed major has every module and structure-level
  fingerprint, a semantic golden and a posture golden; 14, 15, 19, 20 refused with the range), `owner-bootstrap.spec.ts`
  (14, 15, 19, 20 and garbage refused in both modes; 14 and 19 end to end: no password stored, no BEGIN, no write),
  `database-boot-gate-rules.spec.ts` (14, 15, 19, 20 refused at gate `version`; 16.0, 16, 17, 18 pass), the
  `bootstrap-owner-login-check.ts` PG15 scenario and the deploy-order db-setup PG15 block (new refusal text). Live: the
  server and Worker suites on PostgreSQL 16, 17 and 18 and the db-setup child on 15-18 (InstaBox; results in the PR).

## CI audit — picomatch GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf: no fix exists anywhere, so a dev/build-only 30-day owner exception (branch fix/picomatch-ghsa-fc5q, PR #229, 2026-11-17; PROPOSAL: the owner's merge is the decision; merges after or with the node-gyp runtime prune PR)
- **Advisory:** GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf / CVE-2026-112366 (HIGH, CVSS 7.5): picomatch `<=4.0.7` compiles single-branch
  repeated extglobs (`+(*)`, `+(*a)`) into an exponentially backtracking regex. Failure: *whoever controls a glob
  PATTERN* → has picomatch compile it and match a short crafted string → blocks the Node event loop. For this
  repository: INFO while the conditions below hold. The required ci-security `audit` failed on every PR.
- **Why not the normal fix (Twenty's way: root `resolutions` documented in `"//resolutions"`):** there is nothing to
  resolve to. The advisory has no `first_patched_version`; the registry's whole list (1.0.0 … 4.0.7, no prereleases,
  dist-tag latest 4.0.7) is inside `<=4.0.7` in every major; the upstream fix micromatch/picomatch#194 is unmerged.
  No dependent can drop it either: the current release of every one still requires picomatch (@nx/js and
  @nx/workspace 24.0.6 `^4.0.7`, vite 8.3.8 `^4.0.7`, jest-util / jest-haste-map / jest-message-util 30.5.1 `^4.0.3`,
  tinyglobby 0.2.17 `^4.0.4`, anymatch 3.1.3 `^2.0.4`, micromatch 4.0.8 `^2.3.1`; node-gyp 13.1.0 via tinyglobby).
- **Paths (yarn.lock, 2.3.2 / 4.0.4 / 4.0.5):** PRODUCTION only through yarn's injected `node-gyp: latest`
  (node-gyp@13.0.1, an install-time native build tool, never imported at runtime). node-gyp has THREE production
  parents, each with an injected `node-gyp: npm:latest` edge: `argon2` directly (`@rab/server > argon2`),
  `node-addon-api` (`@rab/server > argon2 > node-addon-api`) and `msgpackr-extract` (`@rab/worker > bullmq > msgpackr >
  msgpackr-extract`). Below node-gyp there is exactly ONE picomatch chain: `node-gyp > tinyglobby > picomatch@4.0.5`.
  (Corrected on branch fix/npm-audit-register-severity, 2026-11-18: the text above previously listed only the argon2
  and msgpackr-extract parents.) Everything else is dev/build: root `@nx/jest`/`@nx/js` (4.0.4, 4.0.5), jest 29/30 via `@types/jest`,
  `jest-environment-jsdom`, `jest-haste-map > anymatch` (2.3.2, 4.0.5), rab-front `vite` (4.0.5), rab-server/worker
  `ts-node-dev > chokidar > anymatch/readdirp` (2.3.2). No first-party code imports a glob matcher; the rab-front
  production bundle contains no picomatch (built and grepped).
- **Control (`tools/check-npm-audit.cjs` + `tools/npm-audit-decisions.json`, schema 2):** same
  `yarn npm audit --severity high --all --recursive`; a finding passes only with an entry that is
  - *scoped:* exactly one GHSA id + one package (`package`, a `packages` list is refused), `accepted-risk` only;
    the entry also records the advisory `severity` it decided (`high` for this one, added on branch
    fix/npm-audit-register-severity; the check binds it from the follow-up hardening PR on: a finding rated above
    the recorded severity is not covered, so a re-scored advisory needs a new owner decision);
  - *owned and explained:* owner_decision_ref (issue/PR of this repo, no placeholder), decided_by, decided_on,
    `reason`, `drop_when`;
  - *time-boxed:* at most 30 days; expired / over-long / duplicate entries fail; no date override;
  - *lapsing on a fix:* fails as soon as the GitHub advisory has a `first_patched_version` or the registry has a
    release in ANY major outside the vulnerable range and newer than an installed version (prereleases are not fixes);
  - *dev/build only:* fails while the package is in the production closure = yarn.lock reachable from the
    `dependencies`/`optionalDependencies` of the shipped workspaces (the check-licences.mjs list), yarn-injected
    dependencies included, minus `RUNTIME_PRUNE` exported by `packages/rab-docker/rab/runtime-deps.cjs` (a pruned
    package and what is reachable only through it). No export = nothing excluded.
  Every other advisory fails as before. Fails closed on an unparseable audit, a failed registry or advisory lookup,
  an unresolvable lockfile descriptor or an unevaluable range.
- **Dependency on the prune PR:** on origin/main runtime-deps.cjs exports no `RUNTIME_PRUNE`, so this check FAILS on
  #229 today (picomatch@4.0.5 via node-gyp is in the production closure). The node-gyp prune PR must export
  `RUNTIME_PRUNE` (e.g. `['node-gyp']`), keep its CLI under `require.main === module`, and remove node-gyp's
  exclusive subtree (tinyglobby, picomatch@4.0.5) from the image. #229 merges after, or together with, that PR.
  Verified locally by patching that export in: the check passes (1 decided) and the real yarn.lock closure minus
  node-gyp contains no node-gyp, tinyglobby or picomatch.
- **Drop condition (also in the entry):** remove the entry and upgrade (`yarn up -R picomatch`, or a root
  `resolutions` override documented in `"//resolutions"`) as soon as a fixed picomatch exists in any major (the
  check fails on its own then); otherwise it expires 2026-12-17 and needs a new owner decision.

```
SECURITY TRADE-OFF
Decision:   The required ci-security audit passes with a known HIGH advisory (picomatch GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf) in the
            dev/build dependency tree, via one dated owner exception, for at most 30 days (to 2026-12-17).
Reason:     No fixed picomatch exists in any major and no dependent release drops it, so neither an upgrade nor a
            `resolutions` override is possible; keeping the audit red blocks every PR (security fixes included);
            disabling the audit, `npmAuditIgnoreAdvisories` or dropping `--recursive` would hide it with no expiry,
            no owner record and no production check. Replacing Nx, Jest and Vite is out of proportion.
Risk:       A developer/CI process that compiles an attacker-chosen glob pattern can be stalled (CPU DoS of a build or
            test, not of a deployed service). A pattern source would have to be repository config, i.e. someone who
            can already change CI. If prune and lockfile drift put picomatch back in the runtime closure, the check
            fails rather than hiding it.
Mitigation: One advisory + one package; 30-day expiry; lapses automatically on any fix; fails while the package is
            in the production closure (lockfile walk minus the image prune); every other advisory still fails;
            runtime-deps.cjs forbids the dev tools in the image.
Reversal:   Upgrade / `resolutions` override (documented in "//resolutions") as soon as a fix ships, then delete the
            entry; or replace the parent tools.
```
- **Tests:** `tools/check-npm-audit.test.cjs` (ci-security "The check's own tests", 9 tests): range evaluation incl.
  the advisory API's `<= 4.0.7` spacing; lapse on first_patched_version, on a same-major and on a NEW-major release,
  not on a prerelease or an older unaffected release; production closure finds the injected node-gyp chain, ignores
  devDependencies (also behind a `workspace:*` dependency whose lockfile entry merges devDependencies), excludes a
  pruned package's exclusive subtree, applies `resolutions`, fails closed on an unresolvable descriptor; the committed
  register is well formed; scope (wildcard, comma, `packages` list), decision, owner reference / placeholder, id,
  future date, reason, drop_when, schema, duplicate, >30 days, expiry refused (expiry day valid); NDJSON parser fails
  closed; evaluate(): decided, undecided for another advisory / package / no id, production path, fix (both kinds),
  each lookup failing, unevaluable range, expired; unused reported.

## Runtime image: node-gyp and its install-time-only tree pruned (branch chore/prune-node-gyp-runtime, 2026-11-17; no SQL)
- **Context:** `yarn workspaces focus --production` kept node-gyp 13.0.1 in the one runtime image, because Yarn injects
  `node-gyp: npm:latest` into the lockfile entries of argon2, node-addon-api, msgpackr-extract and fsevents. Two
  production paths reached it: `@rab/server > argon2 > node-gyp` and `@rab/worker > bullmq > msgpackr > msgpackr-extract
  > node-gyp`. With it came tar, tinyglobby, fdir, picomatch 4.0.5 (GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf, High, unfixed), a nested
  undici 8, which, isexe, nopt, abbrev, proc-log, env-paths, exponential-backoff, graceful-fs, minizlib, chownr, yallist
  and @isaacs/fs-minipass. Nothing at runtime loads them (argon2 and msgpackr-extract use their prebuilt addons through
  node-gyp-build; the image has no compiler), but they were attack surface and scanner noise that would HOLD every
  release once the scanners ingest the GHSA, and the policy forbids an agent from adding a register entry for it.
- **Control:** `runtime-deps.cjs prune` runs in both dependency stages right after `focus` (and before the Worker delta, so
  the delta cannot carry the tree back). It cuts the edges to `RUNTIME_PRUNE` (`['node-gyp']`, exported for other gates)
  and deletes every package then unreachable from the explicit `--root` workspaces (review L2: `@rab/server` in
  runtime-modules, `@rab/worker @rab/server` in worker-modules; a missing root refuses). Edges are each package's
  declared dependencies/optional/peer dependencies plus its lockfile entry (so injected or extended dependencies count),
  located with Node's own lookup, so a package any runtime package reaches stays. Workspace links are never removed.
  Fail closed: it removes nothing when an installed package has no lockfile entry, a drop name is not installed, or a
  kept package's code literally loads a package it would remove (an undeclared dependency that only worked through
  hoisting). Review L1: that scan reads every file of every kept package, comments included (a false positive is a
  refusal), and also matches the bare side-effect `import 'x'`; the only tolerated hit is a `bin` file that is neither
  the package's main nor an exports target loading a `RUNTIME_PRUNE` name itself (node-gyp-build's and
  node-gyp-build-optional-packages' install-time `bin.js` require node-gyp). The final stage's existing import scan still
  has to resolve every compiled import, and its `--forbid` now includes `node-gyp` and `tinyglobby`. Review I1: the image
  gate's `container` check runs `native-addons-smoke.cjs` inside the finished image as 1000:1000, `--network none`,
  read-only, on amd64 and arm64: argon2 (as the API resolves it) must hash and verify with argon2id m=19456,t=2,p=1 and
  reject a wrong password, and msgpackr (as BullMQ resolves it) must report native acceleration with msgpackr-extract's
  native `extractStrings` loaded; any other outcome fails the gate.
- **Measured:** a local `focus --production` of this lockfile removes 18 package directories from the API tree (554 ->
  536) and the same 18 from the Worker tree (610 -> 592); the undeclared-dependency scan read 12 427 / 13 743 kept files
  with no hit. The image build numbers are in the PR.
- **Residual risk:** a kept package that loads a pruned package by a computed (non-literal) specifier would only fail at
  runtime. None of the pruned packages is a runtime library of the API or the Worker; the image gate's PDF render and the
  compiled-import scan exercise the real image.
- **Tests:** `packages/rab-docker/rab/test/runtime-deps.test.cjs` (ci-security `deployment-config`): an exclusive node-gyp
  subtree (including the hoisted picomatch@4 and the nested undici@8) is pruned through both production paths; a
  dependency shared with a runtime package (semver, picomatch@2, undici@6) is kept; lockfile-only edges keep a package;
  a workspace devDependency is never a root; prune refuses on an undeclared dependency, a tree that is not the lockfile's
  install, a stale or wildcard drop; the final `--forbid` fails if node-gyp or tinyglobby returns, top level or nested; the
  Dockerfile prunes in both stages before the delta with the exported list and explicit roots. L1/L2 regressions (each
  exits 1 and removes nothing): a bin that is also the main requiring graceful-fs, a bin that is an exports target,
  a bin-only file loading a non-drop package, `import 'graceful-fs';`, `/*! x */ require('graceful-fs')`, no `--root`,
  `--root @rab/server` without that link, a `--root` that is not a workspace. `tests/test_image_gate.py`
  (NativeAddonsSmoke): the smoke runs as 1000:1000 offline read-only, and a non-zero exit or a missing OK line fails.

## PG_SSL_CA_CERT — the database CA as PEM text, for hosts that cannot mount a file (branch feat/pg-ssl-ca-cert-inline, 2026-11-17; no SQL)
