```
Reversal:   refuse GRANTED_EXISTING in the boot path only (PlatformAdminBootstrapOnBoot), leaving the CLI as it is.
```

- **MFA at first sign-in (confirmed, unchanged).** The command's path does not enforce MFA itself. The ordinary sign-in policy
  (`LoginSecondFactorPolicyService`) makes a platform admin enrol at sign-in only when `AUTH_MFA_ENFORCE_PLATFORM_ADMIN=true`.
  The default, including production compose, is false. When the switch is off, the boot logs a warning after creating or
  granting the admin. ASSUMPTION FLAGGED: whether production should turn it on is the owner's decision; nothing here changes it.
- **Residual (unchanged from the CLI).** If the 24 h link expires unused, neither a restart nor the command sends another
  one: the bootstrap is one-time, and forgot-password serves ACTIVE accounts only. Recovery is a deliberate database action
  today. A resend path for the bootstrap invite would be a separate owner decision.
- **Operator log lines** are fixed text in `PLATFORM_ADMIN_BOOT_LOG` (no email, user id or database message), context
  `PlatformAdminBootstrap`.
- **Tests.** Unit: platform-admin-bootstrap-on-boot.spec (every outcome's line, password refused, no throw, one attempt per
  process, failure labels), platform-admin-bootstrap.service.spec (ALREADY_BOOTSTRAPPED writes nothing; the one invite is
  addressed to the configured email; authority refused before the function runs), never-in-runtime-env.spec,
  compose-owner-login.test.cjs, run-prestart-shell-tests.cjs (cases 1d/1e/3/13b). PostgreSQL:
  bootstrap-admin-at-boot.integration.spec (fresh, existing admin no-op, four concurrent boots, password refused,
  crewflow_app refused, malformed email, CLOSED). The existing bootstrap-admin integration suites run the CLI unchanged.

---

## First platform administrator at API boot: independent security review of #264 fixed (2026-11-19)

This entry supersedes these parts of the entry above: its MFA bullet ("unchanged ... the boot logs a warning"), trade-off
BOOT-3, and the "Residual" bullet.

- **F1 (HIGH), MFA at first sign-in is now required by the boot path.** `PlatformAdminBootstrapOnBoot.runOnce` refuses before
  the bootstrap runs when `AUTH_MFA_ENFORCE_PLATFORM_ADMIN` is not true. Nothing runs: no transaction, no write, no email. With
  the switch on, `LoginSecondFactorPolicyService` answers `enroll` for a platform admin without a factor, so the
  boot-created admin gets the enrolment challenge at its first sign-in and never a session. Proved through the HTTP app:
  activate, then `POST /auth/login` returns 409 `SECOND_FACTOR_REQUIRED` with `requirement: 'enroll'`. The CLI is unchanged.
- **F2 (MEDIUM), an existing account is granted at boot only when its email ownership was proven.** Boot policy
  (`requireProvenExistingAccount`): GRANTED_EXISTING requires `status = 'active'`, `email_verified_at IS NOT NULL`, a
  non-deleted row and a manager-tier profile. Anything else rolls the whole transaction back (the function's
  `platform_admin` row included) and is reported as REFUSED_EXISTING_ACCOUNT_UNVERIFIED or REFUSED_EXISTING_ACCOUNT_NOT_MANAGER
  (staff-only, F3). The check runs on the row the database function resolved, in the same transaction, under its advisory
  lock and `FOR UPDATE`. That makes it atomic, unlike a separate pre-lookup. The migration and the function are unchanged.
  The CLI keeps its rule.
- **F2, defence in depth (all actors, all paths).** `assertPlatformAdminTargetAllowed` (engine/core-modules/platform-admin)
  answers 404 when the target holds an active platform-admin claim and the actor does not. It is wired into
  `ManagerService.findPendingProfileOrFail` (resend, re-point and cancel of a pending invitation; before the CEO rule's 403),
  `ManagerService.changeEmail`, `StaffService.findPendingProfileOrFail` and `StaffService.changeEmail`, and
  `UserDeletionService.assertCanDelete` (a tenant actor now gets 404 instead of 409 `CANNOT_DELETE_PLATFORM_ADMIN`; another
  platform admin still gets the 409). The Admin Panel's platform-admin resend keeps working (the actor is an admin).
- **F5, an existing admin that never activated.** On every later boot, when the existing admin is still invited and holds no
  unexpired, unused invite, the boot logs a distinct warning (`activationExpired`) and re-sends nothing. **Supported recovery:
  none exists today.** No command re-sends the bootstrap invite. `grant-platform-admin` needs an existing account and does not
  send invites. Forgot-password serves ACTIVE accounts only. The tenant resend paths are closed to this account by F2. Do not
  improvise SQL. A supported path (for example an audited `resend-bootstrap-invite` command) is an owner decision.
- **F4.** `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` must not exist in any platform environment before this deploys. rab-api and rab-worker
  refuse to start with it (exit 64 / runtime guard).
- **I1.** The deploy-file lint (`bootstrapAdminComposeTextProblems`, in the owner-login gate) allows `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_*` only
  under rab-api, only the five inputs, and only as `KEY: ${KEY:-}`. The two compose files themselves are not edited in this PR
  (see the PR body).

```
SECURITY TRADE-OFF (BOOT-3, revised): boot grants an existing account only if active, verified and manager-tier
Decision:   the boot path refuses (rolls back) any other existing account; the operator uses grant-platform-admin for those.
Reason:     security review F2/F3: an INVITED manager's address can be re-pointed by a tenant manager before activation.
Risk:       none new; a legitimate existing account that is not manager-tier must be granted with the CLI.
Mitigation: named refusal lines; nothing is written.
Reversal:   drop requireProvenExistingAccount from PlatformAdminBootstrapOnBoot.runOnce.
```

- **Tests added.** Unit: the F1 refusal (bootstrap.run never called), the F2/F3 refusals and rollback, F5 activation states,
  `assertPlatformAdminTargetAllowed`. PostgreSQL: MFA off is refused with no rows; the INVITED-manager email is refused with no
  `platform_admin` or outbox row; ambiguous email and ambiguous organisation; a boot racing the CLI gives one admin and one
  email; the activation token is absent from every log line and from `audit_log.metadata`; F5. HTTP app: F1 activate gives
  the enrol challenge; a tenant CEO resend or cancel on the pending bootstrap admin gives 404; resend or delete on a granted
  account gives 404; staff-only email refused. `user-deletion-abuse-cases` expects 404 for a tenant actor.

- **Re-review follow-up (N1, Low) and CF-04 wording (2026-11-19).** `assertPlatformAdminTargetAllowed` (404 unless the actor is
  an active platform admin) now also guards `ManagerService.update` (PATCH /managers/:id) and `ManagerService.resetPassword`,
  `StaffService.resetPassword` and the staff status change (deactivate / reactivate), and `MembersService`'s member lookup
  (suspend, reinstate, role change). Each check runs after the tenant-scoped lookup and before any permission-specific 403.
  **CF-04 wording, superseded:** "a platform administrator's email cannot be changed through this path (403
  PROTECTED_ACCOUNT)" is no longer what a tenant actor sees. A tenant actor now gets **404**, and the email stays
  unchanged. `EmailChangeService`'s 403 `PROTECTED_ACCOUNT` stays as the inner layer, and a platform-admin actor still
  receives it (tested). In the same way, a tenant actor deleting a platform admin gets 404, while another platform admin
  still gets 409 `CANNOT_DELETE_PLATFORM_ADMIN`.
- **REFUSED_AMBIGUOUS_EMAIL test seeding.** The database now refuses a second account with an email that already exists
  ("This email address is not available for a new account"). So the integration test plants that legacy state with
  triggers off (`SET LOCAL session_replication_role = replica`, fixture superuser, its own transaction). The function's
  refusal of the state is still exercised.

## AI: operator-set in production, default off (branch chore/ai-enabled-operator-set, owner decision 2026-11-20; compose and gates only, no SQL, no server code)

The owner wants AI usable in production, Anthropic only. This reverses the "AI pinned off in production" decision: the
production compose files (`docker-compose.production.yml`, `docker-compose.image.yml`; `docker-compose.local-build.yml` kept
in step) no longer pin `AI_ENABLED: 'false'` on rab-api and rab-worker. They commit `AI_ENABLED: ${AI_ENABLED:-false}`
(production: once, in the shared optional list both services merge), so AI is off unless the operator sets
`AI_ENABLED=true`. No `OPENAI_API_KEY` or other provider key is added (owner: Anthropic only).

- **Who can turn it on?** The operator who controls the deployment's interpolation values: `compose.env` (image compose) or
  the platform's `AI_ENABLED` variable (OpenShip). The compose-owner-login lint refuses it in `database.env` / `runtime.env`
  (the committed expression would silently override it there) and accepts exactly `true` or `false` (X3.1 strict switch).
- **What else is needed (unchanged controls, all fail closed).** `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (already passed through, a secret, never
  committed); each organisation's AI switch, default OFF, which only a platform admin with step-up can change (Settings →
  AI); and a model the build marks `productionApproved` (catalog.ts). **Today no model is production-approved and
  `realProviderEnvironment` refuses every real provider under NODE_ENV=production**, so `AI_ENABLED=true` alone gives "AI not
  configured" (503 to eligible users) until a separate, reviewed code change records release checklist §3.7 (DPA, zero
  retention, no training, region, sub-processors, DPIA, privacy notice). That change is not in this PR.
- **Spend ceilings (unchanged, committed defaults).** `AI_DAILY_BUDGET_USD` (per organisation per UTC day, default 2),
  `AI_USER_DAILY_BUDGET_USD` (per user, effective min with the organisation's, default 1), `AI_ORG_DAILY_TOKEN_BUDGET` (tokens
  per organisation per day, default 200000), plus the rate and turn limits already in the shared list. A meter failure refuses
  the step.
- **Still refused.** `AI_DEV_ALLOW_REAL_PROVIDERS=true` outside development (boot refusal, `aiBootProblems`); it is not
  listed in any production compose file and compose.env refuses it.
- **Gates (fail closed).** `scripts/compose-owner-login.cjs`: every uncommented `AI_ENABLED` line of a compose file must be
  exactly `AI_ENABLED: ${AI_ENABLED:-false}` (a literal `'true'` as much as the old `'false'`, another default, `:?`, no
  default, a quoted or list form are refused), and `docker-compose.production.yml` must carry it; every rendered combination
  gives both services a true/false value, the same on both; the gate's own renders (no `AI_ENABLED` in compose.env) must give
  `"false"` on both (`aiDefaultOffProblems`); the child environment drops a stray `AI_ENABLED` of the machine running the
  gate. `staging/verify-image-compose.cjs`: the reference render must give `"false"` on both services in both files; in the
  operator's deployed model `AI_ENABLED` is exactly true or false, identical on rab-api and rab-worker, and never from an env
  file.
- **Abuse cases (tests).** A committed literal `'true'` → refused (raw text and rendered default). AI on for the API only, or
  the Worker only → refused. `AI_ENABLED=yes` / `True` / `1` in compose.env → refused. `AI_ENABLED` in database.env /
  runtime.env → refused. A blank compose.env value → renders `false`, never the code default.

```
SECURITY TRADE-OFF: AI_ENABLED is operator-set in production instead of pinned 'false'
Decision:   a pinned-off control becomes an operator-controlled interpolation value, default off.
Reason:     owner decision 2026-11-20: AI wanted in production (Anthropic only).
Risk:       an operator (or anyone who can edit compose.env / the platform variables) can enable the platform AI switch
            without a code change. Residual: the code default of AI_ENABLED is true (EX-2), so a BLANK service-scoped
            platform override (OpenShip lets a service value win over the compose expression; no gate can see it)
            would enable it; the compose expression itself maps blank to false.
Mitigation: default off; exactly true/false; one value for both services; still needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, a per-organisation
            switch (default OFF, platform admin + step-up) and a production-approved model (none today); budgets and rate
            limits cap spend; AI_DEV_ALLOW_REAL_PROVIDERS stays refused outside development.
Reversal:   restore AI_ENABLED: 'false' under PINNED on rab-api / rab-worker and revert the two gates' AI_ENABLED rules.
```

## SF-2 review L-1 — the Venue Manager route flag pins every per-record Manager action to the caller's own Venue Managers (branch fix/venue-manager-target-pin, 2026-11-18; no SQL)
- **Threat:** a job, CLI command, AI tool or another service calls a per-record `ManagerService` method directly with
  `requiredPermission = venue_manager.create` (the flag `VenueManagerService` passes for the `/venue-managers` routes):
  `update`, `setActive`, `resetPassword`, `changePendingEmail`, `changeEmail`, `getTimeline`, `listNotes`, `addNote`,
  `listEmails`. The service re-checked that flag (SF-2 part 1) but not the target: only
  `VenueManagerService.assertOwnWorkspaceVenueManager` pinned it to a Venue Manager of the caller's own workspace, and in a
  separate transaction. A caller holding `venue_manager.create` that can see an Internal Manager, a CEO or another
  workspace's Venue Manager under RLS (e.g. a CEO granted the flag) could rename, suspend / reactivate, admin-reset the
  password of, correct or change the email of, or add a note to that account, or read its timeline, notes and email log,
  through the Venue Manager authority (finding L-1 of the PR #237 review; Low: needs a direct service call, no HTTP route
  reaches it).
- **Control:** `assertVenueRouteTargetTx` (the same helper, same name and signature, as PR #237 adds for `resendInvite` /
  `cancelInvite`): when the flag is `venue_manager.create`, in the action's own transaction, after the route-flag check
  (403) and before any row read, the target must be `{ id, organisationId, workspaceId: ctx.workspaceId, type: venue }`
  (organisation and workspace from the verified context, never from the caller's input); anything else, or a context with
  no organisation or workspace, is 404. All nine methods above call it (`addNote`: after its 400 body checks, which read no
  row; `changeEmail`: before the direct correction and before the verified path's `EmailChangeService.request`). No-op for
  the `/managers` flag (`manager.manage`), whose behaviour is unchanged. Layers: route guard
  (`PermissionGuard(venue_manager.create)`) → `VenueManagerService` gate → this in-transaction pin → organisation-scoped
  lookup → `manager_profile` RLS.
- **Verified email change (security review of PR #248, Low):** `EmailChangeService.request` read the target only by
  organisation, so a direct caller holding `venue_manager.create` (or `staff.edit`) and its own password could start a
  verified email change (a token to an address it chooses, i.e. an account-takeover path) for any Internal Manager, CEO or
  other Manager's staff member it can see. `request` now takes a required `targetScope` (`manager` | `venue_manager` |
  `staff`) instead of a free permission flag; the scope fixes the flag re-checked (`manager.manage` /
  `venue_manager.create` / `staff.edit`; anything else 403 before any read) and, against the target's `core.user` row
  locked FOR UPDATE in the same transaction, the reach: `manager` = a Manager profile of the organisation (a CEO only for
  an active platform administrator, 403, the existing `ManagerService` CEO rule); `venue_manager` = a `type: venue`
  profile of `ctx.workspaceId`; `staff` = a staff profile in the caller's workspace that the caller created (mirrors
  `StaffService.changeEmail`'s `assertOwned`). Out of scope, or no workspace for the two workspace scopes, is 404, before
  any other check on the target. `ManagerService.changeEmail` passes `venue_manager` for the Venue Manager flag and
  `manager` otherwise; `StaffService.changeEmail` passes `staff`.
- **Invariant the pins rely on:** `manager_profile.type` never changes after creation and `manager_profile.workspace_id`
  only goes from NULL to a value (first venue assignment, own-workspace creation), enforced in application code only. A
  future "move a Venue Manager between workspaces" or "change a profile's type" feature must revisit
  `assertVenueRouteTargetTx` and the `venue_manager` email-change scope (both say so in code).
- **Behaviour change:** none over HTTP (the `/venue-managers` routes already 404 these targets in `VenueManagerService`). A
  direct service call with the Venue Manager flag on a target that is not a Venue Manager of the caller's own workspace is
  now 404 instead of acting or returning data.
- **Related, different shape (flagged, not changed here):** `ManagerService.bulkEmail` also accepts `venue_manager.create`
  but takes a list of ids, and only `VenueManagerService.bulkEmail` narrows that list to the caller's own Venue Managers. A
  direct caller passing the Venue Manager flag can still email any Manager of the organisation it can see. Whether
  out-of-scope ids should be skipped or refuse the whole batch (404) is an owner decision, so it is left for a follow-up.
- **Tests:** `venue-manager-target-pin.integration.spec.ts` (real PostgreSQL, RLS on as `crewflow_app`, service called
  directly): a CEO that CAN read the Internal Managers and the Internal Manager's notes under RLS (precondition asserted
  through `ManagerService.get` / `listNotes`), holding `venue_manager.create` through a real per-user grant override plus
  `user.reset_password`, with a workspace and a real signed-in session for the step-up-gated methods. On an Internal
  Manager: `update`, `setActive` (suspend and reactivate), `resetPassword`, `changePendingEmail` (pending target),
  `changeEmail` (direct path on a pending target, verified path on an active one) and `addNote` are 404 and leave the
  organisation inert (audit log, outbox, reset tokens, revoked refresh tokens, invites and live invites, email-change
  requests, notes, every user's email / name / phone / status / must-reset / security version, every manager profile's job
  title / archive); `getTimeline`, `listNotes` and `listEmails` are 404, return nothing, and leave it inert. `update`,
  `setActive` and `resetPassword` are also 404 + inert for the caller's own CEO profile and another workspace's Venue
  Manager. Positive controls: the same caller updates, suspends, reactivates and resets an own-workspace Venue Manager
  (audit rows written); corrects and changes a pending own-workspace Venue Manager's email; adds a note to and reads the
  timeline, notes and emails of an own-workspace Venue Manager; the `/managers` flag still updates the Internal Manager.
  The six newer methods are also 404 + inert (reads return nothing) for the caller's own CEO profile and another
  workspace's Venue Manager; a context with no workspace gets 404 with the Venue Manager flag even on the caller's own Venue
  Manager. `EmailChangeService.request`: the `venue_manager` scope on an Internal Manager, a CEO and another workspace's
  Venue Manager, the `staff` scope on a staff member another Manager created (caller holding `staff.edit`), and the
  `venue_manager` scope with no workspace are 404 + inert; an unknown scope is 403 + inert; positive controls start a
  verified change for an active own-workspace Venue Manager (through `ManagerService.changeEmail`) and for the caller's own
  staff member. Fail-first: with the `assertVenueRouteTargetTx` calls removed, every ManagerService refusal fails (the
  calls act or return data); with only the email-change scope check removed, every `EmailChangeService.request` refusal
  fails (a request is written).

## Semantic posture: trigger definition hash, and a pinned search_path for the read (branch feat/posture-trigger-def-hash, 2026-11-18; split from #251 review F5; no migration)

- **Finding (security finding format, §5.8).** Severity: Low (detection gap).
  - **Actor:** anyone who can re-create a trigger. In the owner-login build that includes an injected statement as crewflow_owner (the owner-accepted G-02/G-03 class).
  - **Action:** `DROP TRIGGER` plus `CREATE TRIGGER` under the same name and function, but with a different definition: AFTER instead of BEFORE, another `UPDATE OF` list, a WHEN clause that never matches, or other arguments (for example a widened grant-parity allow-list).
  - **Consequence:** the guard silently stops guarding, and the semantic posture monitor (`posture-drift/semantic-posture.ts`) reports nothing.
- **Root cause.** The trigger line was `trigger|table|name|enabled=…|function`. It pinned the name, the enabled state and the function, but not the definition.
- **Fix.** Every trigger line now ends in `|def=<md5>`. The hash covers:
  - tgtype (timing, level and events);
  - the `UPDATE OF` column names;
  - the whitespace-normalised WHEN text. It is cut out of `pg_get_triggerdef`, because `pg_get_expr` cannot deparse OLD and NEW together. Only an anchored qualifier of the trigger's own schema is removed;
  - DEFERRABLE and INITIALLY DEFERRED;
  - the arguments;
  - the transition-table names.

  No table or schema name goes into the hash, so workspace copies stay comparable. The PG16/17/18 goldens are regenerated from a migrations-only database, and only the `def=` suffix changes.
- **Also.** `readSemanticPosture` pins `search_path = pg_catalog, public, pg_temp` for the read and restores a caller's value afterwards. Rendered names (regprocedure, pg_get_expr, pg_get_triggerdef) are qualified relative to search_path, so a role-level or database-level search_path can no longer change a line. Residual (security review L-3): `public` stays in the path so extension types such as citext render unqualified, as in the goldens, so operator and overload resolution through `public` remains a residual risk for this read until the L-3 follow-up lands (a session-level pin and/or OPERATOR(pg_catalog.…) in this query).
- **Tests.**
  - `semantic-posture-trigger-def.integration.spec.ts` (rolled back): re-creating a probe trigger as AFTER, with another column list, with a WHEN clause, with other arguments or with other events keeps the line prefix and changes `def=`. Re-creating the original definition restores the original line. A search_path that includes core renders the same lines, and the caller's value is restored.
  - `semantic-posture-trigger-def.spec.ts` (static): SQL shape, the anchored strip, the goldens, and the pin/restore order.

## Upgrade runner — reviewed upgrade-from lists, and a patch resumes its failed `.0` step (branch feat/runner-cross-upgrade, 2026-11-18; owner decisions 2026-11-18; no SQL)
- **Threat:** (1) after #219, a minor release accepted only the LAST published version. Once 0.6.1 is published, a database
  still at 0.6.0 is refused by 0.7.0 (65), so the operator's only way forward is an extra hop or `--force`, which skips the
  previous-version check for everything. (2) A wider "accept anything older" rule would let a database two minors behind
  skip the commands of the minor in between (0.5.0 → 0.7.0 would never run 0.6.0's workspace commands or the adoption).
  (3) When a minor's instance command fails (the HWS switch-on: 0.7.0's cutover refuses without a verified backup), the
  workspaces it blocked stay blocked (503) and a fixed patch (0.7.1) could not take over: it refused 65 because 0.7.0 was
  not complete. The only way out was `--force`, and a forced patch skipped the `.0`'s instance commands, so the one-way
  cutover sentinel and the copy never ran. (4) A retried step that is not idempotent could duplicate or corrupt data when
  it runs a second time after a partial failure. (5) A patch that "resumes" a `.0` it cannot actually finish (a workspace
  with no logbook row: only 0.6.0 adopts) would block that workspace forever instead of refusing the start.
- **Control (a), Twenty's model (TWENTY_PREVIOUS_VERSIONS + TWENTY_CROSS_UPGRADE_SUPPORTED_VERSIONS @ eedb0a73,
  re-implemented, not copied):** `CREWFLOW_UPGRADE_FROM_VERSIONS` (`upgrade-version.ts`) is an explicit list per MINOR release,
  reviewed with that release. A minor release accepts exactly the versions on its list (0.7.0: every published 0.6.x it
  lists); anything else is refused 65 with a message that names the list. Fail closed (`AppVersionError`, config 64, before
  any outcome, fresh and rollback included): a missing or empty list, an unsorted or duplicate entry, an entry that is not
  published (`CREWFLOW_PREVIOUS_VERSIONS`) or not older than the release, an inherited (prototype) key, and any entry that is
  not on the PREVIOUS minor line (it would skip that line's commands, threat 2). The adoption release 0.6.0 must list exactly
  0.4.0 and 0.5.0. Patches keep their own-line rule (no entry). The M-1 fold (a patch counts as complete only with its `.0`)
  and the L-2 ascending check are unchanged. `crossUpgradeSupportedVersions` = list + code version, as Twenty.
- **Control (b), Twenty's resume (upgrade-sequence-runner.service.ts:98-247 "Rerun the upgrade to resume from this step",
  resumeWorkspaceCommandsFromCursors):** a patch start resumes its minor `.0`. `decideUpgradeStart` continues a patch when an
  earlier UNFORCED, non-initial instance row was executed by the `.0` or by an earlier patch of its line (review O3: a fresh
  0.7.1 whose 0.7.0 retry failed wrote rows as 0.7.1 only; 0.7.2 must still resume) AND every READY workspace has a logbook
  row; otherwise it still refuses 65 (threat 5; forced rows never count). Every `.0` instance COMMAND whose latest attempt
  is not completed runs again under the `.0`'s own step name with `executed_by_version` = the patch.
  - **Order invariant (review R1):** the locked runner applies every pending migration between `beforeApply` and
    `afterApply`, so the retry runs in `beforeApply`: BEFORE any migration of the patch's start (never after this start's
    migrations; on the `.0` schema unless an earlier `--force` or fresh patch start applied later ones), and only when the
    `.0`'s migrations step is completed (nothing maps a migration to a release, so that step proves every migration the `.0`
    ships was applied). A `.0` command with its migrations step incomplete refuses 65 ("Nothing was applied") unless
    `--force`. A command that fails again is recorded failed (attempt + 1): with migrations pending an unforced start refuses
    (`MinorReleaseResumeFailedError`, 66, fail closed: the code cannot serve with its migrations unapplied); the patch's
    migrations are NOT applied, and the log names the `.0` command and its attempt, never a migration (review A). Under
    `--force` the start goes on (review B): the migrations apply and it serves degraded (70), every row forced, the blocked
    workspaces stay 503. With nothing pending it serves degraded (70). Only after the `.0` is resumed is the patch's own
    migrations step recorded.
  - **Hotfix case:** when a `.0` MIGRATION failed and the patch ships the fix, and the `.0` has instance commands, the patch
    start refuses 65 unless `--force`: the `.0`'s commands must never run on a schema whose `.0` migrations are not all
    applied, and the patch cannot apply them without also applying its own, so there is no order that runs the commands
    first. `--force` applies every migration, then runs the `.0`'s commands (WARNING; rows forced). A `.0` with no instance
    command has no such conflict (its migrations step alone is recorded).
    Exceptions, which run the `.0`'s commands after every migration: a start with no instance row (fresh install or an
    unchecked local / test history: no data of the `.0` exists) and a `--force` start whose `.0` migrations step is
    incomplete (logged as a WARNING). The invariant is stated in `upgrade-runner.ts`, `upgrade-version.ts` and
    `upgrade-command.ts`.
  - **`--force` (review O4):** a `--force` patch start that is resumable reports decision `continue`, not `forced` (the resume
    check comes first); every logbook row it writes is still marked `forced = true`. A later retry of a `.0` step that an
    earlier `--force` start attempted, run when nothing is pending (that start already applied this code's migrations), is
    recorded `forced = true` too, with a WARNING that it runs on a schema the forced start moved past the `.0`. The
    in-process `testUpgrade` seam is refused unless NODE_ENV=test on a disposable, non-production database (like
    `readTestFailCommand`).
  - Failed `.0` workspace steps are retried by the workspace pass under their `.0` names (it walks each cursor's sequence). A
    blocked workspace stays blocked (503 "Workspace is being upgraded.") until its step passes. `/healthz` reads the `.0`'s
    instance steps for a patch too, so a still-failed `.0` step reads `failed`, also when the patch's own step is completed
    (review R2). A fresh 0.7.1 install now runs 0.7.0's instance commands, as a fresh 0.7.0 install does.
- **Idempotency audit (threat 4):** 0.6.0 has no instance command. Its workspace commands re-run as no-ops:
  StaffProfileMemberSelect (CREATE POLICY guarded by IF NOT EXISTS; ws-staff-member-select spec, crash after COMMIT),
  DropWorkspaceCoreForeignKeys (DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS; ws-core-fk-removal spec, second run up-to-date) and
  SyncStandardObjects (plans nothing on a re-run; standard-objects-catalog spec). Every workspace step is one transaction,
  rolled back whole on failure. 0.7.0 (not registered, #175 / #177): HwsCutover is resumable by design (it blocks first,
  keeps per-workspace state started → verified, copies with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, skips verified workspaces, inserts the
  activation sentinel ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; hws-c3-cutover spec: kill and resume, second run copies nothing, failed then
  completed through the logbook). #177's Q3 `VALIDATE CONSTRAINT` is a no-op on a validated constraint and the runner skips
  the level bump at or past its level. The rule is written into `upgrade-command.ts` / `workspace-upgrade-command.ts`.
- **Not changed:** no SQL, no migration, no grant. The shipped version stays 0.6.0; the shipped map holds only 0.6.0's
  adoption entry. 0.7.0's release PR (#175) must add `CREWFLOW_UPGRADE_FROM_VERSIONS['0.7.0']` next to the version bump (a
  release guard test refuses a minor code version without a valid entry).
- **Tests:** `upgrade-cross-upgrade.spec.ts` (pure): the list rules and every fail-closed case (64), a refusal names the
  list (65), M-1 and L-2 kept, the patch resume decision (resumable / not / forced / minor never resumes), the instance steps
  of a start, a release guard on the shipped version. `cross-upgrade-resume.integration.spec.ts` (UpgradeRun on the locked
  runtime login, a probe instance command shaped like the C3 cutover): 0.7.1 before 0.7.0 refuses 65; 0.7.0 from 0.6.0, the
  cutover fails, workspace blocked (resolver 'upgrading'); a READY workspace with no logbook row stops the resume (65);
  0.7.1 retries `0.7.0_ProbeHwsCutover` (attempt 2 by 0.7.1, still blocked, `/healthz` not ok); 0.7.1 again succeeds
  (attempt 3), then 0.7.1_TypeOrmMigrations, unblocked, `/healthz` ok, a further start records nothing; a failed 0.7.0
  workspace step is retried by 0.7.1 under its 0.7.0 name; R2: `/healthz` is exactly `failed` while the `.0` step is failed,
  also with the patch's own step completed; R1, through the REAL locked start with a REAL patch-only migration: the cutover
  runs before the migration (66 and the migration not applied when it fails again; 65 and nothing applied when 0.7.0's
  migrations step is incomplete); O3: after a fresh 0.7.1 whose 0.7.0 retry failed, 0.7.2 resumes. Existing patch / ledger /
  C3 specs updated for the list.

## Worker marker bound only through the tenant-context binder (2026-11-18)

- **Asset.** `rab.actor_type = 'worker'`: the RLS marker that opens the `*_worker_scan` / `*_worker_select` /
  `*_worker_update` policies (staff_profile, payroll_record, payroll_run, payroll_run_line, shift_staff_review, ...).
- **Threat.** A new code path writes the marker directly (a copied `set_config('rab.actor_type', 'worker', true)`), so a
  wider read/write path opens outside the reviewed binder, without the binder's pool-safety checks and without anyone
  noticing in review. Before this change `worker-actor-type-trusted-only.spec.ts` (#217) allowlisted three raw sites (HWS
  backfill, the workspace -> core orphan check, the account-invite cleanup's level-22 pass), so a fourth raw site in one of
  those files, or a moved one, was a matter of updating counts.
- **Control.** All three now bind through `tenant-context.service.ts`, the one statement that writes the identity GUCs
  (`bindGucsSql`, `rab.actor_type` from `ctx.actorType` only):
  - HWS backfill read identity: `TenantContextService.bindCoreIdentityGucs` (RESET ROLE, then current_user = session_user,
    then the binding statement), owner lookup, then the same binding with the owner as `rab.user_id`.
  - Orphan check and level-22 pass: `bindMaintenanceSessionGucs`, the same statement and parameter mapping but no RESET
    ROLE: the orphan connection acts as `crewflow` through a session-level SET ROLE on the owner login, which RESET ROLE
    would drop for the rest of the connection (the check would then read as `crewflow_owner`). The orphan check stays
    `BEGIN READ ONLY`. The level-22 pass re-binds the organisation, workspace and role in force, then binds them back with
    the previous user and no marker, and refuses (the candidate is retained) if the marker or an optional scope GUC is
    already set.
  - The static spec's raw-GUC allowlists are now empty in rab-server and rab-worker: any direct `set_config` / `SET` of
    `rab.actor_type` outside TenantContextService fails CI. The three files moved to the `actorType` allowlists (exactly one
    literal `'worker'` site each).
- **Behaviour change (none intended).** The binding statement also resets `rab.team_shift_id`, `rab.team_staff_id`,
  `rab.admin_scope` and `rab.upgrade_scope` to `''`, and the orphan check's first binding sets `rab.user_id` / `rab.role` to
  `''` instead of leaving the session value. None of these jobs sets those GUCs, and on a reused connection they already
  read `''`, so the RLS outcome is unchanged; the HWS backfill gains RESET ROLE + the identity check (a no-op on its
  connection, which never sets a role).
- **Residual.** `bindMaintenanceSessionGucs` does not RESET ROLE or check the role (by design, see above). Two separate
  misuses, two separate controls:
  - *Setting the marker* through it needs an `actorType: 'worker'` literal in a file on the `actorType` allowlist of
    `worker-actor-type-trusted-only.spec.ts`, which review sees.
  - *Skipping RESET ROLE* needs NO such literal: a request path could call it with an ordinary context and lose the pool
    safety layer of TenantContextService's binder (a session-level SET ROLE left on a pooled connection would survive).
    `tenant-binder-callers.spec.ts` pins its callers to exactly the orphan check, the account-invite cleanup
    and the Worker re-export; any other file that names the function fails CI.
  - The Worker reaches it through `engine/worker-shared/maintenance-session-binder.ts`, a runtime re-export the
    import-boundary checker cannot see through. `worker-shared-reexports.spec.ts` lists the runtime re-exports allowed in
    that folder (today only this one), so a new one fails CI and needs an explicit entry (owner asked to accept the pattern).
  - *Running the binding statement by hand* (`manager.query(bindGucsSql(), [..., 'worker'])`) needs neither a raw
    set_config nor an `actorType` literal. `tenant-binder-callers.spec.ts` pins `bindGucsSql` too, with an EMPTY external
    allow-list: only tenant-context.service.ts may name it outside tests.
  - The raw-GUC pattern also catches `E'rab.actor_type'`, dollar quoting (`$$rab.actor_type$$`, `$tag$…$tag$`), a
    parenthesised `('rab.actor_type')` and `UPDATE pg_settings … rab.actor_type`.
  - **Known limits of these static fences (covered by review, deliberately not detected):**
    - a wrapper exported from an allow-listed file (`export const g = bindMaintenanceSessionGucs`, or an exported function
      that calls it or `bindGucsSql`) and then called elsewhere under its own name;
    - a re-export under another name beyond its first hop, outside `engine/worker-shared/`;
    - a run-time GUC name or a GUC name passed as a bound parameter, computed keys, access by a computed property name;
    - non-`.ts` files.
- **Tests.** `worker-actor-type-trusted-only.spec.ts` (empty raw allowlists; a raw site appended to any Worker file fails
  it; the extended forms each tested), `tenant-binder-callers.spec.ts`, `worker-shared-reexports.spec.ts`; `hws-backfill.integration.spec.ts`, `ws-core-fk-removal` / `hws-c1-org-level-workspace-paths` (orphan check),
  `account-invite-cleanup*.integration.spec.ts` and `phase-d-account-invite-cleanup-worker.integration.spec.ts` (level-22
  pass), `tenant-context.service.spec.ts` (binding statement text unchanged).

## CI supply chain — actions pinned to verified commit SHAs, release via gh, Dependabot covers composite actions (branch ci/actions-pins-sha, 2026-11-18; replaces Dependabot #222, #223, #224; no SQL, no runtime code)
- **Threat:** *whoever can move a tag or push to an action's repository* (a compromised maintainer, a hijacked release, a
  fork commit served through the parent's API) → has their code run in our jobs with the job's GITHUB_TOKEN and secrets
  → for cd-deploy-tag that token held `contents: write` on the whole workflow and was handed to a third-party action
  (softprops/action-gh-release). A SHA pin only helps if the SHA is a commit of the named repository: dorny/paths-filter
  was pinned to `15192bc0…`, the annotated **tag object** `v3`, not a commit (it resolved to the v3.0.4 commit
  `0e4a8c6e…`, which is now the pin; same code).
- **Control (`tools/check-action-pins.cjs`, ci-security `action-pins`, in the gate's `needs`):** every `uses:` under
  `.github/workflows/**` and `.github/actions/**` must be `owner/repo[/path]@<40 lowercase hex> # vX.Y.Z`; only
  `./.github/actions/` and `./.github/workflows/` local references are exempt (any other `./` path fails); `docker://`
  needs `@sha256:<64 hex>`. Two readings must agree (independent review of #236: an escaped quoted key `"uses"`, an
  explicit `? uses` key and a fake block scalar inside an open `{` each hid an unpinned `uses` from a line scanner
  alone): (1) a line scanner, which also refuses those three forms, flow mappings, aliases and a value on the next
  line, and ignores `uses:` text inside `run: |` blocks and comments; (2) the real YAML parser (root devDependency
  `yaml`; missing = fail): every mapping key `uses`, aliases and `<<` merges resolved, duplicate keys and parse errors
  fail. The multiset of `uses` values must be identical. Before either reading, a file containing NEL / U+2028 /
  U+2029, a bare CR or any other C0 control character (tab, LF, CR excepted) is refused: YAML 1.1 / libyaml-family
  parsers may break a line there (`# c<U+2028>      - uses: evil/act@main` is a comment to a 1.2 parser, possibly a
  step to Actions; re-review of #236). The parser must be yaml 2.x. `--remote` (GITHUB_TOKEN) asks the
  API, per distinct repository@SHA: `git/commits/<sha>` must exist (else `git/tags/<sha>` tells a tag object apart and the
  error names the commit to pin), and the comment's tag (`git/ref/tags/<tag>`, through tag objects) must resolve to
  exactly that commit — this also refuses a fork-only "impostor" commit, which no tag of the parent points at. Any
  lookup that cannot complete fails the job (fail closed). Limitation: the check proves the pin matches the named release
  today; it does not review what that release does (Dependabot's 14-day cooldown and code review do).
- **Release path:** cd-deploy-tag now runs `tools/create-github-release.sh` (`gh release create <tag> --repo …
  --verify-tag --title <tag> --generate-notes --notes-file <our notes>`); workflow `permissions: {}`, the job
  `contents: write` only, checkout `persist-credentials: false`. Behaviour changes, both fail closed: a tag that does not
  exist on GitHub is never created, and an existing release for the tag is an error (softprops updated it silently).
  The workflow only runs on a tag, so `tools/create-github-release.test.cjs` runs the script on every PR: exact argv
  and notes through a recording `gh`, a dry run, refused inputs (no gh call), the installed gh's own flag list, and the
  workflow's permissions/checkout wiring.
- **Bumps:** actions/upload-artifact v4.6.2 → v7.0.2 (`cf430e03…`), actions/download-artifact v4.3.0 → v8.0.2
  (`9000827c…`) together (v8 fails on an artifact digest mismatch instead of warning; since v5 a `pattern:` download
  that matches ONE artifact lands in `path/` instead of `path/<name>/`, so image-security-gate's manifest job puts a
  one-platform download back under its name before the merge; caught by this PR's own PR-mode gate), actions/setup-node v4.4.0 →
  v7.1.0 (`949feb24…`, also in the yarn-install composite action; v5's automatic cache applies only to npm since v6, so
  nothing changes for Yarn). Every SHA checked against `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/tags`. Version comments of the
  unchanged checkout/cache pins corrected from `# v4` to the exact release (`v4.4.0`, `v4.3.0`).
- **Dependabot:** `directories: ['/', '/.github/actions/*']` (composite actions were never scanned, so yarn-install's
  setup-node pin could not be renewed) and `cooldown: default-days: 14` for github-actions; security updates are not
  delayed by it. The docker ecosystem entry is unchanged.

## Phone apps print money exactly like the website (branch fix/mobile-money-format-en-gb, not merged)

Display only. No payroll, rate-resolution, rounding or pay-date rule changes; no endpoint, table, migration, role, grant
or RLS change. Owner decision: the iPhone (`Money.formatPence`, `ValueFormatting.swift`) and Flutter (`formatPence`,
`lib/core/theme/money.dart`) formatters print the web's en-GB `Intl.NumberFormat` currency output, matching `@rab/shared`
`formatPence`: sign before the pound sign and comma thousands separators (`-£1,234.56`; before: `£-1234.56`).

- **Asset:** pay amounts shown to staff and venue managers (pay rates, estimated pay, earned pay, payslip net and
  statement amounts).
- **Risk addressed (Low, integrity of what a person reads):** the same amount printed differently on the website and on
  a phone (`£-1.50` vs `-£1.50`, `£1234.56` vs `£1,234.56`) invites misreading a deduction or a total. Both apps still
  format from integer pence with integer arithmetic (never a float, never the device locale), and the sign comes from
  the value itself, so `Int64.min` / the most negative Dart int print correctly.
- **Drift control:** one table, `packages/rab-shared/src/utils/money-format-cases.json`, is read by the web
  (`money.spec.ts`, which also checks every case against `Intl.NumberFormat('en-GB', GBP)` where the float input is
  exact), Flutter (`test/money_format_test.dart`) and iPhone (`MoneyTests`, bundled via `project.yml`) test suites.
  `ci-iphone` now also runs when that file changes; `ci-mobile` already runs on any `packages/rab-shared/**` change.
- **Callers checked:** every money display in both apps goes through `formatPence` / `payRateLabel` /
  `estimatedPayLabel`; none pre-formats an amount or concatenates its own sign.

## CI audit — owner exceptions read from the base ref; audit ignore lists, broken yarn, missing tree versions and re-scored advisories fail (branch ci/npm-audit-decisions-harden, 2026-11-18; review F1, F3-F8 of #229; register prerequisite: branch fix/npm-audit-register-severity)
- **Re-checked first (2026-11-18), so the exception is still the only option:** GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf has
  `first_patched_version: null` (range `<= 4.0.7`); the registry's picomatch list ends at 4.0.7 with no prerelease ever
  published; micromatch/picomatch#194 is open; the latest tinyglobby 0.2.17, anymatch 3.1.3, micromatch 4.0.8, jest-util
  30.5.1, vite 8.3.8 and @nx/js / @nx/workspace 24.0.6 all still require picomatch. No `resolutions` target exists.
- **F1 (Medium) — a PR could approve itself:** CI ran the PR's own `tools/npm-audit-decisions.json`, so a PR could add
  an entry and the dependency it covers in one diff. Actor: anyone opening a PR → adds a register entry next to a
  vulnerable dependency → the required audit passes on that PR's say-so. Fix (the #225 import-boundary pattern):
  - `--base <ref>` (ci-security passes `origin/${GITHUB_BASE_REF}` on every PR) reads the decisions with
    `git show <ref>:tools/npm-audit-decisions.json`. Fail closed: an unknown ref, a shallow clone (no merge-base) or any
    git failure throws (exit 1); only git's "path does not exist in <ref>" means "no decisions". git runs without a
    shell with `LC_ALL=C` and no `LANGUAGE`; `--base` accepts a plain ref plus `~N` / `^N` only. The head copy is
    validated as well. The audit job checks out with `fetch-depth: 0`.
  - Decision-only PR: when the merge-base diff touches only the register and THREAT-MODEL.md, the head decisions are
    used, and every entry that is NEW OR CHANGED against the base (deep equality by id) must have `owner_decision_ref`
    equal to this PR's `pull_request.html_url` from `$GITHUB_EVENT_PATH` (unreadable payload = fail). Removing an entry
    needs no reference. **Owner to confirm:** the review asked for this on NEW entries; it is applied to CHANGED ones
    too, because otherwise a register-only PR could move `decided_on` / `expires` of an existing entry (a renewal)
    while still citing the old PR.
  - CHANGED TOGETHER: `--base` fails when the diff adds or changes a register entry together with `yarn.lock`, any
    `package.json`, `.yarnrc.yml`, anything under `.yarn/` or `.github/actions/yarn-install/`,
    `tools/check-npm-audit.cjs`, `packages/rab-docker/rab/runtime-deps.cjs` (its `RUNTIME_PRUNE` decides the
    production-closure condition), `ci-security.yaml` or `npm-audit-weekly.yaml` (the last four beyond the review's
    list). A pure removal may go with any of them.
  - No `--base` (push to main, the weekly run, local): the checked-out register decides; a `pull_request` event without
    `--base` is refused.
- **F3 (Low):** before auditing, `yarn config get npmAuditIgnoreAdvisories --json` and `npmAuditExcludePackages` must
  both be `[]` and no `YARN_NPM_AUDIT_*` variable may be set; otherwise exit 1 without auditing.
- **F4 (Low):** a yarn that cannot be spawned (`error`), is killed (`signal`) or exits outside {0, 1} for the audit
  (outside {0} for `config get` / `npm info`) fails. `main(argv, deps)` takes `yarn`, `env`, `root`, `today`,
  `fetchAdvisory` and `production` so this is tested.
- **F5 (Low):** a finding with an empty `Tree Versions` cannot be checked for a fix: undecided ("cannot evaluate").
- **F6 (Low):** each entry records the decided `severity` (`high` | `critical`); a finding rated above it is undecided
  (a re-scored advisory needs a new owner decision); unknown severities are undecided. The picomatch entry records
  `high` (prerequisite branch, merged first because CHANGED TOGETHER refuses register + tool in one PR).
- **F7 (Info):** `decided_on` / `expires` must round-trip through `Date` (2026-02-30, 2026-11-31 refused).
- **F8 (Info):** `.github/workflows/npm-audit-weekly.yaml` runs the same check every Monday 06:17 UTC (and on demand)
  against main; any run prints `::warning::` when an in-force entry has 7 days or fewer left (expiry day = 0).
- **Security review of #238 (2026-11-18):**
  - **G1 (Low):** a register change mixed with a path that is NOT on the CHANGED TOGETHER list (e.g. `src/x.ts`) was
    neither CHANGED TOGETHER nor decision-only: the base decided for that PR, but the new entry merged unbound and was
    in force from the next PR on. Fix: outside a decision-only PR, `selectRegister` fails when the head has entries that
    are new or changed against the MERGE-BASE (what this PR itself changed, so a base that moved on does not flag an
    untouched entry); pure removals stay allowed anywhere.
  - **G3:** the weekly run passes `--fail-on-expiring`, so it fails (and notifies) at 7 days or fewer left instead of
    only warning; ci-security still only warns, so PRs stay green until the real expiry. Read-only token, no issue.
  - **G4:** `npmAuditRegistry` must be unset (`null`) and `npmRegistryServer` `https://registry.yarnpkg.com` or
    `https://registry.npmjs.org`; `YARN_NPM_REGISTRY_SERVER` is refused like every `YARN_NPM_AUDIT_*` variable. An audit
    pointed at a server that reports nothing can no longer pass.
  - **Re-review follow-ups (2026-11-18, approved at 11f52617):** (1) CHANGED TOGETHER binds only additions and
    changes: a pure removal may go with yarn.lock / package.json / anything (the upgrade PR that drops an entry, as its
    `drop_when` says); an addition next to yarn.lock still fails. (2) The audit's connection is pinned as well as its
    URL: `httpsProxy`, `httpProxy`, `httpsCaFilePath` unset, `enableStrictSsl` true, `networkSettings` empty (yarn
    prints `undefined` when unset), and `YARN_HTTPS_PROXY`, `YARN_HTTP_PROXY`, `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, `NODE_OPTIONS`,
    `SSL_CERT_FILE`, `SSL_CERT_DIR` and `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0` refused (the last three variables since the
    22487db0 spot-check). **Plugins (corrected after the 22487db0 spot-check, Low):** the first version trusted
    `yarn plugin runtime --json`, but yarn marks `builtin` by the plugin's DECLARED name, so a `.yarn/plugins/x.cjs`
    that calls itself `@yarnpkg/plugin-npm-cli` (or `@@core`) and is listed under `plugins:` ran its `factory` inside
    yarn while the runtime list looked identical to a clean run (reproduced locally with yarn 4.13). The control now
    checks where plugins come from: no `plugins` key (even `[]`) in any `.yarnrc.yml` yarn reads (the project folder,
    every ancestor folder, the home folder), no `YARN_RC_FILENAME`, and `.yarn/plugins/` absent or empty; the runtime
    list stays as a supplementary check only. **Key allowlist (final check at 6d5365da, Low):** a `plugins` key
    hidden under `__proto__:` (yarn's js-yaml makes it a prototype assignment, so yarn loads the plugin, while a
    JS-object view of the file shows no `plugins` key), or the same under the legacy `# yarn lockfile v1` header (yarn
    then uses its v1 parser), still loaded a plugin. Instead of chasing parser tricks the rc check is now fail-closed:
    each `.yarnrc.yml` is read as a YAML DOCUMENT (keys as written, never through a JS object); its top-level keys must
    all be in `RC_ALLOWED_KEYS` (the seven the repository uses today: `enableConstraintsChecks`, `enableHardenedMode`,
    `enableInlineHunks`, `nodeLinker`, `yarnPath`, `networkConcurrency`, `httpRetry`, plus the nine whose values the
    audit-config checks verify); `plugins`, `<<` merge keys and any other key fail; `__proto__`, `constructor` and
    `prototype` fail at any depth; a non-mapping top level, a non-scalar key, a duplicate key or any YAML error or
    warning fails; a file starting with the legacy header (`/^(#.*\r?\n)*?#\s+yarn\s+lockfile\s+v1\r?\n/i`) fails;
    without the `yaml` library the check reports a problem. Adding a setting to `.yarnrc.yml` now needs the allowlist
    extended in the tool (a CHANGED TOGETHER path when it comes with a register entry, a review item otherwise). The
    repository's real `.yarnrc.yml` passes. Order (final review at bcff7c21): the plugin-source check runs first and
    alone, before yarn is spawned at all, because every yarn invocation (even `config get`) loads the configured
    plugins; only a clean result goes on to the yarn-based checks. `caFilePath` is not a yarn 4 setting: yarn
    refuses to start ("Unrecognized or legacy configuration settings") when it is in .yarnrc.yml or the environment,
    which already fails the check, so it is not queried. The repository's real effective config passes every check.
    Not covered: generic `HTTP(S)_PROXY` variables (yarn 4 does not read them). (3) Any argument other than
    `--base <ref>` / `--fail-on-expiring` exits 1, so a typo cannot turn the weekly expiry failure off. (4)
    `.github/actions/yarn-install/**` is on the CHANGED TOGETHER list. Nits: the decision-only path compares with the
    merge-base like G1, and the merge-base is computed once.
  - **G2 (owner decision, not built):** there is no cap on the total time an advisory may be excepted across
    renewals; each renewal is a new decision-only PR citing itself, at most 30 days each.
- **F9 (Info):** wording corrected on the prerequisite branch (node-gyp@13.0.1 has three production parents — argon2,
  node-addon-api, msgpackr-extract — and one picomatch chain, node-gyp > tinyglobby > picomatch@4.0.5).
- **Residual (accepted):** CI still runs the PR's own copy of the tool and workflow, so a PR that edits the tool can
  change the rules for itself (CHANGED TOGETHER makes it also impossible to touch the register in that PR, but the tool
  edit itself is a review control: owner review, no CODEOWNERS file). The register on the base is trusted as reviewed.
  A decision-only PR's owner reference proves only that this PR is the record, not who approved it; the owner's merge
  is the decision. A push to main runs without `--base`, so a register that landed on main is used as is. Every
  yarn-side check (ignore lists, registry, transport, plugins, the audit's own output) trusts the yarn binary:
  `.yarnrc.yml`'s `yarnPath` pointing at a modified yarn release (or a modified `.yarn/releases/*.cjs`) defeats all of
  them, and CHANGED TOGETHER catches a `.yarnrc.yml` / `.yarn/**` change only when the same PR also adds or changes a
  register entry; otherwise it is a review control. Generic `HTTP(S)_PROXY` variables are not checked (yarn 4 does
  not read them).
- **Tests:** `tools/check-npm-audit.test.cjs` (45). End to end in throwaway git repositories (`main(argv, deps)`): a
  head-only entry does not cover the finding on a non-decision PR, the same entry on the base does; a decision-only PR
  passes, one citing another PR fails, a renewal keeping the old reference fails, a missing event payload fails, a
  removal needs no reference; register + yarn.lock / package.json / the tool / ci-security.yaml fail CHANGED TOGETHER
  (also uncommitted); an unknown ref, a non-ref argument, a missing `--base` value and a depth-1 clone throw; a base
  without the register means no decisions; a German locale still reads a missing path as absent; the checkout decides
  without `--base`, and a pull_request run without it exits 1; F3 ignore list (not audited) and env var exit 1; F4
  `{error, status: null}`, a signal and exit 2 exit 1; F5 / F6 / F8 end to end; F7 dates; the workflows (`fetch-depth:
  0`, `--base` on PRs, the weekly schedule); an invalid (expired) base entry fails a non-decision PR that drops it. G1:
  adding or editing an entry next to `src/x.ts` exits 1, removing one next to it exits 0, an untouched entry is not
  flagged when the base moved on. G3: `--fail-on-expiring` exits 1 at 7 days left, 0 at 8, warning only without it; the
  weekly workflow passes it. G4: a non-default `npmAuditRegistry` / `npmRegistryServer` and both env variables are
  refused (end to end: exit 1, not audited). Follow-ups: a removal plus yarn.lock exits 0 and an addition plus
  yarn.lock exits 1; each transport setting, a non-built-in plugin, a failing `plugin runtime` and each env variable is
  refused (`NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=1` is not); unknown arguments exit 1 before auditing. Plugin sources: a
  `plugins` key in the project, an ancestor or the home `.yarnrc.yml` (also `plugins: []`), a file in `.yarn/plugins/`,
  `YARN_RC_FILENAME` and an unparseable `.yarnrc.yml` are refused; the repository itself passes; end to end, an
  impostor plugin named `@yarnpkg/plugin-npm-cli` listed in `.yarnrc.yml` exits 1 before auditing even though the
  runtime list looks clean. `NODE_OPTIONS`, `SSL_CERT_FILE`, `SSL_CERT_DIR` refused. Allowlist: the real
  `.yarnrc.yml` passes and each of its keys is allowlisted; `__proto__` hiding `plugins`, the legacy header (also with
  CRLF and a leading comment), an unknown key, a `<<` merge key, a quoted `"plugins"`, a duplicate key, `constructor` /
  `prototype` nested under `networkSettings`, a list top level and a non-scalar key are refused; end to end, the
  `__proto__` impostor, the legacy-header file and an unknown key each exit 1 before auditing; without the `yaml`
  library a problem is reported; a YAML warning (an unresolved `!foo` tag, also on an allowed key) fails; a planted
  plugin exits 1 with zero yarn invocations, a clean checkout calls `config get` first. Mutation check: 50 hand-made
  mutants of the tool (one per control), each killed by at least one test.

## CI release path — cd-deploy-tag on rab/vX.Y.Z tags, drafts only; publish-image starts from a person's publish (branch ci/release-tag-alignment, 2026-11-18, on top of ci/actions-pins-sha; no SQL, no runtime code)
- **Finding:** cd-deploy-tag listened for `v*.*.*` while every release since rab/v0.1.0-beta.1 used `rab/vX.Y.Z`, and
  publish-image's release guard (`release_guard.py` RELEASE_TAG, review F2) and the `release` environment's tag policy
  accept only `rab/v*`. The workflow had never run (zero runs). Had it run, the release it created with GITHUB_TOKEN
  would not have started publish-image: events caused by GITHUB_TOKEN start no workflow (only `workflow_dispatch` /
  `repository_dispatch` are exempt). Releases were in fact cut by the owner in GitHub, whose `release: published`
  event started publish-image directly (rab/v0.4.0); for rab/v0.6.0 the image was published by a dispatch from `main`
  first, and the release-event run was rejected at the `release` approval.
- **Control:** cd-deploy-tag triggers on `rab/v*.*.*`. `tools/create-github-release.sh` accepts exactly RELEASE_TAG
  (a test compares the two on accepted and refused samples, in JS and through the real Python module). It refuses a tag
  whose commit is not on `origin/main` (`git fetch --no-tags origin main` + `git merge-base --is-ancestor`, full-history
  checkout), the rule release_guard.py applies before publishing, so a tag on an unreviewed branch commit gets no
  release record at all (review of #250). It then looks the release up (`gh release view`, drafts
  included) and, if one exists, changes nothing. Otherwise it creates a **draft** (`--draft`, `--prerelease` for a
  `-suffix` tag, `--verify-tag`), never a published release, and its job summary tells the owner to publish the draft.
  Publishing is a person's event, so publish-image starts on the tag and the `release` environment approval (required
  reviewers) still gates the push. Fail closed: a failed fetch or merge-base, and any lookup error other than gh's exact
  `release not found`, fail the job and create nothing; a release created between lookup and create makes
  `gh release create` fail, never overwrite. The job has no `environment:` (it deploys nothing; `production` only
  recorded a misleading deployment). RELEASE_TAG itself now uses `[0-9]`, not `\d`: Python's `\d` matched Unicode
  digits (`rab/v\u0661.2.3`, U+0661 ARABIC-INDIC DIGIT ONE), which the guard accepted and the environment's tag
  policy would then have had to stop.
- **Not chosen:** a PAT or GitHub App token for cd-deploy-tag (a long-lived credential that could publish releases and
  so start the image push, held by a tag-triggered workflow) and `gh workflow run publish-image --ref <tag>` with
  `actions: write` (the guard allows dispatches only from `main`; widening it to tags is a change to review F2 and is
  not needed when a person publishes the release anyway). The job keeps `contents: write` only.
- **Tests:** `tools/create-github-release.test.cjs` (ci-security `action-pins`): a fake `git` (off-main -> refused
  before any gh call; failed fetch / merge-base -> fail closed); missing release -> exact git calls, then `view` and
  `create --draft` argv, notes and summary; prerelease tag; existing published / draft release -> no create;
  lookup error -> fail, no create; dry run calls nothing; refused inputs (bare `v1.2.3`, `+build`, ...) call nothing;
  RELEASE_TAG alignment including Unicode-digit samples (`test_release_guard.py` refuses them too); the installed gh's flags (`--draft`, `--prerelease`, `view --json isDraft`); the workflow's
  trigger, permissions and wiring; publish-image still starts on `release: published`.
- **Residual:** anyone with write access can push a `rab/v*` tag (no tag ruleset). On a commit of `main` that only
  drafts a release; a publish still needs a person to publish it and a `release` reviewer's approval.

## attendance_correction insert-only in the database, core copy (branch fix/attendance-correction-insert-only-core, 2026-11-21; DRAFT: new SQL, owner review first)
- **Finding closed (security finding format, §5.8; S11 / architecture §5.7).** Severity: Medium (integrity of pay evidence).
  Actor: any code path, CLI or injected statement running as the runtime login with a tenant bound (for example a Manager
  context). Action: `UPDATE` or `DELETE` (or `TRUNCATE`) on `attendance_correction`. Consequence before: allowed. The
  runtime login crewflow_owner inherits the table owner (owner-login BC-01 / BC-13), so the original `REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE`
  never bound it; the schema role crewflow_app still held both (copied-grant drift); the tenant policy is FOR ALL; TRUNCATE is
  never filtered by RLS. A correction row is the audit record of a pay change ("original values are never overwritten in
  place"), so rewriting or removing it hides who changed someone's hours. Root cause: insert-only was only a grant.
- **Change.** Migration AttendanceCorrectionInsertOnly1786722110000: three statement-level BEFORE UPDATE / DELETE / TRUNCATE
  triggers on `core.attendance_correction` calling the existing, unchanged `core.owner_login_grant_parity_guard()` (the PAY-1
  guard). The runtime login gets 42501 per statement, even when RLS leaves no row; INSERT and SELECT are unchanged. Definers,
  the workspace migrator and foreign-key actions (they run as the table owner) and superusers pass.
- **Retention unchanged (flagged for the owner).** Because FK actions pass, deleting the parent attendance (or the
  organisation) still CASCADEs its corrections exactly as before. No code path deletes attendance today, and a
  `payroll_record` already RESTRICTs deleting approved attendance. Making `attendance_correction.attendance_id` RESTRICT (as
  the owner chose for breaks and receipts) would also block that path; it is a retention decision, so it is proposed, not done.
- **Not in this PR.** `REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE ... FROM crewflow_app`: tools/check-rls-coverage.ts requires workspace grants to
  equal core's, so that cosmetic schema-role grant moves with the workspace-schema copies (0.7.0 workspace command, after
  #175 / #177 / #243). The workspace copies (HWS on) get the same three triggers then; until then they keep today's state.
- **Residual risk.** An injected statement can `SET ROLE crewflow` or disable the trigger (BC-01); the semantic posture
  monitor pins the three trigger lines (detection, not prevention).
- **Tests.** `attendance-correction-insert-only.integration.spec.ts`, as the runtime login (asserted crewflow_owner, a
  member of crewflow, not superuser / BYPASSRLS): a Manager who can read the correction gets 42501 for UPDATE and DELETE of
  it, for an UPDATE / DELETE matching no row, and for TRUNCATE (with and without tenant context); the stored row is
  unchanged; INSERT still works; `SET ROLE crewflow` (definer / FK-action path) can still delete (rolled back); zero rows
  with no tenant context; down() / up() round trip (rolled back) and a re-run of up() is a no-op.
  `attendance-correction-insert-only-sql.spec.ts`: statement shape, end-state check, goldens.
- **Security review fix (2026-11-21, Medium; owner decision 46).** The reviewer showed corrections still vanished through
  `attendance_correction.attendance_id ON DELETE CASCADE` when the runtime deleted the parent attendance (core.attendance has
  a FOR ALL policy and no delete guard; the FK action runs as the owner and passes the guard). New migration
  AttendanceCorrectionEvidenceRestrict1786722115000 makes that key ON DELETE RESTRICT (the pay-evidence principle the owner
  approved for breaks and receipts). Such a delete now fails (23503, or 23001 on PostgreSQL 18) and the correction stays;
  a hard user delete that would reach it already falls back to a soft delete on a foreign-key refusal. The organisation
  CASCADE (tenant offboarding, LC-2) is unchanged. Tests: the runtime's delete of an attendance with a correction is refused
  and both rows remain; a real FK cascade started by the runtime login passes the guard (probe table, rolled back) while
  its direct DELETE gets 42501. The workspace copies get the same key change with the level-26 command (#310).
## CF-23 — notes on the user profile page no longer persist to browser storage (branch fix/cf23-staff-notes-no-browser-storage, 2026-11-21; no SQL, no server change)
- **Finding (CF-23, LOW):** `packages/rab-front/src/features/users/UserProfile.tsx` (`/users/:id`) kept notes about a
  person in `localStorage` under `user-notes-<userId>`. Browser storage outlives logout and is shared by every account
  that signs in on the same browser profile, so a note written by one console user was shown to the next one on a shared
  device and stayed readable in devtools indefinitely. It was also fake persistence: nothing reached the server.
- **Control:** notes on that page live in React component memory only, keyed by the profile's user id (a note added on
  one person's page is never shown on another's), and are lost on navigation or reload. The page says so ("Notes on
  this page are not saved...") and the button reads "Add note", not "Save note". At app start-up (App.tsx, whatever page
  opens first) and again when the page mounts, every `user-notes-*` key an older build left in `localStorage` is removed
  (other keys untouched; `features/users/legacyNotes.ts`); storage errors (private mode,
  blocked storage) are swallowed because nothing was stored there. No new table, endpoint or SQL.
- **Assumption (data retention, flagged):** purging the legacy `user-notes-*` keys deletes notes a console user may
  believe they saved. They existed only on that one browser, never on the server, and keeping them is the leak this
  finding is about, so they are deleted rather than migrated. Veto if those notes must be kept.
- **Note:** the server has no `/users/:id` route today (staff and manager notes go through the RLS-scoped
  `/staff/:id/notes`, `/managers/:id/notes`, `/venue-managers/:id/notes` endpoints used by `UserDetailPanel`), so this
  page currently renders "User not found" and the notes tab is unreachable in a live console. The fix still applies so
  the page cannot leak if it is wired up again, and the purge cleans devices used with older builds.
- **Tests:** `packages/rab-front/src/features/users/UserProfile.spec.tsx`: adding a note shows it while
  `Storage.prototype.setItem` and `sessionStorage.setItem` are never called and both storages stay empty; notes seeded
  under `user-notes-*` by an older build are not shown and are removed on mount, an unrelated key survives; a note added
  on user A's page is not shown after navigating to user B's page. `App.spec.tsx`: rendering `<App>` (the login page) with
  a seeded `user-notes-x` key removes it and keeps an unrelated key (fails without the start-up purge).
- **Residual:** notes on this page are not saved at all until a server-side, RLS-scoped notes store backs it (a new
  table = owner SQL review).

## engine/ stops importing modules/ — identity entities, venue resource scope, entity cache (branches refactor/engine-owns-identity-entities, refactor/engine-modules-scope-and-cache, refactor/engine-modules-venue-summary, 2026-11-21; no migration)
- **Finding:** CLAUDE.md's "engine/ never imports from modules/" had 24 production violations (ratchet baseline
  `engine-to-modules`), 20 of them auth, permissions, audit, email, platform-admin and user-deletion services importing
  identity entities from `modules/identity`. A dependency in that direction lets a domain-module change silently alter
  platform security code (and a domain module could add an entity relation the auth path then loads).
- **Control:** the 18 identity/access entities move to `engine/core-modules/identity/entities` (pure file move, re-exported
  from `modules/identity/entities`); `ManagerVenue` moves to `engine/core-modules/resource-scope/entities`; the by-owner
  workspace and venue display-cache reads move to `modules/manager-workspace` and `modules/venue` (same cache kinds, keys and
  projections, through `CoreEntityCacheService.getOrFetch`). The baseline loses the rule entirely, so any new engine ->
  modules import fails ci-security (`tools/check-import-boundaries.cjs`; owner-dated approvals are the only exception).
- **Changed read (authorisation input):** `ResourceScopeService.resolveTx`'s venue-manager scope no longer joins the
  `ManagerProfile` entity; it filters `mv.manager_profile_id IN (SELECT mp.id FROM core.manager_profile mp WHERE mp.user_id
  = $1)`. Same rows (mp.id is the primary key, so each manager_venue row joined at most one profile), same RLS on both
  tables, `manager_venue` still schema-qualified by the bound manager, user id still a bound parameter. A venue manager with
  no assignment still gets `{ kind: 'venue', venueIds: [] }` (sees nothing), never an owner scope.
- **Tests:** `resource-scope.service.spec.ts` (exact SQL under core routing and a bound workspace schema, parameter binding,
  empty-assignment fail-closed, non-venue-manager never queries manager_venue); `manager-workspace-display-cache.spec.ts`
  and `venue-summary-cache.spec.ts` (same cache kind/key, no extra enabled/TTL argument, same projection, null never
  cached, hit skips the database); `core-entity-cache.integration.spec.ts` follows the moved reads; the live venue scope
  stays covered by `venue-manager-scoping.integration.spec.ts` (assign -> visible, unassign -> gone, another manager's venue
  invisible).
- **Residual:** engine still names domain tables in raw SQL in several places (e.g. `core.manager_profile`,
  `core.manager_workspace`); the ratchet sees imports, not table names.

## Payroll approval: maker-checker and a fresh step-up, no override (decision 5, branch feat/payroll-approval-maker-checker, 2026-11-21; no SQL)

- **Who can call this:** a workspace manager holding `payroll.approve` (approve / bulk-approve a payroll record; finalise a
  run). Venue Managers are refused categorically (unchanged).
- **Threat:** one person prepares pay and approves it (fraud or an unchecked mistake), or a hijacked-but-live session
  (stolen cookie / token, unattended machine) approves pay.
- **Controls (layer 2, in the services, so jobs and direct calls are covered too):**
  - `PayrollService.approve` / `bulkApprove`: refused when the caller finalised the shift report that created the record
    (`shift_report.finalised_by`, read under the same row lock; the report finalisation is what prepares a record). 403
    single; per-id `prepared_by_you` in bulk. An unreadable preparer is refused (409 / `not_ready`), never treated as
    "someone else". The own-hours refusal is unchanged.
  - `PayrollRunService.finalise`: refused (403) when the caller created the run (`prepared_by`) or added lines to it through
    `prepare` (the insert-only `payroll_run.prepared` audit row each prepare writes in the same transaction as its lines,
    `linesAdded > 0`). A run the check cannot read counts as prepared by the caller (fail closed).
  - All three need a fresh step-up of THIS session (`StepUpReauthService.assertRecentStepUp`, actions
    `payroll.record.approve` / `payroll.run.finalise`): password within AUTH_STEP_UP_WINDOW_SECONDS (default 5 min) plus the
    authenticator code when the approver has 2FA. Checked before the transaction opens (the step-up uses its own short
    transactions; holding two pool connections is the deadlock class fixed in #323) and before the record is looked up,
    so an unknown id discloses nothing. Refusals are audited (`auth.step_up_failed` with the action). Admin Inspect is refused.
  - No override exists; an organisation with one payroll person cannot approve until it adds a second (decision 5's stated
    consequence).
- **Not changed:** reject, statement retry, prepare, upload, net and mark-paid need no step-up (decision 5 names approval).
- **Database layer:** none added. The maker-checker facts live in other tables (shift_report, audit_log), and decision 5
  says "no SQL unless b is chosen". RLS still refuses own-hours approval (`payroll_record_update` WITH CHECK).
- **Tests:** payroll-approval (decision-5 case: preparer refused single + bulk with a fresh step-up, stale session refused
  and audited, another organisation 404 after step-up, second manager approves), payroll-runs (preparer refused, stale
  session refused, second manager finalises), lane-d step-up adoption (three new routes), and every suite that approves
  pay now uses a second manager of the workspace (server: realtime-c1b, w5-timeline; worker: shift-statement,
  shift-statement-wake, phase-d cutover, phase-d two-worker).

**Update after the independent review of #335 (HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW fixed; the trade-off above is withdrawn):**
- **Fresh 2FA, bound to the action, single use:** approve / bulk-approve / finalise now call
  `StepUpReauthService.assertFreshSecondFactorForAction(ctx, action)`. An approver with no authenticator factor is refused
  (403 `STEP_UP_MFA_ENROLMENT_REQUIRED`, audited). The session must hold a grant written by `POST /auth/step-up` with
  `action` set and a verified TOTP code (key `step-up:<session hash>:action:<action>`); a sign-in grant, the ordinary
  session grant, or a grant for another action never counts; the grant is read with GETDEL, so one proof serves exactly one
  approval call. The web dialog receives `action` in the 403 and sends it back with the proof. Lane P2's approval actions
  use the same helper (add them to ACTION_BOUND_STEP_UP_ACTIONS).
- **Preparers:** whoever reviewed the attendance seat (`shift_assignment.attendance_reviewed_by`) is a preparer too.
- **Database layer (DRAFT, new SQL, PayrollMakerCheckerBackstop1786723020000):** `core.payroll_record_guard()` (the one trigger
  function of core AND every workspace payroll_record). On the move to `approved`: `approved_by` must be the signed-in caller
  (no worker exemption: the worker never writes it and the marker is a plain GUC); the record's finalised report and seat
  must be readable with a non-null finaliser and reviewer (fail closed); the approver is neither of them; and because those
  live columns are writable by managers, the insert-only `core.audit_log` must hold the finalisation BY the live finaliser
  and the review BY the live reviewer, and none of those history rows may name the approver (re-pointing `finalised_by` or
  the reviewer afterwards, even with a forged history row naming a colleague, does not help). The lookups are uuid = uuid
  on (organisation_id, entity_type, entity_id), the leading columns of audit_log_timeline_idx (EXPLAIN test).
- **Rollout note (owner):** records with no finalisation / review history, or a null reviewer, can no longer be approved.
  Read-only pre-deploy count (run as the database owner; `core` while HWS is off), `PAYROLL_GUARD_PREDEPLOY_COUNT_SQL` in
  payroll-maker-checker-sql.ts:
  `SELECT count(*) FROM core.payroll_record pr LEFT JOIN core.shift_report sr ON sr.shift_id = pr.shift_id AND sr.status = 'finalised'
  LEFT JOIN core.attendance a ON a.id = pr.attendance_id LEFT JOIN core.shift_assignment sa ON sa.id = a.shift_assignment_id
  WHERE pr.status = 'pending_approval' AND (sr.id IS NULL OR sr.finalised_by IS NULL OR sa.id IS NULL OR sa.attendance_reviewed_by IS NULL
  OR NOT EXISTS (finalisation row by sr.finalised_by) OR NOT EXISTS (review row by sa.attendance_reviewed_by))` (full text in the module).
  Outside that move `approved_by` never changes (so a two-step "set approved_by, then flip status" is refused at step one).
  The service mirrors the same rule (live columns + history, null reviewer refused). The payroll_run finaliser rule (core
  and workspace copies, plus a real per-line `prepared_by`) moves to a follow-up blocked on the 0.7.0 chain; until then the
  run rule is service-only (creator via `prepared_by`, top-ups via the audit row).
- **Tests:** payroll-approval (11) / (11b): no proof, a sign-in or ordinary grant, a sign-in grant planted under the action
  key, a proof for another action, an un-enrolled approver: all 403; the real step-up with code then exactly one approval,
  a second approval on the same proof 403; a reviewer who did not finalise: service 403 and DB 42501.
  payroll-maker-checker-rls (core, runtime login): finaliser / reviewer approving 42501, run preparer finalising 42501, a
  third manager allowed.
## Payroll adjustments: corrections, bonuses and expenses as separate approved lines (Lane P2, M5, owner decision 3, branch feat/payroll-adjustments, 2026-11-21; NEW SQL: PayrollAdjustmentSchema1786723100000, DRAFT for owner review)
- **Asset / actors:** money added to a person's pay after their hours were approved. Attackers considered: a payroll
  manager paying themselves or a friend (insider), a manager approving their own entry, a Venue Manager or a staff member
  writing pay lines, another organisation reading or approving by id, a stolen but live manager session, a bug or direct
  SQL changing an approved or already-paid line, and a deduction taken from a worker without consent (Employment Rights
  Act 1996 s.13).
- **Controls (five layers):** (1) PermissionGuard: list `payroll.view`, add `payroll.calculate`, approve / reject
  `payroll.approve`; console only (`@ManagerApplication`). (2) PayrollAdjustmentService re-checks the flag and refuses
  Venue Managers before any read; nobody adds, approves or rejects a line that pays THEMSELVES (403
  `PAYROLL_ADJUSTMENT_OWN_PAY`); the creator never approves or rejects their own line (403
  `PAYROLL_ADJUSTMENT_SAME_PERSON`); approve needs a recent step-up of the session, checked before any read (403
  `STEP_UP_REQUIRED`, `payroll.adjustment.approve` in STEP_UP_ACTIONS); a correction must point at an approved record of
  the caller's workspace and takes the staff member from that record, never the body; a reduction can never exceed what
  the original shift paid. (3) Every query pinned to the session's organisation AND workspace (404 for anything else).
  (4) RLS tenant predicate, ENABLE + FORCE in the same migration. (5) RLS non-venue, non-archived workspace manager
  predicate on every write and manager read; staff read only their OWN APPROVED lines. In the database itself: CHECKs
  for exactly three kinds (no deduction kind exists), only a correction may be negative, a correction names its record,
  creator != paid person, decider != creator and != paid person; `core.payroll_adjustment_guard()` refuses any change
